ipc-title__text: Faithful to LOTR not Peter Jackson
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I absolutely love LOTR. The books, the Peter Jackson movies and especially the theme music. I was very critical of this show at first. I have then since realized that my dislike for the show was because it had a different feel than Peter Jackson.It is faithful to the books and history. The CGI is incredible. Character depictions are slightly off to me in addition to temperament. However, I think it has the potential to be great if you are open minded. Peter Jackson is not LOTR. Many complaints and dislikes are due to the feel of the show. Characters are portrayed differently, the original actors we grew to love are not present. Give it time.

I've waited until the end of Ep 4 before commenting. I accept that this show wasn't created for me, a Tolkien fan before Ralph Bakshi, who loved Sir Michael Hordern's Gandalf etc
However, despite wonderful cinematography, this show fails on too many levels.Not least is it's heartless. Impossible to root for anyone. No respect is given by any of the main characters. Tolkien's vision of Numenor and its failings has been subverted to other matters all of the present day and therefore there's no fantasy escape. Another example of Americans not 'getting' IP of a British origin. Cf The Avengers etc. As for following the lore, yeah, right! Too many deviations to list. Avoid. Life's too short.

ipc-title__text: It is not what I expected.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I had high hopes when I first heard about this show, but I find it to be bland and hollow, lacking sophistication. The script is simple and the dialog often cringy.What is really ruining it for me above all else is the portrail of elves. I see nothing of Tolkiens elves in them, just regular humans with some martial arts skills and pointy ears. Elves are so close to my heart, I can not understand why they are not given the beauty and wisdom Tolkien described.I will admit I might have given a couple more stars if this was not supposed to be an adaptation of Tolkien, but to be honest I would probably not cared enough to write a review at all then. I can not give this show more than one star. The only thing I really like about it is when you see glimpses of the beautiful nature of New Zealand.

ipc-title__text: Cheap jab at milking the success of others.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I'm not even going to write the book the mistakes in story and lore this deserves; it would take way too long.But for a series of this caliber; they have failed in numerous ways.For starters, what are physics? I understand that props are made of foam, but we're supposed to be immersed. They're supposed to act! Then why do they fling things that supposedly weight hundreds of kilograms around like paper?I understand that the concept of having ice climbing boots just popped into some amateur's head and seemed cool... but all you have to do is google a bit and understand how bad that idea is. But I guess you can just call them magic. Well, maybe do that instead of trying to recreate physics.Furthermore; there is so much bad, silly and eye hurting choreography. Is this supposed to be a musical? I haven't seen tagged as one. Unrealistic and breaking immersion.I honestly feel like this is more of a children cartoon than a serious series.For me it couldn't even be used as background noise while doing something else. It was such a disappointment that those comical theories about an upcoming age of bad cinematography don't seem so far fetched anymore.

ipc-title__text: A poor adaptation of a masterpiece
ipc-html-content-inner-div:
This is a very expensive TV series for what is an exceptionally dull program.The script is quite terrible, full of filler sudo-wise quotes, devoid of natural language.The plot is attempting to condense 3000+ years of history into perhaps 20 years and is failing to find a compelling story.Galadriel here I don't believe is a very likeable character, the people around her seem to be dummed down to make her look better. They simply don't show the viewer that she is the most powerful being (apart from maybe souron) in all of middle Earth. It is her that helped resurrected Gandalf in the 3rd age, and destroyed fortress walls and armies with her magic - here she is depicted as but a shadow of a simulacrum of her true power - resorting to essentially rolling around in the dirt to kill such petty things like trolls.I really enjoyed the humanity of Owain Arthurs portrail of Prince Durin IV, along with the animation of Lenny Henry's performance of a proto-hobbit. These and getting to see the beginnings of a dwarven city are perhaps the only good things with this season.Plot: terrible 1/10
Scrip: 2/10 (anakin talking about sand being course was better than the wooden scrip we get here).Costumes: 1-7.5/10 (dwarves, men, and the orc have so far had the best costumes - the elves and Proto-hobbits leave much to be desired).Allegory: 1/10 (Tolkien was most explicit in his distain of allegory in his middle Earth. And the writers have obviously projected their own contemporary allegorical messages into Tolkien's work. The only intended allegory in his work was that power corrupts and that of Catholicism (the magisterial etherealness of Galadriel being reflective of Mary).For this and much more I give it a 2/10.

I enjoyed the first two episodes and looking forward to the rest of the series. It seems to be building to something very nicely. It is set so far before the films that it feels like its own thing but also feels like it will move in much the same direction as the original trilogy.The dwarfs bring a bit of much needed levity but the tone works quite well overall.Only downsides are the Hobbity people are very dull and I could not care what happens to them and I hope they don't feature prominently. It is also bit too Downton elvey at times with all these posh dislikeable people talking too much about nothing of consequence.

Honestly I wasn't sure if I'd like this series, however I absolutely loved the first two episodes, and I'm looking forward to seeing the rest.The casting is brilliant, I wasn't sold on the choice for Galadriel at first but by the second episode I had changed my mind, she's amazing! I love Elrond, I did not like the casting for him in the movies, absolutely loving him in this.I haven't read The Silmarillion so I am not sure how true to the history of Middle Earth it is keeping, but so far I'm enjoying this adaptation.Definitely worth the watch with an open mind; I love the books and the original movies, I'm enjoying this as well.

ipc-title__text: Simply bad even if you are not a fan of original series!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The fact that first season alone has times higher budget than all of the three original movies combined is mind blowing! Even if you are not a fan of original series, you will not going to find this show any good. Bad costumes, even some cosplayers could do it better! Elfs having plastic looking ears and you can clearly see some characters wearing cheap wigs. Some dialogues and face expressions are straight up cringe. Orcs for some reasons are oppressed, trying to fight for freedom, have families with babies while in the meantime destroying nature and killing, eating and torturing every race they encounter. Unlike previously Galadriel is not a wise guiding character who has seen the world since its creation but rather someone who is emotionally unstable, likes arguing with everyone and can be easily fooled. It just butchers all the work that was done in order to carefully create magic universes. Just a friendly reminder that The Return of the King alone has 11 Oscars. Why would you claim to be part of this legacy? I have never written a review in my life but this is just unacceptable and disrespectful to Tolkien! Bad acting and production, plot wholes and constant rewriting of the story to fit in with today's agenda! Incredibly bad!

This is a terrible representation of Tolkien's world. At best, it is fan fiction of the worst sort with typical modern writing tropes. It constantly relies on the Jackson movie trilogy to bait up nostalgia. There is no heart or soul here, a cheap imitation that does not understand the source material or why it is so beloved. There is so much potential in creating a story set within the second age and so many directions the showrunners could have taken it. But they chose to nostalgia bait and create a world that is small. The most disappointing thing to me is that this is going to be a generations first introduction to Tolkien, and it will be a poor imitation of such a rich fantastical world brought down by terrible writing.

ipc-title__text: Distortion of Tolkien's novels; needs better lead cast, script, & less meandering plots
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Huge disappointment. If u read Tolkien's detailed unforgettable LOTR trilogy, this show fails to follow it. In any significant way.If one has read the Hobbit or 300+ pages dry history of "middle earth" completed by Tolkien's son, this series fails to follow them too.One Major problem is uncharismatic actress playing Lead elf warrior bursting with non credible "revenge & hate." In 2 seasons she displays same grim expression of anger. She gets a lot of screen time & dull dialogue too.Tolkien's Elves are elite beings, ultimate nature conservationists/ environmentalists, not materialistic, nor desiring power over others; cherishing wildlife & its beauty; gifted with advance medicine, science, meditation, weapons, craftsmanship & magic. All various elven cultures reside WITH nature & in different habitats throughout Middle Earth; eating sparsely except for holidays; great elf leaders are of both genders possessing gift of foresight & wisdom, aided by experienced council. Here, these basic facts of elves are discarded..This series intro states "time is 1000 years before LOTR events." Yet S2 previews show Gandalf & Elrond; dwarf king & Orcs; no Hobbit exists yet, but there's a new species of "star beings" with wizard powers, & nomadic fearful Hartford/ "halfings." Here the Halfings are supposedly ancestral hobbits. Again Tolkien's creations are disregarded bc Hobbits despise traveling outside beloved wooded Shire, love creating & eating gourmet food & drinks with friends.This series has mostly poor casting & overall character development. Add several unrelated soap opera plots that unfold very slowly as if the show was to last 18 seasons, repetitive dull tedious dialogue, and result is befuddled boring formulatic mess. Little action, no tension, no suspension. Predictable female lead elf does whatever she wants, is really a copy of Captain Marvel, & is always best warrior without receiving injury.Sad unimaginative writers couldn't simply take what Tolkien created & transfer it to screen. Viewer has to wonder exactly how the big 1 Bil $ budget to produce this show was spent bc it's not the actors, location, script, direction, score, cgi nor decor. 2 stars for the few lovely horses shown, & curing insomnia.

ipc-title__text: A boring, incoherent, and troublesome depiction of Middle Earth.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I came into Rings Of Power with no expectations. In fact I specifically didn't watch trailers to avoid any spoilers or reveals, etc... just so that I have no bias or doubts when I sit down on my couch ready to embrace what should be a new and exciting TV show.But Lord Of The Rings is already a incredibly masterful journey into Middle Earth that is impossible to forget. Followed up by The Hobbit years later which wasn't as good, but thoroughly entertaining. The weight of the world rests on these characters.In Rings Of Power there is no weight. There is no sense of impending doom. They tell us it's there, but its acted so poorly and the plot unfolds so slowly and lackluster that you simply feel no emotion towards it. I feel bad for the stars of the show as the writing is often horrendous.The entire production looks incredible, and you can tell they spent a lot of money on it, but the writing, story, and acting feels like a very bad fan made short.Unfortunately this show is anything but short. Each episode is long, and boring. It's packed full of characters you really cannot care about. The plot bounces around so inconsistently it's tough to watch.The visuals can be incredible to look at as new areas are revealed and the camera pans up or out to reveal this gloriously beautiful landscape, or mountain range, etc... But you soon realize it's all fluff.The writing is perhaps the worst I've ever seen on any show ever made. Which in return makes the actors suffer. They have to deliver such jibberish and poorly scribed lines, that its no wonder you don't get a standout performance. I see so much potential in Morfydd Clark, but none of it is properly tapped into. Imagine what she could do on House Of The Dragon?The story is just incredibly bad. Little of it makes sense, and these character choices are quite ridiculous. Casting aside, these people look too fantastical and the world doesn't feel lived in.When you have so much inconsistency in the writing, story, acting, and plot, you end up on the chopping block. That's where this show is, on the chopping block. Amazon should stop this abomination, and start over from scratch. It's time to hire people who know how to make an actual episode of TV. Episodes need to be more tightly focused, and move at a better pace. This is saddest, sloppiest, and silliest stroll through Middle Earth that no one deserves to sit through. 2 out of 10.

ipc-title__text: Initially interesting but fell apart at the end
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I was initially drawn into the story. Although it dragged at points, there was enough interesting parts to keep me engaged. But the end of season 1 made no sense. People made decisions contrary to their character development. The reasons for making the rings made no sense. And Galadria was so out of character in the last episode. Up until then, she had been a strong character but completely stalled out in a way which snapped me out of the story. Actually, now that I think about it, her character was inconsistent. I enjoyed the actress' portrayal but her motivations were unclear and her actions inconsistent.

The story is absolutely captivating and very detailed. The dialogue is full of nuggets of wisdom and beautiful interactions that stay with you and make you think. I don't think it was neither fast nor slow, just the right pace, however, the dialogue does take precedence over the action which might make it seem slower paced.The production quality is off the chart and clearly extremely well made. Galadriel is such a wonderful character, fierce and sweet at the same time, such that you fall in loved with her straight away. You can feel the anguish and pain in her story as well as the power and strength she has. I think the actress played it perfectly. Elrond and the dwarfs also do an excellent job but the harfoots steal the show in my opinion.Overall, this is by far the best show I could have hoped for and one that I'll rewatch on a yearly at least (have already watched it twice)

Not sure why the low rating. I love the LOTR and Hobbits. But this is a TV series. Having said that, this is still quite very good and entertaining and I really enjoyed it. Its an expounded version of the rings story so expect more characters, more stories. The setting, costumes/makeup were excellent its like watching a movie every episode, they really invested so much on it.What I kept doing throughout watching was I keep connecting the series to the trilogies. The main characters: Galadriel, Elrond, Sauron...the whys and so far the series have answered them somehow but still leaves you wondering for more, probably left for later...Like any other first seasons, it will ask you to wait for more. Anyway, I cannot wait to watch the second season of this--I hope not too long like other series that takes a year to wait, arghhh!

This is a beautifully lavish production, which is mostly why I gave it a 6. It's that gorgeous. And the characters and their motivations are somewhat interestingOn the other hand, it is soooooooo boring. I find that to be the case with my reaction to most of Tolkien's work and adaptions. However, this one especially so. When I saw that episode 6 or 7 clocked in at another 72 episodes, I said to myself, I can't make myself sit through this again. Because 72 minutes really means 90 minutes, because I kept letting my attention wander and would go back 2 minutes to see what the hell they were talking about or reacting to... sometimes multiple times for the same plot point. It is THAT un-engaging. I don't mind a show being this uninteresting if the visuals are this good, but the length of every episode is unnecessarily long.....

Well that was an abject total failure.Who knew Tolkien's legacy could be utterly destroyed by inexperienced producers and show runners who never read the source material? YouTube fan fiction is better than this disaster. Plot-holes, long and drawn out stares, recycled Peter Jackson lines, and elementary acting are just the beginning of countless criticisms.I've wasted my time and I cannot ever get that time back. Heed my warning to future viewers. Do not invest any time and do something else more productive. Go outside and touch the grass, breathe in fresh air, and bask in sunshine.You will thank me.

The writers have no idea how to visually tell the amazing story that is already written by Tolkien. The protagonist Galadriel is so unlikable and is behaving like a sociopath because according to the writers that's what a hero does. None of the characters makes you feel the warmth of the original trilogy by Peter Jackson. The pacing is way off and the way the episodes are edited is very boring. This doesn't make us feel compelled to wait and watch the next episode .The visuals and some of the background scores are the only good thing about this series. Not at all worth watching. House of dragon>

For me, the series main issue is the miscast of major characters like Elrond and Galadriel. I am sure both actors are great but Robert Aramayo doesn't have the imposing presence of Hugo Weavin and Morfydd Clark fails to deliver a convincing Galadriel. If the movies didn't exist, this wouldn't be an issue, but since they do, both actors lack in comparison to their predecessors.Another issue for me, is that the Hobbit scenes break the immersion and pace so far. They are extremely childish and predictable.The show isn't bad and it has all the elements to become better, but they have to bring up the pace.

ipc-title__text: The Most Stunning TV Series I've ever seen!!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Don't let the negative review fool you. I've watched 6 episodes of this show non stop and I can't express in words how much I've enjoyed it. Everything about the show whether it's visual effects, action, dialogue, all are superb so far. I've watched the all LOTR and Hobbit movies and I must say that this movie is taking the imagination to the next level by stunning visual effects and new faces of the characters. I can't understand why people are not appreciating the series and actors? Every character is justifying his/her role perfectly. I am really enjoying this show. If you haven't watched the show, go and watch it. Believe me guys! This is by far the best fantasy show I've ever seen.

The Rings of Power is beautiful to look at... but, good golly, every scene is a petty argument between two characters. It's as melodramatic as a daytime soap opera.Drama drama drama.Long gone are complex individuals with their own identities. Instead, each character acts roughly the same as every other character... just with different accents.Also missing, is a sense of good folk struggling in a fight against a greater evil. The writers seem to think silly arguments among all the characters is griping conflict. It's not. A family constantly arguing about almost everything may work on Days Of Our Lives, but not Middle Earth.And forget about the mysterious nature and beliefs of dwarfs or elves or orcs. They are reduced to emotional wrecks (once again, just like every other race in this series).In short the majesty, the depth, the mystery, the grandeur, the peculiarities, the magic, and epic nature of Tolkien's Middle Earth are all missing... and are replaced with trivial squabbles between drama queens in costumes. Disappointing.

ipc-title__text: Incredibly Bad - I wanted to like this
ipc-html-content-inner-div: My issues:1) Galaderiel - thoroughly unlikeable - in the books she's a powerful sorcerer who is wise and has a presence . She's not a warrior. She doesn't twitch like a lunatic. This portrayal is awful.2) The Harfoots - a waste of time and space, who don't exist in the second age. Featuring female Sam and Frodo. Some of the relationships make to sense. Their behaviour is psychotic. They leave people behind to die who cannot keep up.3) Dialogue - this is just cringe. Whoever wrote this needs to be sacked.4) The Story - as mentioned above this is not the second age.5) The world building of Tolkien ignored - it's a shame that races like Harad ignored. That would have been great representation rather than cheap inserts.6) All the men are dumb - overcompensation for gender roles by Hollywood leads to bad characterisation. It makes the female characters look horrible , almost chauvinistic and the male characters pathetic. Series like Cobra Kai have shown us how female characters can be awesome if treated with good storylines.7) Special Effects - the green screen in some scenes look absolutely awful. Looks like old 70's style back projection.

ipc-title__text: If you are capable of letting go ANY TOLKIEN Lore you may find this watchable

ipc-html-content-inner-div:
The effects, cgi and visuals are very goodbut there are a lot of problems with RoP: the two most important are that
the next issue is the quality of sound in specific cases and the expression from actors. There is no voice acting, everything is flat and in intense scenes, in scenes when a message is to be passed or whenever emphasis is necessary, audio/sound is completely underwhelming or missing...

I was excited about this show, but after watching the first couple episodes, I couldn't get over a few issues.The script seemed nonsensical. The things people said didn't really make sense or were purely audience-facing dialogue. It sounded like they wanted to write something that sounded old and profound but they just didn't know how.Small details seemed off like the number of people in Galadriel's expedition was too small. Galadriel's team of elite warriors seemed terribly ill-equipped to deal with a troll - how did they expect to defeat Sauron? The celebration that Sauron was gone had an audience of like 20 or 30 people in the Elven capital, and the celebration itself contained nothing of substance. Celebrimbor and Elrond leaving for Kazad-dum and then arriving the next scene, walking out from behind a mountain with no sense of how long it took or how they got there, and then Celebrimbor just walking back nonchalantly? The entrance to the undying lands seeming like a raging fire instead of a beautiful utopia. A random ship being close enough to the undying lands to pick up Galadriel. Galadriel thinking she could swim all the way back to middle-earth.Being unable to easily distinguish between men and elves seems off.The lack of older wiser characters who have advice worth hearing. Everyone in this show is super young. Contrast Galadriel and Elrond's emotional conversation to Gandalf and Elrond having a big-boy discussion about what to do with the ring. Older, wise characters add a sense of gravity to the show and a point of reference about what's truly important and what's not.On the flip-side, I did like the Harfoots for the most part. They blended older, mature characters with young fun characters.I might watch another episode to see if it improves.

ipc-title__text: Worth Watching, Especially if You Like Fantasy.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I'm not a Tolkienite so never read the books but have seen all the movies. This has a somewhat different feel than the first and second trilogies but still feels like another world. The elves seem more man-like and less regal than in the trilogies but not terribly off the mark. The hobbit like people are a little hokey and kid friendly for my taste but it is what it is and not stopping me from watching the series. Keep an eye out for the multitude of easter eggs, the development of already well known characters and remember that this is an adaptation - it will never be to everyones taste. ipc-title__text: Only on Season 1 still, but I'm enjoying it.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: After hearing and reading so many mixed reviews, I have finally convinced myself to start watching this series. I'm not one to write reviews on here, but I would love to give this show some credit. I have read the Lord of the Rings, The Hobbit, and I have read The Silmarillion (after many attempts). It was difficult coming into this show with an open mind. I grew up watching Peter Jackson's movies - I still go back and watch the extended versions every year. A LOTR marathon is absolutely necessary. And those movies are definitely a hard act to follow. But this series is not a remake of the original trilogy. It's set long before the events of the trilogy.Because of all the other reviews, I decided it was best to clear my mind of any high expectations. I'm glad I did.I think the show is visually stunning. The music is gorgeous, and there are performances in here that I find compelling and highly entertaining. The only reason I took away two stars from what I think would give this a perfect 10 out of 10, is the pacing. There are times where I feel like this show has dragged on and I'm just waiting for it to get to the action. Some of the scenes just feel like filler and don't really seem necessary. As a huge Apocalypse Now fan (my favourite film actually), I chuckled when Adar was introduced himself. The "River" dialogue is NEARLY identical when Captain Willard meets Colonel Kurtz in Apocalypse Now.As of right now, my favourite characters are Nori Brandyfoot (Markella Kavenagh), I think the actress does an incredible job. The relationship between her community, her family, and The Stranger are so heartfelt and engaging, I'd say that these are probably my favourite scenes from the series so far. My other favourite character in this show is Durin (Owain Arthur). I always loved the dwarves. Gimli was my favourite character in the Lord of the rings movies, I love the hobbit movies a lot. Despite how many people chewed them out for being too cartoony and childish, Arthur did such an incredible job, keeping the proud and stubborn personalities that usually come with the dwarf characters.The elves. Absolutely, you have characters that were portrayed by great, if not, legendary actors who did these characters such justice in the movies. When I hear Galadriel, Cate Blanchett will always come to mind. When I hear Elrond, Hugo Weaving. That being said, I am thoroughly enjoying the performances by these new actors. Very interesting takes on these characters. Elrond's relationship with Durin. Galadriel's relationships with Elrond, Elendil, Gil-galad, and Halbrand (yes, I know who he is).I haven't started season two yet. Again, trying to keep an open mind when I go in and watch it. But it's so far I am enjoying the show. Slow, definitely a slow start, but I can't keep my eyes off of the screen. I think the show runners did an incredible job breathing life into the world, the characters, and the lore. There are Tolkien fanatics who love the show, but also Tolkien fanatics who actually go out of their way to rip the show a new one. The same way Peter Jackson fans go about expressing their opinions.At the end of the day, you're either going to enjoy a movie or a show, or you're not. Or maybe in between. There are going to be parts that you are mesmerized by, and moments that make you cringe. It's your opinion, and your opinion is not wrong. If you did not enjoy the show, cool. If you did enjoy the show, also cool. I am enjoying the show. I am glad I took the time to watch it, And I look forward to seeing how the second season plays out.

ipc-html-content-inner-div: With all the one star reviews, I wasn't sure what to expect. After giving the show a shot, I really got sucked into the plot threrads and was rooting for the characters. I highly recommend this show.With intricate world-building, complex characters, and jaw-dropping visuals, a well-crafted fantasy series can transport you to another world. With a talented cast and crew behind it, this show is sure to be a must-watch for fans of the genre.Whether you're a die-hard fan of the genre or just looking for something new and exciting to watch, Rings of Power is a good fantasy show that has something for everyone.

First of all, I read all of Tolkien's books, as well as I got to draw and hand-paint a 1m x 1m map of Middle-earth, so this is not a layperson's opinion on the work, but a reader's and admirer.It is important for people to know that Tolkien published basically "The Hobbit", "TLOTR" trilogy and "The Adventures of Tom Bombadil" during his lifetime, the rest of the material from his universe was either small or published posthumously through a reunion of incomplete texts by his son. It is also important to know that the rights acquired to the series gave access to a very limited material of information about the 2nd Era, basically excerpts and footnotes from official books published in life. Therefore, within these limits, it's a very beautiful and honest show, wrunging blood from a stone to create a plot with unity, character development and good thread.Don't be swayed by purists, who were bothered by the inclusive cast of actors or by the insertion of non-canonical characters and locations (non-existent in the books), watch the show with eyes free out of spite, Tolkien made it clear in life that he would like other minds to continue his universe, and that's what we see here, he would certainly approve. Unfortunately, we are living in an era of hate and cancellation, and here is no different.In closing, what amazes me the most is the complaint of being boring and slow, not an action show. Well, anyone who has read Tolkien's work and is a admirer knows very well that his books are long, descriptive, with stories told with a lot of patience until reach the moments of action, including several poems throughout the narratives. So whoever complains about this in the series is because didn't like the books or even haven't read them.Great production and performances, good script, beautiful soundtrack and an opportunity to once again see Tolkien's wonderful universe on screen.8 out of 10.

ipc-title__text: One Star: Avoid at All Costs!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Rings of Power is an absolute disaster! The show's production team seemed to have poured all their effort into replicating the design of Peter Jackson's films, but forgot the most important aspect of storytelling: creating interesting and engaging characters with a well-structured plot.The writers, if they can even be called that, appear to be completely ignorant of the basic rules of storytelling. The show is nothing but a disconnected jumble of scenes that fail to form a coherent story. There is no beginning, middle, or end to be found here, no character development, and no resolution. It's just a bunch of isolated bits and pieces that make no sense.For a series that claims to be based on J. R. R. Tolkien's legendary works, it's astonishing how little Rings of Power resembles anything he wrote. Professor Tolkien was able to create a timeless masterpiece armed with nothing more than a pen and paper, yet the "writers" of this show have managed to squander obscene amounts of money without creating anything remotely worthwhile.If you're a fan of Tolkien's work or just enjoy good storytelling, avoid Rings of Power at all costs. It's a boring, annoying, and utterly nonsensical mess that doesn't deserve your time or attention.

ipc-title__text: The TV equivalent of the uncanny valley !!!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Watching this gives you the feeling of walking around a wax museum. Yes it's got an aesthetic but it lacks context and gravitas. Combine this with the poor protagonists and it feels like looking into a doll's dead eyes. It's vacuous and empty. This is all the more shameful when the source work is considered. To have had such a plethora of artistic avenues to follow and yet settled on this attempt at a series is so surprising. The rich depth and beauty of the Silmarillion is NOT reflected at all. At best this can be compared with fantasy films of the 80's/90's (think Legend with CGI). I'd suggest giving it a miss.

I held off reviewing till the show was over, but man am I disappointed. The CGI environments are beautiful, half of the costumes are decent, and every once in a while there will be a line of dialog that is profoundly Tolkien-esque. Unfortunately, the majority of the dialogue, fight scene choreography, character development, world building, and general cohesive continuity is absolutely terrible. The characters are boring and unlikeable, their motivations are inconsistent and unclear, and the reveals in the last two episodes are unsurprising and uninspired. Even divorced from Tolkien, this series is a complete mess of story telling. It is baffling to me that so much money was spent on this show for this lackluster outcome.

ipc-title__text: Excellent show. Meets expectations and then some.

I'm not exactly sure why there are so many lower reviews. Maybe peoples expectations were way too high to begin with. Truly wonderful on so many levels. It is not action packed however and if that's what your expecting you will be disappointed. It has some action with excellent characters. So far I highly enjoy this show and hope they don't mess the show up in the future adding modern day things to it trying to make it fit with this day and age culture. So far, wonderful experience.

That means attention to detail, to the construction of characters and a well connected and interesting plot to keep the audience invested in it. Instead, it feels like it resorts to cheap tricks, which is ironic coming from what is supposed to be the most expensive tv show ever.Maybe it would be better if they did kept it more faithful to the well established universe of Tolkien (one of the most respected fantasy writers in history) and the great cinematic adaptations (one of the most successful, beautiful and likely enduring pieces of art in modern history).

ipc-title__text: Portrayal of Elves is a bit disappointing
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The portrayal of Elves is much disappointing as the elves in The Rings of Power are been disgusted everywhere, shown weak (like in the Witcher realm) and a bit ignorant. Elves should be much more powerful and noble, and full of knowledge and pride just like Tolkien described in his books, and Galadriel here is very aggressive and acts like a young, novice warrior and she looks very puny. Galadriel is one of most powerful and eldest of the Elves, lived through many things since the first day of Arda, should be much wise, calm and powerful, and of course taller. The actress is doing a good job but it's an impossible task to overcome Cate Blanchett's portrayal and performance here. The paced dialogues and the looks of the Elves (short hair, some ordinary looks and miscast of some actors, like the companions of Galadriel in the beginning) are also not helping.

I grew up with Tolkien's work, so I felt it a necessity to give this a try for myself. The fact that the creators thought they could change/rewrite Tolkien's work and come out with something better is a complete joke. Make no mistake, this is not Tolkien nor Lord of The Rings, it is simply generic modern fantasy.The writing is absolutely the worst part of the show. I don't understand how anyone could write it and be proud of what they've done. You can tell that the writers watched game of thrones before writing this because of the sheer array of cast, characters and "story-lines". Problem is, none of the stories are interesting.Do yourself a favor and give this show a skip. 4 episodes in and I won't be wasting anymore time on this garbage.

ipc-title__text: First episode is great, can't wait for more
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I have to admit I was a bit hesitant to give this a watch as so many IPs have been brutalized in recent years, but the first episode delivered on all aspects for me. It's a great blend of original story while blending with some key characters in early development. I can't say too much as have only watched the first episode, but it has me more drawn in that the Hobbit did and has paced itself much more akin to the original Jackson trilogy. I can only guess that the negatives are mostly coming from people who didn't even give it a try, as if a show had to be developed, this is definitely among the best that could come of it. KY opinion may change as more is unveiled, but for now I'm hooked and looking forward to more.

Honesty these fan boys and girls need to get over the fact that JRR Tolkien was not involved, he died in 1973 so his input was not expected or required, no it's not associated with the original books but it's not a book, it's a TV series, it stands alone and should be watched as such. Fits rich character development to breathtaking visuals, the series transports viewers to a world where epic battles and intricate plots intertwine. The casting choices bring depth and nuance to the characters, while the narrative expertly balances action with heartfelt moments. The world-building is meticulous, and the attention to detail is impeccable. Each episode offers a blend of suspense and intrigue, A true gem for fantasy enthusiasts.

The *Rings of Power* may not follow the book lore exactly, but it offers a compelling story. Each episode brings excitement, thrill, and leaves me longing for more. As someone who hasn't read the books but loves the movies, I think this show does a phenomenal job.The story and character development were done very well, and the quality of filming is on par with movies. The only thing I wished for was more action like in the films; however, episode seven of season two delivers what I had been waiting for.I'm eagerly anticipating the release of season three, as I've been more impressed with season two than with season one.

I challenge anyone to name even one character from this series that will be as memorable as a single member of the Fellowship. Honestly, this show is a disaster. It barely holds on to the name "The Lord of the Rings," and everything else is an embarrassing parody of the source material. The main characters? They don't just look different-they've been butchered in terms of personality and morality, completely disconnected from who they're supposed to be. And even if you try to pretend this is just another random fantasy series, it's still a painful watch. Let's break down exactly why this thing fails so miserably:Plot: It's hard to believe the writers had the books in front of them and still came up with this mess. The plot is incoherent, full of random additions that make no sense, and non-existent characters who don't belong anywhere near this story. There's absolutely no narrative cohesion, just a sloppy attempt at throwing together big set pieces and hoping something sticks.Character Development: What development? Every character has been stripped of their core traits. Orcs, elves, dwarves, humans, even wizards-none of them resemble their original counterparts. They're flat, soulless versions of what they should be, drained of all depth. In a world overflowing with potential for character growth, this show somehow manages to reduce everything to a cartoonish, shallow interpretation.Pacing: Painfully slow, dragging you through episode after episode with no reward at the end. There's zero sense of the epicness that Tolkien's world deserves. The storytelling is so devoid of energy or passion that it's a chore to get through each scene. Where is the sweeping grandeur? The love for the intricate cultures, landscapes, and histories of Middle-Earth? It's all been replaced by a dull, lifeless crawl.Dialogue: The dialogue is atrocious. Every conversation feels awkward and poorly written, like the writers were trying to sound profound but ended up cranking out generic, uninspired lines. I can't help but cringe every time the Harfoots appear-watching them interact feels like a punishment. The relationships between characters are forced and hollow, with zero emotional payoff. If one of them died, I wouldn't care. In fact, I might even be relieved just to thin the herd of forgettable personalities.Direction and Cinematography: Sure, the cinematography isn't terrible, but with a budget like this, the fact that it's merely decent is a disgrace. It feels like they threw money at the problem, expecting visuals to save the show. But pretty pictures without heart fall flat. The music, while not terrible, never rises to the emotional heights we expect from something tied to Middle-Earth.Special Effects: Technically speaking, the special effects are fine, but there's no magic to them. The creatures and landscapes are competently rendered, but they lack the sense of wonder and awe that the world of Tolkien demands. It all feels like a soulless, overproduced visual display that forgets to actually make you feel something.The Rings: Let's talk about the rings, the whole point of this series. They look utterly ridiculous. Oversized and cartoonish, like gaudy toys you'd win at a fair. In the hands of the dwarves, they look even worse, making them seem clunky and out of place. The rings are supposed to hold immense power and intrigue, but here they're nothing more than oversized, gaudy trinkets.In conclusion, despite the occasional decent technical aspect, this series is an absolute failure. It's a hollow, soulless shell of Middle-Earth, made worse by its failure to deliver on even the basic promises of a compelling story or faithful adaptation.

What a shame what a disgrace this is both first and second Seasons the main problem is the horrific god-awful casting it's like the first 30 people that wound up at Central Casting was told they're hired without even auditioning as great as the movies were for casting this is equally bad the opposite way but there is a mundane boring conversations of Plenty very very little action. Disappointing travesty that fails to respect Tolkien's legacy. The show takes unforgivable liberties with the source material, completely undermining the essence of Middle-earth. One glaring example is the absurd portrayal of Orcs as sympathetic, human-like creatures with families and babies. This utterly contradicts Tolkien's depiction of Orcs as embodiments of pure evil, created solely for destruction. The series sacrifices the moral clarity and depth of Tolkien's work in favor of modern, misguided reinterpretations. The writing is shallow, the characters lack the richness of their literary counterparts, and the plot meanders without purpose. This is not the world Tolkien painstakingly crafted, but a hollow, commercialized imitation that tarnishes his legacy.

Words can't fully capture how terrible this show is, but I'll give it a try...This series serves as a masterclass in "how not to write." Whether it's the acting, the execution of the story, or the pacing, everything is a mess. The plots are shallow, the build-ups are tedious, the twists and reveals are painfully underwhelming, and every character seems to have an absurdly low IQ. This is especially disgraceful considering that these characters are supposed to be high-merit heroes, like multi-thousand-year-old elven leaders.The billions of dollars spent on this production would have been better invested in writing and acting courses for the cast. While I appreciate the inclusion of diversity in the story, it shouldn't be done "just because." The show's attempts to address issues like toxic masculinity and traditional storytelling are so poorly executed that they only fuel the criticism, all while tarnishing a piece of literature that holds a special place in the hearts and minds of people worldwide. Although I didn't have high expectations for this project, I'm genuinely annoyed and upset.

"The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" disappoints with its sluggish pacing and excessive focus on character backstories and relationships. Straying far from Tolkien's epic narrative, the series drags viewers through tedious subplots, neglecting the heart of the story. With minimal progress on the main storyline, it fails to capture the essence of Middle-earth, leaving fans longing for the grandeur and adventure of the original novels. The overemphasis on character development detracts from the magic and enchantment that made Tolkien's world so captivating, resulting in a dull and uninspired adaptation that fails to do justice to its source material.

As a big fan of the original trilogy and The Hobbit trilogy, I must admit that I am very pleased with this tv show.I think that it was a great first season as a « big » introduction for what this show will become when it's completed.Of course it is very slow, very contemplative sometimes (maybe to much for some people) but I found it georgous. Where to start this review is an awkward thing to answer. As a Tolkien fan I was eager to venture back to middle earth like only a true fan could be. I watched the series as soon as it was released and again just recently. As a show one can not but love the scenes. CGI is slightly overdone and everything is slightly too sanitised but still worthy of a 8/10. Story itself is middling and does not follow the writings of Tolkien where it counts. This could be forgiven but for one thing. The characters are empty.The richest fantasy world ever created and yet the taste is overly sweet without any substance. Too many things do not make sense. It's almost like they have tried too hard and yet they have missed what makes JRR so wonderful. In the rush to set-up the coming series the character arc's and story have been pushed. This may be fine for the usual TV shows but not for a world of this breath. Once in a lifetime chance and the spirit of the middle earth has been corrupted.Just tried watching the second series and it is as poorly made as the first. Yes it's pretty due to the budget but the world is not middle earth as penned by JRR. I understand the need the producers were trying to meet, but to use Tolkien as the vehicle is incredibly sad. Just gets worse as the episodes continue. Now just watch with a sick fascination. How did this get made? Same developers as Concord?

ipc-title__text: This Mithril shirt is turning my skin green!

ipc-html-content-inner-div: After six episodes out of eight it can be easily stated that this is a great addition to cinematic Middle-Earth Universe.Astonishing production value, awesome technical execution and mesmerizing world-building.Done with love to the source material despite absolutely ludicrous bickering you may encounter online. Two initial episodes were enough (for me) to be transported yet again into the world of Tolkien, and as worthy depiction of it as seen before in both Jackson trilogies.By far one of the best epic fantasy pieces of fiction ever on screens.Hopefully this is only the beginning of multi-year journey.

I wanted to remain impartial to the immediate backlash this series obtained as a result of diverting away from the Tolkien lore. As much as I would agree that it was a poor decision for the writers to do so, my wish was simply to enjoy the creation for what it was.Unfortunately what this is; is extremely underwhelming. I have currently dragged myself through to episode seven. At this point morbid curiosity is the only excuse I have for continuing to watch.Each character in this story is vaguely introduced via overly pretentious and meaningless conversations in scenes that are devoid of any emotional connection to the audience.The pacing of the episodes is so sporadic that upon the arrival of action, these events seem random, misplaced and lack immersion. An attempt to fabricate the illusion of grandeur comes in the form of lengthy, awkward slow-motion that is so frequently used to patch the cracks it becomes confusing and even humorous at times.There is an ever present predictability surrounding each characters decision making whereby some potentially dynamic shifting choice is frequently interrupted by another character entering the scene out of nowhere, immediately returning their ark back to it's previously boring state. Blanketing all of this is a thick and noticeable layer of exactly zero chemistry between any pair of actors thus far.The orcs are portrayed as clowns, quite literally. They are not formidable nor fearsome and provide no element of danger or tension.The Elves do not appear ethereal and otherworldly as they are usually depicted and are more likened to regular men/women wearing prosthetic ears.The Men are obnoxious, theatrical and unbelievable. Mob mentality and sheeping is a reoccurring theme and no one outside of the main character circle seems to be able to think for themselves, there are moments where I feel like I'm watching Monty Python or an SNL reference sketch.The end result is a poorly written, poorly paced fantasy story about characters I've very quickly grown to loathe. It has the stench of inexperience, the innards of bad taste, a surface that lacks passion... It's a corpse with $100 bills for make up.

I'm a big Tolkien fan - love the Hobbit and Lord of the Rings books, and I enjoyed the Lord of the Rings movies.I was really hoping that 'The Rings of Power' would be a great show, but after five episodes, it's clear that it's not.First, the good things.1. The scenic shots (CGI, I presume) of the various locations are gorgeous, which makes sense given the budget.2. The orcs look amazing. Far better than the orcs in the Peter Jackson movies, which I thought looked a bit too weird a lot of the time. Anyway, these orcs look great.But that's where the good stuff ends. Everything else is awful.The costumes look really fake. You can see that they've spent 100 hours and a thousand dollars making some 'worn rags' that are shaded just right, and hang perfectly in position. They've spent so much money on the costumes (and some of the sets) that they've become 'hyper-real', and no longer look believable.The makeup is puzzling as well. So many of the women are clearly wearing rouge and eye shadow, which makes little sense in the world.But mostly it's the writing that falls short. Sadly, this includes the plot, the dialogue, the themes, the characterisation etc. - all the stuff that makes a good story.The actors may be quite good - I don't know - it's hard to be moved by performances that are limited by the awful script.The one feeling that keeps coming up as I watch is that I just don't care. Somehow, in five hours of TV, they have failed to give me a reason to care about any of the characters, or the plot. I don't think that's ever happened to me before.Sometimes I can see what they are trying to do with a scene - 'Oh, this is an exciting rescue scene', 'Oh, this is where they share some deep wisdom like Gandalf did', 'Oh, this is where they expound the themes'... but for some reason it just falls woefully short every time. It's like they know what they are supposed to do, but they just don't know how to do it.I'm starting to think that they took a dozen TV writers, fresh out of grad school, made them all read 'The Lord of the Rings' once, and then put them in a writers' room and told them to produce more of the same. As if they could somehow match Tolkien, with his years of life experience, mastery of ancient languages, and deep knowledge of medieval literature and thought. It's like me watching a video of Mohammad Ali boxing, and then thinking I can get into the ring and win a title.If this was some indie fantasy offering in a newly-written world, I would give this 4 or 5 stars for looking great, even though both my wife and I fell asleep in 3 out of 5 episodes.But this is a billion-dollar production in the best-built fantasy world in history. There's just no excuse for it being this bad, so I'm giving it 2 stars.

ipc-title__text: Story telling so bad it distorts the source material
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This show is slow and yet all over the place, but I think I can distil my discomfort with the show with its complete disregard for the passage of time.When we look at the prime source material - Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit, both of these stories are fundamentally about observing the limitations of the world and as a result, 'the journey'. I mean, The Hobbit was 90% 'the journey' and 10% Smaug. I appreciate the movies were probably different, but I haven't watched them.Similarly, Lord of the Rings was largely about the difficulties of the journey, singing songs, conflict set pieces, and recovery/friendly town hook ups in your typical story telling arc.However, this show? "We're over here, now we're over here". Its failing to suspend my disbelief. This is so contrary to the rules of the world! There is a fundamental failure in the ability for Amazon to tell a story here. I mean, I can forgive any actor or actress in this film for delivering a garbage performance on the grounds that they have a schizophrenic plot to work with that entirely disregards the point of the source materialAnd, I'm going to draw a parallel here. NuTrek (JJ Abrams Star Trek) has this same problem. J. J Abrams Star Trek established that people can beam for any planet to any other planet, which makes the entire concept of Star Ships entirely obsolete. Goodbye Star Trek. Because Star Trek is about the journey, not the destination. The payoff of the outcome can't be cashed without the struggles to achieve that within the rules of the world. If you have a Deus Ex that allows you to beam anywhere (thanks Kahn) then travelling in a star ship is like walking as opposed to taking a plane.And THAT is why The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power is a terrible, terrible show.

ipc-title__text: Morfydd Clark needs a few more acting classes
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The show is not THAT bad as the 1-star reviews would make you think it is, but the biggest problem, by far, is the lead actress, Morfydd Clark, who is absolutely horrible in every scene! How this person got past casting is beyond me... Again, the show has a lot of potential and maybe, with time, will turn into something great, but in its current form and with the main actress performing like an amateur, you won't be seeing that anytime soon. And people need to stop comparing this with Game of Thrones, two vastly different budgets and two vastly different casts. And yes, RoP took some liberties with the narrative and the characters, things that you won't find in Tolkien's lore, but that doesn't mean it's a 100% bad thing, you never know what could come up from this.

ipc-title__text: Watch on the largest screen you can find!

You can totally immerse yourself into this world, the quality feels like it was done for the cinema.Very good actors that bring their distinct and memorable characters to life, lovely script and dialogue with humor and a little wisdom.This was worth waiting for.
