And although I am sure there are many wigs involved, it always feels natural...

ipc-title__text: Fundamentally flawed, but surprisingly becoming better
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This is a very difficult one to rate. Were we not that familiar with the Lore surrounding Middle Earth, it would probably be seen with kinder eyes.Some storylines are close to unbearable (the harfoots, Theo...) and Galadriel could probably be better cast. But the main problem perhaps is the fundamental incoherences regarding the world of Middle Earth.On the other side, Celebrimbor, Durin, Elendil, Elrond and surprisingly Sauron are big standouts, and their plotlines have taken the series to a higher level, especially in the second part of season 2.Overall, the good things are becoming surpisingly close to great, but some major incongruences and boring plotlines are very easy to hate.I remain skeptical, but I am looking forward to seeing more, at least much more than after the first season.

ipc-title__text: Perfect blend of action and drama.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Season 1 was bit slow may be due to introductions and unfamiliar characters but season 2 is surprisingly excellent. Visually spectacular. Richness in each and every frame made every penny of budget and every minute of audience time.Last 2 episodes are no less than any movie in terms cinematography and war choreography.Season 2 is a perfect blend of action and drama. Many loose ends from season 1 ,lord of the rings and hobbit are connected here.After watching disastrous House of the dragons season 2 ,this series is a sigh of relief l. Hope Amazon will keep this up and deliver best in season 3.

"The Rings of Power" is a series that promises much but delivers little. The narrative is slow and boring, the characters are flat and forgettable, and the overall atmosphere is very soporific rather than epic. Middle-earth, once a place of unforgettable adventures, appears as an often dull world. Special effects are not enough to save a series that lacks heart and originality. A dull, non-canonical, poorly written series that disappoints Tolkien fans, in short "The Rings of Power" is an expensive series whose end result is a disappointment. Failed. The Rings of Power: An epic delusion. The end.

ipc-title__text: A wonderful expansion of the world of Tolkien
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This may not be a 100% accurate translation of Tolkiens work but the entertainment value is great and I am happy to be back in the world of Tolkien. Picture and production value is phenomenal. Some of the scenes in darker settings are hard to make out, but that is the only complain i would have.The show takes thousands of years of history and attempts to tell them in a more compact format in order to draw it all together and avoid having to create an endless show. The task of attempting to tell the mythology of Tolkien is a daring one and they do a great job at telling all of the important bits and pieces so far.

There's not a single character I like in this series. Characters such as Elrond, who are supposed to be the embodiment of strength, wisdom, and leadership, have been reduced to little more than your local librarian who enjoys sipping chai and writing poems. The portrayal of such iconic characters feels off, and it's hard to connect with any of them emotionally or intellectually. There's a lack of depth in the personalities, and instead of feeling like I'm watching mighty figures of Middle-earth, it feels more like a shallow caricature of what they should be. *
Tolkienwould undoubtedly turn in his grave at how far removed this interpretation is from the complex and layered characters he originally crafted.

While it's clear that significant effort and resources went into the second season of The Rings of Power, the series ultimately falls short. The narrative struggles to find its footing, with a disjointed story and basic screenwriting principles seemingly overlooked. Characters come across as one-dimensional and unrelatable, failing to engage the audience.The pacing is another issue, with slow, meandering scenes that often feel unnecessary. Despite the large cast and substantial budget, the series is weighed down by dull sub-plots, uninspired dialogue, and performances that lack the necessary spark to bring the world to life.As a viewer, I kept hoping for improvement, but instead, I was left with hours of lost potential. The twists and reveals, which should have been moments of excitement, were often so obvious that they left me feeling more like a passive observer than an engaged audience member.It's particularly disheartening to see this series tied to the legacy of The Lord of the Rings films, which were masterful in their execution. This series had the potential to be a worthy successor, but it misses the mark in too many ways, highlighting the need for stronger writing and a more compelling vision.

ipc-title__text: The character development that season 1 desperately needed
ipc-html-content-inner-div: They really flesh out the characters well in this season. You see a lot more of their motivation and their relationships become more complex. This is made more interesting for the viewers by considering how these motivations are affected by the characters being elves, who view the world very different from middle earth humans, and even further from how we would view the situation. Things become much more cutthroat this season but the evil is hiding behind the beauty of an elf.Overall, it seems like they continued on the same track as season one but they added to the stakes of the story by fleshing out the characters and their motivations. This season makes it possible to fall in love with some of the characters you vibe with the most.

ipc-title__text: Really Good Big Picture type of story
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This is the first show in a very long time that has me wanting more. I am into monster of the week type of stories. I do not care for too much small talk and mundane interaction between characters. This story developed rather well and also introduced new characters along the way. We are not stuck with the same few characters episode after episode. Although, my suspension of disbelief gets ruined when writers have the 5 most important people in the world run into each other at a fast-food joint at the same time the 5 greatest armed robbers are robbing the restaurant. Then they all pair up and fall in love. Plus they happen to be good looking too, and only 19-24 years old. I am glad this show did not fall hard into this trap. It ruins it for me every time. I do not want to see personal stories between 2 people that have little to do with the main story. I don't care that characters have feelings for each other. I don't care that they may fall in love. This interaction or context can be demonstrated in other genres, so there is no need to include it here. Show us stuff that only exists in middle-earth. If you need to put the girl and the guy together, do it quickly and MOVE ON! This is a land of make believe and there is so much more that an active imagination can create, and it seems that this show could actually pull this off. Less mundane drama, more active imagination. We need big story stuff with a monster of the week thrown in for rising action.

This is one of the worst TV show ever made in human history. You can spend bilions on CGI but it will never save the bad writing. You can see how untalented the writers are and what a mistake Amazon did. When you are so full of yourself that you think you can do a better job than Tolkien himself this is the proof you can't. Characters are acting like they never would, story is told like it is some cheap soap opera on cw. It was stated that only 37% of people who starts watch the show have watched all episodes. Most bizare thing is that amazon is blaming fans of Tolkien. Like why have this property value? Yea bc of fans you blame.

I'll start off by saying I haven't read ANY of the books, so I could not care less about it's authenticity to the source material. The show held true to the movies, the character arcs were maintained and was very clear how this world worked into the plots of the movies. It was very entertaining and kept me wanting to watch the next episode, so that in itself is a huge success. Unlike the new House of Dragons which was erratic in its story/timeline and mind numbingly boring at points, this reboot was well worth the wait and the watch. I'm anticipating the next season and hope this can be a 5+ season effort.

In Turkish we have a saying: "Zorla güzellik olmaz (Beauty cannot be created by forcing)."It doesn't matter even if Amazon poured 1 billion dollar into this project. They just bought the copyright for names. This is LOTR only in name; rest of it is just another Netflix type high-fantasy drama. The characters, dialogue, atmosphere, every other element is forced. This is Frankenstein's monster; they took a part from here, another part from there; haphazardly sewed them together, Lo and Behold! This disgusting TV series came out.I'm not saying Amazon shouldn't make such a Netflix type fantasy series; just don't tarnish Tolkien's name. This is nothing like the nostalgic original LOTR trilogy.20-30 years later when this fad dies out, people will look back and say: "Wow, corporations can be this evil. Money can make them blind". In this day and age nobody can say "The Emperor has no clothes" because they will be cancelled; however in the future, this TV series will be seen a joke. Shame on whoever partook in this abomination. Shame on you for tarnishing Tolkien's name for money.

ipc-title__text: So bad it hurts to watch
ipc-html-content-inner-div: It doesn't matter if you like the books or the previous movies, the score of 1 out of 10 would still remain, cause this is not just a bad adaptation of the Middle Earth universe, this is bad on all levels of filmmaking.Everything about this is lacking of passion, love or care from a movie making standpoint. There was no love for either the wonderful medium of film nor for the stories Tolkien once made. This show doesn't add more, it has no purpose, reason or excuse to have been made.This was made ONLY to make money, it was low quality produced garbage, it doesn't matter how much money they spent on it nor how it looks, it completely lack everything in the departments of story, characters, excitment. And nothing feels like Lord of the Rings. Admittedly, I haven't watched every episode, I gave up after 5 cause what I saw simply unwatchable.But what can you expect from Amazon, they made some garbage games too, like New World, who wasn't 10% of what World of Warcraft was. And I see this here too, it's not even 10% of ANY fantasy TV series worth watching. It lacks heart, soul and feels like a hallow shell.Be warned, do not waste your time watching this, don't spend money on this. Avoid at all costs. Shows like this ruin Hollywood, please don't encourage it, it's so painfully bad, it hurts to watch.

ipc-title__text: Watched the first season. Did not enjoy it.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The dialogue is terrible. Rarely if ever do characters talk to each other. Instead every conversation is just a setup to an over-written monologue about darkness and the sea.There isn't a single likeable character in the whole showm, except for Elrond and Prince Durin. Galadriel is obnoxious, Halbrand is from Manchester and has no charisma, the stranger is boring, the Harfoots are Irish traveller stereotypes dialed up to 11, and all the humans are utterly dull and forgettable 1 dimensional add-ons.Characters die that you have absolutely no interest in. Yet the music kicks in to try and force an emption, that isn't there, out of you.This show also claims to be inclusive, and it is, if you call 3 black actors in a cast of about 30 inclusive. I wouldn't mind. But it doesn't even make sense... I mean you have society consisting solely of white Dwarves, and one black dwarf as the princess... Where are the other black dwarves. I'm not saying "get rid of the black dwarf". I'm saying "make the general dwarven population more evenly black and white, so that it makes sense".I have the same issue with the black elf. Why are there 99 white elves and 1 black one. At least make it 60/40 or something. If anything. The show somehow seems more offensive by pointing out its inclusive, rather than less offensive.Some pros about the series:

ipc-title__text: I waited until watching the whole season before reviewing.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I wont lie, it was a bit confusing and slow for the first few episodes. Trying to figure out who characters were and whether they were god or bad or even important was a struggle, but a fun struggle at least. I guessed a couple characters before they were revealed. Last few episodes got me hooked, and I was sad to see we were only getting eight episodes this season.The good: High production value. Feels like you are watching an extended version of a theatrical release. The story is good once you get a feel for what's going on, and the costumes and makeup are top notch!The bad: If I could say one thing that really bugged me, especially toward the last episodes, it's how completely the Hobbits or half foot or whatever changed their ways, which they were so serious about in the beginning. They basically went from, "Nobody leave the trail even if it means we have to leave the crippled behind!" to "Oh hey let's not only start acting brave and heroic, but willingly send a child to go with someone who is being chased by evil people who just murdered one of us! Yeah no problem! Here's a big lovely dovey farewell scene!Also I can see what they are doing with Poppy Proudfellow, but she is not the Samwise the Brave they are trying to make her out to be lol.

Enjoying the slow burn of this first season, looking forward to four more! This show is visually stunning and very enjoyable.Got into the books after the Peter Jackson trilogy and I am enjoying the slower pace and greater focus on set up and drama. Rings of Power feels like Tolkien to me.I am very happy the show runners decided to go with a story from the 2nd age rather than a remake of the Lord of the Rings or the Hobbit. There is so much content written by Tolkien and it is lovely seeing how the show runners are adapting it. I am very impressed with how accurate they have been with the lore and still maintaining an entertaining story line. Can't wait till season 2!

Overall the story drags on and on with some really epic moments but the rest of the time it falls flat on its face. The cast has potential to be an amazing group with some cool moments. It feels like this was a filler season with not a lot of action or great story moments. The woodland people feels like such a middle of nowhere story with not much added to the storyline. It just brings more questions with no answers at all. I'm at the end and I'm still confused as to who is who and what purpose they have in the story. It could be someone amazing and fun but literally no hints makes me uneasy. The season also feels like you're supposed to forget about that charecter until they randomly appear. Hopefully next season has answers.

ipc-title__text: Beautiful and a long time fan

ipc-html-content-inner-div: Messy timelines, wooden acting. But it looks pretty. Overall boring and it's a glorified d&d campaign with a tolkien skin. Not enough to appeal to most LOTR fans and too bland to appeal to general fantasy fans. They have turned major lore characters into shadows of themselves. While the majority of their new characters add nothing. The humanizing of the orcs takes away the spirit of escapism. It's okay to have something be purely evil. The added story with Elrond I'd empty and meaningless and has no root in the lore. The dwarves are near perfect and are one of the high points of the show in style and substance.

ipc-title__text: Not that bad, but far from a great show

ipc-html-content-inner-div: I so wanted to love this series and I was intrigued & excited after episode one, but now, 50% through season one... oh dear.The writing and story are so dull and the characters are developing awfully, generating little connection with the viewer.Ignoring some of the divergence from Tolkien's Lore, I actually think most of the cast are likeable and the landscapes are awesome. However, as someone who's read and loved The Silmarillion, The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit, The Rings of Power pales in comparison.If you love a good story or you want something that is a close reflection of Tolkien's work then this is probably not for you...If you're simply happy to experience an excellent visual spectacle and some epic scenes of Elves charging about on horseback or Hobbits running across amazing landscapes then give it a whirl and make up your own mind.I will continue to persevere as I am a big fan of the broader Tolkien universe, but if it wasn't for that I'd have given up!

I was lucky enough to have watched a few videos on youtube on the History/Timeline of Middle Earth. That made the backdrop of the this show far more digestible. Otherwise, like some people said, the plot may come across as gibberish and boring.For anyone wishing to continue the show, I highly recommend doing that. Otherwise names like Morgoth and Valar just won't mean anything to youIt's quite interesting understanding the origin of deities, races, and wizards, etc. In this word. Even die hard fans of the LOTR trilogy or the books may not have ever fully picked up on the actual history of Tolkein's universe. So highly recommend finding info on those first.I may fault the show for not spending more time introducing its lore. But I certainly find this far superior to The Hobbit movies which just had mass appeal and little depth.

Having read all of Tolkien's published work and watched most of the available adaptions of his writing, I feel compelled to give my biased view to counterbalance the review bombing and misrepresentation going on.I'll start by saying that the world created by Tolkien is, in my humble view, one of the single greatest things ever written by anyone. At the same time, I find his writing to be average at best, especially when compared to other prolific writers. The magic of Tolkien, for me, is the world, and not the syntax of his writing.The Rings of Power are not Jacksons portrayal of the original trilogy, but they are also not the massive disaster that was the hobbit. The success of the original trilogy is this sense a shame, as people go into any portrayal of the beloved story expecting Jackson, and not Tolkien. This aspect alone, I think, helps explain the mixed feedback the Rings of Power has received. But no director should have the honour of becoming canon over Tolkien, and everyone has the right to try and create their own portrayal of Middle Earth. Especially when one keeps in mind that Jackson also condensed the books, leaving out many great characters present in the original works (Tom Bombadil comes to mind straight away).This show has the inhumane task of portraying around 2000 years of history, and to do that, shortcuts have to be taken. Otherwise, fans would never be able to see the events of the Second Age on their screens. This is a shame, but big events in the Middle Earth are spread over a great period of time. As such, I have no problems with the show taking liberties in condensing the great history of the SA. If anything, I find it fascinating to observe as the creators had to decide, which events to display, and how to portray them.There are many legitimate critiques of this show, as is the case with any piece of art. The only way to find out if this show is for you, is to watch it. And keep in mind that like every other adaptation ever, this is not canon.As for me, this show scratches the itch of seeing Middle Earth during the SA, and I am able to forgive the showrunners for not being entirely faithful to the original material.

ipc-title__text: Very generic and clean Narnia/Wheel of time kind of show
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I was so excited for last 3 years to dive into Middle Earth one more time. Deeply hurt and disappointed, can not connect visually or emotionally with the show. Watched both episodes twice in English as well as in my native language just so I can force myself to love this show. Not even close, did not like it.Elves look like men, lack that ethereal glow and demeanor. PJ captured it perfectly, every movement, every word they said had a impact that we are looking at a superior creation of Iluvatar.Even after 4 hours (2X) of this show, I still do not feel connected to these stories or their fate. As a LOTR fan I will watch every episode in hope to feel connected.You can see that village of men was created a few months ago. It does not give a feeling of middle earth. It was exactly like Wheel of Time show. Amazon you messed it up real bad.Dwarves are the best till now, love Durin and Disa. Acting is on point, feels great. Harfoots are good to have in this show, a nice unexpected addition.

ipc-title__text: A real review from someone that doesn't read the books.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This is what happens when you try to turn a very intricate/detailed book into a live action series. Avid readers will critique this to every little detail.Take all that away and take this as it is...a well directed, well written and thought out production so far in these 2 episodes. 60M per episode sounds a bit of a stretch but so far so good.I love how they dont use big screen actors and all the actors were fantastic. Sound/Score was on point. VFX was good but with 60M per episode i believe some shots could have been done on site vs a green screen.Good job so far by JA Bayona and the crew. Looking forward to seeing the rest of the series.

The production values on this show are through the roof, as you'd expect from the amounts of money apparently involved.The first couple of episodes offer a tantalizing start that I hope will continue to develop and find its feet.The big question for me will be if the script and story can elevate this show above 'looks really good' and deliver some compelling interest. But for now it's off to a great start.There's a lot of setup required for this story to work properly, especially if it's going to appeal to people starting fresh in the Tolkien worlds. But Tolkien offered plenty of material to be worked from when he set up his backgrounds to Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit, and some of that material has 'golden age' written all over it - so we should be in for a treat.

Watching the "Lord of the Rings" TV series has truly been an experience of pure pleasure! Every episode feels like stepping into a majestic and immersive world that brings Tolkien's rich universe to life. The characters are brilliantly portrayed, each with their own unique depth and emotional arcs that keep you invested in their journeys. The decor and set design are nothing short of breathtaking - from the sprawling, ancient forests to the grandiose cities of Middle-earth, every frame feels like a masterpiece.But what truly stands out to me is the character of Galadriel. I'm absolutely captivated by her presence on screen! She embodies such grace, strength, and wisdom. Watching her navigate the challenges and struggles with an aura of mystery makes her a fascinating character to follow. Her story arc has layers of depth, showing her as a powerful yet vulnerable figure, and it's impossible not to be in awe of her journey.The production quality is on another level. You can feel the dedication and craftsmanship in every detail, from the costumes to the special effects. It's a visual feast, and the storytelling perfectly balances epic action scenes with intimate character moments that pull at your emotions. I was hooked from the first episode and found myself eagerly anticipating each new twist and turn.The show doesn't just retell the story we know and love from the books and movies-it expands upon it, exploring the lore in ways that feel fresh and exciting. The world-building is incredible, and it's fascinating to see new corners of Middle-earth come to life. And the music? It's hauntingly beautiful, capturing the epic scale and emotional undertones of the series perfectly.I honestly can't wait for the next season! This show has exceeded my expectations in every way, and I'm so excited to see where they take the story next. "The Lord of the Rings" TV series is a masterpiece in modern television, and I'm fully in love with everything it has to offer!

This series was an absolute delight to watch and I'm rooting for a season 3. Don't listen to all of the people comparing it to the originals, etc.. People say the elves are too weak and human like or the orcs are this and that and it just doesn't need to be said. The acting is amazing and it delivered what I personally wanted from the show, although, I'm aware everyone's opinions and views are different but I think it's a must watch. Sauron was my played by a brilliant actor and needs special recognition. Appreciate the show for what it is, and in its own right it's a great watch. 10 out of 10.

ipc-title__text: Rings of power is the missing puzzle
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I have read about these events but there are people who know the story only from the cinema. So this is their only chance to get for real what is the whole story about. To understand how the rings were made and more importantly - why. To understand the complicated faith of elfs, dwarfs, human, orcs, hobbits, sorcerers and how is all connected. To see how the heroes made their way and how the legends did become what they are in the Lord of the rings. And it's also beautifully made. The creators put their work also. 10 out of 10 just because.If you name yourself a true fan of the saga you have to watch this.

Excellent series so far - can't wait for the next ones! As an avid Lord of the Rings fan, this series extends the greatness of the original story and gives an excellent back story to how the rings of power came into existence. If you've read the books or played the video games, you'll see lots of references throughout. When watching the series, I loved experiencing stories of characters frequently mentioned in the books and films and seeing how they intertwine and develop to eventually lead to events that happen in the Lord of the Rings. The music is beautiful and magical, matching the series. Thank you for extending the world of Tolkien and bringing fans an additional perspective on the original story.

ipc-title__text: Everybody hated the Hobbit now loves it
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I've thoroughly enjoyed watching *Rings of Power*. It's easy to forget that when *The Lord of the Rings* films were first released, there was a lot of criticism regarding their accuracy to the books as well-whether it was Tom Bombadil being omitted or other creative decisions. The same thing happened with *The Hobbit* films; initially, many people didn't like them, but now they are widely appreciated. It's important to keep in mind that Amazon doesn't have all the rights to the books, which creates some significant challenges in adapting the material. Despite this, I think the show does an impressive job of capturing the spirit of Tolkien's world. The series itself is very well made, from its visuals to the storyline, and it offers a fresh take while staying rooted in the mythos. I'm excited to see how it continues to unfold.

The show has improved a great deal in Season 2, though there are some pacing issues. However, it has nailed its characters and their motivations and is putting all the pieces in place to move the storyline along. The arcane lore of the books has been streamlined, simplified and is laser focused on young audiences. This is in many ways the opposite of Game of Thrones, and it intends to cast a wide net. It's a good versus evil narrative with twists that a critical thinking adult will probably see coming a mile a way but would delight a fourteen-year-old.The actors all play their parts well. The set designers, costume designers, sound editors and the entire technical crew deserve all the praise in the world.I do think that it's by genre necessity a little slow at times, especially when following a story that an individual might not connection with. There are many characters, each designed to appeal to a different type of person. Therein lies the pacing issue. The Peter Jackson films had the benefit of large swathes of time when the characters were all together, at least in the first film.So, I do hope the pacing improves as the story moves along. But I do think that those who are discovering it as tweens and tweens will grow up loving it and its characters.

Rings of Power is, at best, underwhelming. It struggles to rise above mediocrity, with nothing truly standing out. The script feels forced and lacks the authenticity one would expect from such a high-budget production. The dialogue, in particular, feels disjointed and uninspired.The fight scenes don't help the situation-they're reminiscent of cheesy 90s cartoons, overly choreographed and lacking any real sense of danger or excitement. It's hard to understand what the creators were aiming for with this series. Overall, Rings of Power falls short of capturing the magic and depth fans hoped for.

I've read Tolkien my whole life and loved Peter Jackson's films. I waited for about a decade for this deal to come together. It's already forgotten and certainly won't be included as an entry into Tolkien's works. I'm just sad and disappointed.Elrond had fought a couple wars by this time and they make him someone who hides under bridges like a child. He's a man of strength in body and mind by this time. Galadriel is somehow a great warrior. Her brothers are all dead. I don't see any sign of strength or wisdom.The show can't even portray natural human behavior and emotions. It's all backwards and doesn't touch any emotional strings.

ipc-title__text: This show is one of the best I have ever seen!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This show is amazing and does not disappoint! I love that it has the same vibe as The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit, directed by Peter Jackson. This show is visually stunning and the characters are intricate and the acting is amazing. I love that we are getting this into a show instead of a three-part movie and appreciate the hour-long episodes. The script was very well written and the characters and the actors chosen to play them are likable. I do not understand the bad reviews some people have left, this show is amazing! It is a must-watch for all Tolkien fans and deserves praise for the masterpiece that it is.

This show seems to have very disjointed and rushed storytelling. The character development is mediocre at best. The writing in the show and the story itself is predictable and is uninteresting at best. The majority of people I've talked to do not like this show, I share the same sentiment. After watching the entire show, and some parts multiple times, this is a show I would never watch again. Compared to the movies and the books, this show does not seem to do justice to the lore at all. The show runners added their own weird twist to everything and it did not make sense. I'm glad if some folks enjoyed it. I did not.

With all the money in the world and one of the greatest IP's ever created, Amazon still couldn't turn out a positive experience.The only positive thing to say is really the quality of the visuals, which is expected given the budget.The main protagonist, Galadriel, was unlikeable and significantly and unbelievably overpowered. One day Hollywood will realize that not all protagonists need to be super powered and all supporting characters useless. You almost wanted to root for Sauron to win. They butchered the existing lore as well as many of the characters by trying to shoe-horn in modern world-views and tropes.It was extremely obvious who Sauron was going to be from the start. 90% of the first season was trying to trick you into wondering who Sauron is and they failed miserably. I shan't go into detail on how you can tell who the villain is almost immediately, but if you follow common trends in Hollywood writing/casting, you will have an idea.It is blindingly obvious that the same love, care, and devotion that Peter Jackson put into sculpting his original trilogy masterpiece cannot be found here.

I confess to a certain skepticism about this project: The train wreck that was THE HOBBIT series soured me to any notion of bringing more Tolkien stories to the screen.But I found that season 1 stayed truer to the Tolkien vision than I had imagined. The series is well crafted and acted, and I find several characters quite well-cast. I'm...still not on board with the depictions of Elrond and Celebrimor, but I'll defer judgement for now.The creation of characters and events which did not appear in Tolkien's writings, while regrettable, fall within the filmmakers' discretion. They need to tell a coherent story on a small screen to a modern audience, so I'm willing to give them a bit of creative latitude.

ipc-title__text: Silmaril in the world of Swarovski crystals
ipc-html-content-inner-div: If you see Professor Tolkien as Iluvatar, the creators of the series are hardly the Valar, but then again they have just a few songs of the Music of the Ainur album to build off of and no direct line to Iluvatar like Manwe had.Analogies aside, it is a very watchable show. I'm having a second go at the moment and enjoying every last bit.Is it right to condense the timeline, add debatable personality traits to the characters, take extensive creative freedom with the storylines, create crazy tension between Him and Galadriel?For me it's justified. It's insanely hard to adapt these stories. They wisely chose the Second Age with many blindspots to fill and made it work. I'm eager to see what they do next and really hope they won't pay too much attention to the haters.What is there to hate, really? The series doesn't follow one of the "golden formulas" that Netflix uses coming down to the same stories in various settings, boring moneymaking.This one is fresh, gripping and visually impeccable.Shout out to the black elves and beardless dwarves. For the life of me can't get why black people shouldn't play elves. Makes no sense at all. If someone's key takeaway from the books was that white skin is a superior trait, you should question yourself not the show creators.Let's admit that the Years of the Trees have passed, but these Years of the Sun are not too bad, give them a try!

ipc-title__text: Does Lords and hobbit more than proud! Superb
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Gives lord of the rings and the hobbits a backing that it actually deserves! This was so brilliant. Setting the future up of the later series but giving more of an actual back story to things that makes the lord of the rings and hobbits seem like better movies. This series as buffed and revilatised the whole franchise TR Tolkien would be proud! Please keep up the good work and keep this pace going! We watched the whole seasons so quickly but was amazed with every episode. There seemed to be so many possibilities in this new and exciting world! Where the originals are quite liner this feels free!

ipc-title__text: I was really disappointed on so many levels...
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I really hesitated to write any critique of Rings of power at all... is it worth the effort? First of all the show is mostly beautiful to look at, it has good actors, good props, beautiful,landscapes, a good score... but something feels strangely odd! At first it is the dialogue... a lot of what the characters are saying does not really make a lot of sense to me, or at last i can't connect... pseudo-archaisms are at odds with strengely modern figures of speech, it does feel forced. The it is storytelling... too often story elements do not fit, actions of characters in certain situations or to one another do not make sense... this is all so strange, and why? Time and geography seemingy do not exist, neither does logistics ... or logic! Worst of all i fear is characterisation... the main character is an unempathic bully who likes to boss people around and humiliate other persons, seemingly enjoying their too obvious unabilities. If you want to estrange viewers from formerly well liked book-characters that is the way to go, but is it clever? All in all at its best the first season was a very mediicre fantasy show, at its worst it was disastrous bad storytelling, bad plot, unlikeable or plainly boring characters, exaggerated and unbelievable action scenes, logic errors en masse... sadly it all keeps adding up. In the beginning i was agitated, in the end i just didn't care anymore...

ipc-title__text: Rings of power is a masterpiece everyone needs in this dark age
ipc-html-content-inner-div:
"The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power" is definitely worth your time. Unlike other major fantasy series,
like "House of the dragon" and Disney's Star Wars it doesn't ever want to shock you with graphic violence, clumsy minority representations or epic sceneries. On the contrary, it feels so small compared to the aforementioned fictional worlds, and yet it is so beautiful! The series is a classic fairytale, more classic even, than the original movie trilogy, since this antique title of Tolkien's work must be righteously extended to "The Rings of Power", so full of the writer's kind and magical spirit. The actors' performance is pretty good, although Morfydd Clark spoils the whole thing from time to time, and, of course, 'political correctness gone mad' criticism that did not spare the series, is simply absurd. In fact, it has no political agenda whatsoever, except for notions of peace and respect for the enemy. Isn't that what we need in this bloody time of war and dissent? I can't wait for season two, and I hope creators won't let all the varied negative feedback let them stray from the original idea.

ipc-title__text: Sit back and enjoy the ride
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Was hesitant to watch- but I shouldn't have let the negative hype delay me.SERIES WAS GREAT. Some highlights:Appreciate the show wasn't over-reliant on CGI. Costumes, sets, makeup, props are amazing. No shortcuts taken.Plot and characters develop over the series. You feel like your on the journey too. I found myself enjoying what each character brought to the show.Plenty of links to LOTR lore. Even if not fully accurate, most shows have to adapt books to film. I'm not mad. Reading and watching are totally different experiences.I appreciate the diversity in characters and representation was done well. Nothing felt forced.I strongly hope this series continues and hope this review helps encourage others to watch!

Even if you are not a fan of fantasy, still this show is worth watching. I'm not a fan myself, I haven't even seen all of the Hobbit saga. But this story is just breathtaking. The hobbits are so natural and real, really skilled in stealth and surviving in the world full of dangerous creatures. The dwarves are also so alive and likable, so simple and sweet, strong hands but tender souls.All the production team made a great work: awesome fighting scenes, weapons, costumes, sets are all just great.Dialogs are interesting, with important messages.I think the whole story feels so real cause there are no absolute bad and good guys hear, no black and white. All characters are not 2d they're complicated and therefore real. Finally, the Rings we deserve!

ipc-title__text: People are way too hard on this series
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I liked it and thought it was fairly easy to follow. If you are confused, just watch a YouTube companion video on the first and second episode and you'll be fine. In general, I think the quality of this series vs the movies is similar to the quality of the Star Wars series compared to the movies.The story is new and characters are mostly new, but it is important to understand the backstory of the legacy characters to fully appreciate them. ipc-title__text: I adored this show, brilliant to rewatch

ipc-html-content-inner-div: I've finally had time to sit and binge the whole first season, and I'm glad I did, if I stuck to watching it as released I think I would have given up early on as the first few episodes are very very slow and hardly kept my attention, but as the story progressed and you got more involved with the plot and characters, the show only got better, thanks in part of the outstanding cinematography keeping on par with the epic movies, and keeping the story tied neatly tied to the franchise, and not causing massive plot holes or errors like other shows seem to do (except the opening scene of LOTR FOTR shows a much older Galadriel getting her ring lol) I also enjoyed the vagueness of "the stranger" is and who ends up being Sauron... many wrong guesses while watching.The only downside I find (Its the same with any prequel series) is all peril of some characters completely goes away as you know they survive... there in the film later! And as much as I like Roberts Aramayo's portrayal of Eldrond it is missing some of the "agent smith" I liked about the originalDefinitely looking forward to next season!

ipc-title__text: Honest review from a normie standpoint
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I have no in-depth knowledge of the Lore except having watched PJ triology a long long time ago ... so from a normie point of view this felt CHEAP ! The acting was below average : no emotions were conveyed , reactions felt unnatural .. the writing and dialogues are a JOKE ! It felt like it's treating me like a toddler, stating obvious things bluntly .. Some sets looked nice but some looked awfull, The costumes felt cheap 3D mass printed , especially the Numenorian ones .. The characters are insufferable , unlikeble , and the main character Galadriel is very intolerable, she's portrayed as a superhero but it doesn't work, this is so badly written that it would take you a season to catch the names of the rest of the characters. I felt indifferent to most of them facing hardships , i didn't care , and for some others i was rooting for their enemies !! What a shame.

It's like making a movie on Jesus where he is a turtle that has tea with Satan and instead of dieing for our sins, he farts a lot.Would i recommed anyone watch this? Not really. ipc-title__text: Visually gorgeous, but otherwise frustratingly mediocre and bland
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power is not as bad as I expected it to be, but I am not impressed or amazed by it. I had high hopes for it, because it could've been amazing, but it's not. It looks visually gorgeous and beautiful (the landscapes and the cities are beautiful), but I find little depth in it and I'm more than a little bit annoyed by scenes, which have clearly been added to this series in order to make it more action-packed and longer than it needs to be (a certain swimming scene is simply ridiculous, not to mention a slow-motion horse riding scene, which makes no sense at all).Fortunately, this series is not as bad as the horrendous The Wheel of Time (it was simply horrible, especially the last episode of 1st season), but it's not much better, because the creators and writers disregard many things and details that Tolkien had in his books and have made the script suitable for viewers of all ages, which results in mediocre storytelling. The lack of respect towards Tolkien is evident in many scenes. When compared to HBO's House of the Dragon, this series is no match to it in terms of writing, details and immersiveness.I sincerely hope that this series gets much better, but I'm not holding my breath. Considering the amount of money spent in the making of this epic spectacle, I find it worrisome that Amazon didn't hire better script writers, because this series desperately needs better writing.My verdict is: 5/10 stars.

Purists may be afraid of change, but I can recognize good casting acting production and writing, and this has it all. First episodes too slow? No, that's called world building. They didn't feel slow at all to me and I was completey absorbed into it.The problem with purists is they go in with so many expectations. It's like wanting a new restaurant to serve your favorite food you've been eating for years- they just aren't ready for something new but they can't admit it to themselves so they end up criticizing and hating everything that doesn't taste "exactly" like their favorite food.The problem with that mentality is you will slowly become a hardened shell of opinions and preferences, less flexible, less objective, and less accepting of anything different than what your used to.The thing they don't keep in mind is that everything- and I mean everything, is inspired by something else. That means the originals were inspired by something too. That is how art and creativity is born, from inspiration.Only snobs believe in true originality, a wise man knows he is the product of his environment and everything that came before him, and that should be humbling to one's ego.I think this series is an incredible spin-off, and I couldn't be happier with the start of it. Ignore the rigid purists and dive in. Enjoy the new.

Bad in an EPIC way.Waste of money and tiime.More could have been done to bring this to life. The writing was poor, the acting was half baked and the CGI was very, very poor.Not even the music was a complement but rather a distraction, as if they wanted to merge religious concept in a fantasy setting.Unsure what the writers were aiming for, and if they even knew what they were doing.Some shots were extremely dary or too red or too gold, and was just hard to see for you to appreciate.They need to go back to the drawing board and get this one right.Al in all, there is a chance to redeem this show, but much work is needed.

Rings of Power shows what money can buy: incredible sets, unbelievable costumes, impeccable production. And it shows what it can't: script. Because you need time to write good fantasy. And anyone who spends US$250 million on rights alone and needs to justify it to shareholders has no time to waste. There's a reason why Peter Jackson spent 4 years just adapting the script for Lord of the Rings, an already complete story. This series is even more problematic because it is not a direct adaptation, but practically a new story. Tolkien took 12 years to write Lord of the Rings and Martin will be writing his books for 30 years. Fantasy is difficult. In a world of elves and magic rings, you must take special care to write a story that is powerful and yet believable. Rings of Power is not believable, so it has no power at all.

ipc-title__text: Tolkien's soul is not to be found
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This prequel to LOTR is visually stunning but mostly confusing. The long list of names and characters is nearly impossible to keep track of, making the story difficult to follow. The visual beauty keeps you watching, but it's hard to become truly immersed in the narrative. In a way, it's disrespectful to the creators to ignore the story. However, the real offense comes from the creators themselves, who insult me and every viewer by making this with so little vision. Peter Jackson proved (as we now see) that Tolkien's magnificent work could indeed be filmed, despite many considering any attempt to do so as an insult to the book. And anyone who reads The Silmarillion knows that creating a prequel is a hopeless task. That book is also a nearly incomprehensible collection of Tolkien's writings, which, in my opinion, were meant to make The Lord of the Rings more mysterious. These stories and writings support LOTR, but they are fragments, not a cohesive story. No, I believe the creators fail to capture the mystery and emotion of LOTR; in fact, they unintentionally try to explain it, which they utterly fail to do.

I've been a Tolkien fan for 40 years. Ever since I read Lord of the Rings as a 14 yr old. When this series was first announced I had big doubts. I love the history of the Second Age but it's open to m7ch interpretation and there's 3440 years of history so how can you adapt that much into a TV series? You can't now without a lot of editing of the timeline. This was my issue and is an issue for many fans. I had a similar problem with an adaption of Game of Thrones. Not with the timeline but with any adaption they have to change key events to fit in with a Tv adaption.So I was suspicious and found the first series frustrating because of the many changes and the vision of the show runners. For people who know the timeline it can be annoying to see characters and events moved over a thousand years through history. I enjoyed that first season but it also frustrated me.However. I'm used to it now and i am enjoying the second season very much. I think if I watched the first season again I'd enjoy it more. ipc-title__text: Terrible! Should never be a claimed extension to the epic LOTR series
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Terrible writer. No story to follow. Empty and boring. Nothing makes sense. No likable characters. It's a shame to have this linked to the epic LOTR series. I tried to engage myself and focus in the movie but there is nothing to follow. Like other reviews said, unfortunately a waste of huge money to create this fancy "looking" movie that has garbage value. If you want to make this right, hire the same people who created the original LOTR series and ask them to continue doing what they once did. Change is not always good! Also, having the actors to speak in a weird way like stressing on "rrrrr" does not make them speaking fancy or ancient.I would rather go watch the original LOTR over and over than wasting time on these aberrations.

I'll start with all of the positive elements about the show. It's difficult to capture the depth and world of Tolkien, and people underestimate how much history there is. This show does a neat job of taking some of the things that happened over time and condensing it, loosely. The thing that they screwed up on is casting, character development, which makes it hard to take serious. It's clear that they hired not on performance but they are guilty of "casting for culture" and in the process, they dropped the ball. A few things I wish they had done is made the characters more engaging and intriguing, made elves with long hair like they should have been, done a better job at casting, and overall the show lacks cohesiveness. I'm hoping that the new season is a massive upgrade from the first.

ipc-title__text: A slap in the face to Tolkein and Fans
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Galadriel, in Tolkien's works, was wise, kind, caring, and understanding. She was an accomplished mage, a talented leader, and a brilliant strategist.Yet, in this show, she is hot headed, angry, vengeful, and petty. She is prepared to lead those under her command to their deaths and abandon those who fall... and this Rings of Power Galadriel is meant to be thousands of years old at this point. And that's just one person, the whole show demonstrates a lack of understanding of Tolkien, disregards his lore which he held as nearly sacred, and the studio decries valid criticism of this as hate. Between the total rewriting of entire character arcs, such as those of Celebrimbor, to the overt changes in formerly grand places like Numinor, devolving a great empire into a petty, isolationist power... not to mention making the Harfoots, a hobbit stand-in they created, seem almost sociopathic with how ready thet are to abandon their own due to injury or fear... even ignoring the total and blatant disregard for the source material, Rings of Power fails to stand on its own, with a main character who is generally unlikeable and smug, a group (the Harfoots) who are terrible to their own and hateful of others, to confusing choices in pacing and writing overall.

ipc-title__text: Trash, refuse, garbage, filth, rubble, etc.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Sorry, I couldn't come up with additional synonyms in my title. How is it possible that creators/show runners are unable to learn from the past? Look, the reason why the Peter Jackson Lord of the Rings trilogy was a monumental success is the same reason why the rings of power (see what I did there with lowercase?) is a monumental failure. THE SOURCE MATERIAL!!! Peter Jackson was as true to Tolkien as much he knew how to be. The rings of power writers said to themselves, "I'll bet that we can do soooo much better than that old has been!" Poor, silly writers. Many have tried, none have succeeded, and you haven't done as well as most.

This season feels as if they took all the dullest parts of Lord of the Rings and strung them together. Remember that tedious season of The Walking Dead?Yep, similar experience.I pretty much blame the utter failure on Jackson and his unquenchable need to turn a simple two and a half hour film into far more than was necessary, right Hobbit?Sure Amazon wants to duplicate that success, except without any action to attract an audience.On the other hand the scenery and cinematography is magnificent. Overall the acting is fine with no miscasts.Hire better writers. Maybe grab someone from Deadpool or Doom Patrol.I noticed a serious, hahaha, lack of humor.No humor and no action how is that an appealing starting season.It even ruined my Skyrim experience.With any luck Amazon will realize that in season two instead of dumping tons of cash into a slow story, they should dump tons of cash into good writers.Cody Goodfellow is free as is Jasper Fforde.I imagine they would make wonderful tweaks to the scripts..

ipc-title__text: Best TV show have seen in a while
One Must Watch this epic Series
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I haven't ever written a review before but I love Tolkien's world and what he has created so thought I'd have my say.The first two episodes were far better than I had hoped for. They have made some assumptions regarding certain characters and plot and there are some inaccuracies but I don't mind any of that it's someone's interpretation of a fantasy world.I loved the dwarfs and the relationship Elrond has with them it felt very reminiscent of previous relationships shown in LOTRs, funny and heart warming and the subtle touch that it's only been 20 years to Elrond but Durin has lived a life in that time.The scenes are awe inspiring and so beautiful. The half feet have captured that same vibe as the hobbits and I think Lenny Henry is spot on.The dark undertones with Sauron and just having glimpses of him and not giving too much away really develops the tension and the fear.There is definitely a different take on the Elves then I have seen previously, more kind of mirkwood vibes where they seem to be quicker to emotions and therefore rash decision making. Again this just adds to the drama and the storytelling.So far it has really gripped me and I cannot wait for the next episode!

ipc-title__text: a beautiful tale, I absolutely love it
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This show was so visually satisfying and fun to watch. I did feel like at times it jumped all over the place, but we experienced the same thing in the movies.I don't really understand why the ratings are all over the place, but I honestly think it might be based in fragility around diversity. However, I think having a diverse cast added to the feeling of reality. We already had 6 movies where almost every character was a single race. It's high time we had more diverse casts in fantasy and other shows.I loved it, highly recommend, the main character has such a beautiful voice, and it's just a stunning show.

The expectations were high, but this show even did not manage to reach a average level of quality for any series. Miscast of actors, terrible dialogues, ridiculous scenes, a lot contradictions, inconsistent facts. Do you want an elve? Put pointed ears on a bad actor and let him say some simple words while pretending to be wise. Done. Sometimes it was so badly made, i even had to laugh out spontaneously. It is really sad. Tolkien's work offers material for hundreds of stories. But this show is consuming these like cheap fast food. I finished the season by fast forwarding 50% of the scenes. I badly hope there will be no second season.

ipc-title__text: You'll like it if you didn't read the books
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Shamefully, the only Tolkien book I ever read was the Hobbit, which I thoroughly enjoyed. I watched the Hobbit movies, and I thought they were just ok. Now, there is writing that is a little cringe worthy at times. However, for a piece of FICTION this is an incredibly satisfying and enjoyable story.would definitely recommend for any casual fan.

And takes viewers back to an era in which great powers were forged, kingdoms rose to glory and fell to ruin, unlikely heroes were tested, hope hung by the finest of threads and the greatest villain that ever flowed from Tolkien's pen threatened to cover all the world in darkness. Beginning in a time of relative peace, the series follows an ensemble cast of characters, both familiar and new, as they confront the long-feared reemergence of evil to Middle-earth. ipc-title__text: No one Can Beat Rings Of Power

ipc-html-content-inner-div: I approached season 2 with the hope that it had dealt with the major problems from season 1. I admit, I was hoping for a reboot to get this meandering and unentertaining series back on track. Sadly, developers J. D. Payne and Patrick McKay have doubled down on their flawed approach, which is to put all their effort into phonynvisuals while leaving the characters, storyline, and plot - the elements at the core of good entertainment - weak and uninteresting.Their problem is a failure of authenticity. Everything in this series feels contrived and inauthentic. The characters say LOTR-ish things, but they lack soul and originality. The conflicts are slow burn and too vague, like watching water boil. The vaunted visuals are so fake-looking they keep pulling viewers out of the fantasy action, distancing them from the story. The dark elements are so overdone, they give the entire series a dreary, drab, uninteresting feeling that is also off-putting, not exciting or thrilling at all. Even the rings themselves are so phony it feels like we're watching 'today's special value' on QVC.In the end, it's a tired old rehash of LOTR 'elements' that fails to rise above the fact that it is too dark, meandering, and boring - and stretched out far too long in order to justify its heafty price tag. It gives 'bloat for the sake of a series' energy, with ample time to consider this. I will be avoiding any future efforts from this team - life is too short.

ipc-title__text: It's not terrible but it's far from amazing

ipc-html-content-inner-div: As a fan of the original Lord of the Rings series, I was excited to hear about Amazon's Rings of Power. However, my excitement quickly turned into disappointment and frustration as I started watching the show. In my opinion, it is the worst show I have ever seen.First and foremost, the plot is convoluted and confusing. It's difficult to follow the storyline, and the characters lack depth and development. The show tries to introduce new characters and storylines that are not coherent with the original source material, which only serves to confuse and frustrate fans of the books and movies.The pacing of the show is incredibly slow, with long stretches of boring and uneventful scenes. The lack of action and suspense, which were hallmarks of the original series, is sorely missed. Instead, the show is filled with unnecessary and dragged-out subplots that add little to the overall story.The acting is subpar, with unconvincing performances from the cast. The dialogue feels forced and unnatural, and the chemistry between characters is virtually nonexistent. The show fails to capture the depth and complexity of the original characters, and the new characters lack charisma and interest.As a longtime fan of Tolkien, I was deeply disappointed with Amazon's Rings of Power. It fails to capture the magic and charm of the original stories, and the poor plot, pacing, acting make it an unwatchable mess. I do not recommend this show to anyone, especially to fans of the original series who are likely to be disappointed and let down. Save yourself the disappointment and skip this show altogether.

ipc-title__text: Rings of Power: no rings, but many flaws
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Ok, so we've all heard how flawed this series is. So as a big LOTR fan, after hearing all the negativity, not to mention all the liberties and changes to the canon and lore they did, I had my expectations set pretty low, but finally got around to seeing it.And what is my verdict? It was "meh". It certainly wasn't the horrible disaster that some people are saying, but it wasn't anywhere near great, and was ultimately, pretty forgettable. And for a billion dollar 8 episode LOTR series, that's a VERY bad thing. The LOTR fan-base is a big one, and to not only ignore what the fans were saying, but to dump on them and put out a mediocre series, Amazon really screwed up big time. But as I said, the series was just ok in my opinion.Excluding the change of canon and lore, there were a few main issues that really bothered me. One of the biggest ones was what was happening throughout it. While the imagery was beautifully done, there wasn't much all that great story-wise. For most of the series, nothing of much interest happens. Remember how in the Star Wars prequels one of the biggest complaints was that there was too much talking and politics. Yeah, we basically got that here too. And since there was nothing all that interesting going in, it leaves you feeling bored quite a bit, wondering when something will actually happen. But even when we do get some action scenes, they don't last long at all, and it's not all that great or entertaining to watch. In short, a lot of the series is boring, and that's a big problem.Another issue was the four different main stories going on. We had what was going on with Galadriel, Elrond, Arondir, and Nori and The Stranger, and it really doesn't work that well. Yes, the original LOTR trilogy had different stories with different characters, but they started out together before branching off, and their stories were still connected. Here, not so much. Most of the characters don't know each other, and they're each involved with their own pretty much unrelated story. This makes the series feel disjointed, and when the series switches over to one story, you kind of feel yourself wondering why, and are waiting for them to relate/connect to each other somehow. And when they do switch over, you're kind of like "Oh yeah, this is also going on". But like I said, these are pretty much separate stories that are barely connected at all, making it a little hard to get/stay invested. And also, for a series called Rings of Power, there are literally no rings in it, like at all. The rings don't even get hinted at until the last 20 minutes of the final episode.And now for, possibly, the biggest problem, and that's Galadriel. Don't get me wrong, Morfydd Clark did a good job for the role she was given, but they really botched up Galadriel's character. Yes, I get that this is supposed to be a younger version of her who's lacking the experiences that will make her the person we know she'll be in the future, but it doesn't feel remotely like her character. And worst of all, she's so unlikable. She's got this stuck-up, condescending, holier-than-though attitude, and she maintains it throughout the entire series. There's no real character growth or evolution, she stays the same obnoxious and unlikable person all throughout the series, and you just can't connect her to the Galadriel we know from LOTR and The Hobbit. Not to mention she's a super OP Mary Sue. How are people supposed to enjoy a series when its main character is so unlikable?But like I said, it's not as bad as some people are making it out to be, and it has some good qualities. I already mentioned the nice visual effects and landscapes, and it has certain story points that keep you interested in what will happen next. Unfortunately, it's overshadowed by being boring a lot due to so little happening and Galadriel being unlikable. And while the series wasn't bad, it was ultimately just ok and forgettable. If this was a completely original story/series, then maybe it would be a little better than what it was. But for being part of the LOTR franchise, there's really no excuse for it turning out as mediocre as it did. It's certainly not going to stand the test of time the way the movies did, and will just end up being another forgotten series that happened.In short, it wasn't bad, but it wasn't good either, and it's forgettable. But see it for yourself and decide. As for me, I'm giving it a 4/10 rating, and I consider a 5/10 to be average and a 3/10 to be unappealing.

ipc-title__text: Do not betray the history by underrating this show
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Reading the comments filled me with a deep sadness. I'm the kind of person who is usually indifferent to social interactions-the type who reads others' comments like a ghost, never leaving a trace of myself. But as a fan of Tolkien, reading the reviews for this series moved me to speak up. At the very least, I felt it was my duty to defend this remarkable series and encourage anyone who reads this to watch it, especially if they're a fan of Tolkien's world.In my view, much of the negative criticism stems from the strict adherence of Tolkien enthusiasts who may see any slight deviation from his writings as an unforgivable sin, allowing no creative liberties to the storyteller. This is similar to the kind of devotion some people have toward their religious texts. But what I saw was beauty-a sincere effort to uncover the scattered puzzle pieces of Tolkien's world, pieces that are reassembled with each scene, drawing you back to the core tales. The joy I felt watching this series was nearly as profound as that of experiencing the original trilogy. If I could, I would urge the creators to continue with future seasons.

ipc-title__text: Cancel this travesty. Tolkien's masterwork is being desecrated.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: "Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 2 is an utter disaster that somehow manages to sink even lower than the abysmal first season. It's a wandering mess that further desecrates Tolkien's masterpiece, proving once again that this show could never come close to touching the legacy of Peter Jackson's movie trilogy. Honestly, I've seen high school plays with better writing, acting, and general coherence.The costumes, supposed to add to the epic visual flair, look cheap and uninspired-hardly the high fantasy quality one would expect given Amazon's massive budget. It feels like they spent all their money on sweeping CGI landscapes while forgetting that believable attire plays a big role in storytelling.Then there's Galadriel. Once a character of grace, wisdom, and power, she has been completely reimagined as an insufferable "girl boss" who faces no accountability and receives zero character development. Her version here is far from the ethereal, deeply complex elf we loved in Tolkien's works or the movies. Instead, we get a relentless, arrogant warrior who bulldozes through the narrative without any genuine growth or nuance.The show's insistence on juggling far too many pointless side plots further dooms the pacing. The Harfoots are a prime example-characters who serve no real purpose other than to give the illusion of depth by stretching out the runtime. The duo that's clearly meant to echo Sam and Frodo is utterly forgettable, and the ongoing "mystery" of the "wannabe Gandalf" is just meaningless padding. The constant dangling of mysteries that have no stakes or emotional payoff is exhausting, and it's hard to imagine anyone truly caring.And don't get me started on how they absolutely destroyed Celebrimbor's character. Tolkien's Celebrimbor was a brilliant and tragic figure-this version is reduced to a naive, bumbling fool. After Galadriel realizes who Sauron is, nobody seems to think it's important to tell Celebrimbor, the one elf who *really* needs to know not to work with him. It's a bafflingly stupid plot point that makes the entire elven leadership look incompetent.Then there's the dialogue. Oh, the dialogue. The way they roll the 'R' in "Sauron" is painfully cringeworthy, an obvious and half-hearted attempt to make the speech sound sophisticated, but instead it comes off as forced and childish. It's as if the writers are trying too hard to convince us of the epicness that just isn't there. The result is terrible, juvenile dialogue that sounds like it was penned by talentless amateurs. Amazon, don't you have a principle that says "Insist on the Highest Standards"? How on earth is this show allowed to continue?More than anything else, this show is *boring*. It drags on and on, episode after episode, with uninspired dialogue, convoluted plots that go nowhere, and pacing that tests the limits of even the most patient viewer. The show doesn't just fail to capture the magic of Tolkien's world-it's actively ruining it for a new generation of potential fans.Amazon should do everyone a favor and cancel this travesty. It doesn't deserve the budget, the attention, or the loyalty of Tolkien fans. This feels like fan fiction gone wrong-completely lacking the depth, respect, or creativity required to bring Middle-earth to life.

ipc-title__text: Do NOT Listen To The Haters
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The Rings of Power is an extraordinary series, and those who criticize it do so based on four key reason.First: Some viewers may not fully grasp the history of Middle-earth. Season 1 is dedicated to world-building and character development, which may seem slow at times. However, this pacing is essential for laying the groundwork for future events. By understanding the characters' roles and the larger narrative being constructed, one can truly appreciate the series. The pay off for many of these characters will be well worth the wait.Second: Those familiar with the lore of Middle-earth and The Lord of the Rings often have preconceived notions of how the story should presented. This can make it challenging for them to accept an interpretation of the material that is different for their expectations. It's important to note that much of Tolkiens work was unfinished.Third: There's frustration over changes to Tolkien's works, but it's important to recognize that each modification for the show is approved by the Tolkien estate, which is deeply committed to preserving his legacy. Tolkien left much of his world open to exploration, providing others with the opportunity to build upon it.Fourth: Fans frequently compare this show to Peter Jackson's films, which limits creative appreciation. Every creator brings a distinct vision, and rather than comparing, it's more rewarding to approach each interpretation with an open mind and enjoy it for what it offers.The Rings of Power is AMAZING and should be appreciated. Don't miss out on it because of others.

ipc-title__text: Complete Waste of Time and Money
ipc-html-content-inner-div: There's a lot of things that can be said about Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power and unfortunately being good isn't one of them. I think the fundamental issue is the conception of this show doesn't work and the people running it are a bunch of incompetents who got the job through nepotism.In terms of positives I believe that the actors are giving decent enough performances, but they are weighed down by the mediocre writing and dialogue. Besides that the show looks expensive.As for criticisms the biggest has to be for the story and dialogue. When comparing this series to the Peter Jackson films which I know some people will say is unfair, but considering that this show rips off scenes directly from Peter Jackson and character designs that are not from the Books. I think that's a fair comparison to make. During the writing of the Films Peter Jackson had a Tolkien historian to help write the dialogue to make it more in line with Tolkien's work. The dialogue isn't just a way to communicate information to the audience. It's a way of developing character and giving a sense of the larger world they inhabit. Tolkien's Dialogue was so good that the films largely kept entire conversations the same from the books. Since for this show they're not adapting a specific story, But creating their own inside of a timeline. When they utterly fail to recreate that Tolkien-esque feel the characters come across as goofy and stilited. I feel the biggest problem with this story is that there's simply too many characters and too many plot lines that aren't relevant. I'll just say if you need to change so much lore and insert nonsensical character relationships while jumping through massive logic hoops to tell your story. Maybe you should have picked a different story to tell.Second biggest criticism I have for this show is the showrunners themselves . Considering that these two guys have never done anything of note and only got this job because of their friendship with JJ Abrams, it shouldn't be a surprise that they failed to deliver even one solid season of television. Because if you listen to the concept of this show A larger-than-life continent spanning adventure with multiple characters and battles. The problem is these guys have no experience in show running let alone on a project based on one or Fantasies greatest authors at a massive scale. So of course they're not going to be able to live up to that concept. If these two were competent they probably should have realized. Hey, we don't have the skills to do that so maybe we should pull back. Make the story smaller with fewer characters or just adapt a different book. Why not adapt Beren and Luthien or the Children of Hurin? There are other works that are pre-written narratives that could have been perfect for adaptation but instead they chose to make fanfiction. Terrible smelly fanfiction that assaults the senses of fans who love Tolkien and numbs the average viewer. Who is this show for exactly???The unfortunate reality is I don't see a way to save this show because the very concept of the forging of the rings of power is a footnote in a bigger story. Maybe it could have worked on its own But not in the hands of writers like these. Sadly, I have no interest in continuing with rings of power and frankly I don't see how anyone else could to.

6 episodes in and I decided to quit. This is not Tolkien aesthetics and atmosphere, far from it. There's really nothing in this production that is impressive. Acting is so so at best, except for the female protagonist, in fact, she holds the show together. The show lacks soul and looks clean, studio environment. Evil portrayed here is a joke. Anything but threatening. Battle scenes lack intensity and are not convincing.If anything is amazing about it, it's how such an expensive show falls short in delivering. Did the producers perhaps keep the money for themselves?Maybe ask Jackson, it appears he has a good grasp of the world of Tolkien.

Took a few episodes to hook me, but so worth it to see it through to the end. I'm I have now watched it twice and the second time around it was even more amazing. The acting becomes real and all the lead characters were enjoyable to watch. The imagery alone is beautiful and true to what you expect.
