ipc-title__text: A DARK STAIN FOR MIDDLE EARTH
ipc-html-content-inner-div: There are so many things to criticize, dozens of things are written for just 1 episode, elves that are not elves, a scenario that does not have a sense of time, producing a fake scenario instead of shooting the work of the world's best fantasy fiction writer as a documentary. Bombadil, unrelated to Tom Bombadil. Gandalf, who did not exist in the 2nd age. No matter how you take it, there is a disgrace left in your hands. So, you even made us grateful for the Hobbit movie series. I hope it gets cancelled. It would be an insult to Tolkien to continue this disgrace for another season.Azog returning from the dead and the absurd humor scenes in the Hobbit trilogy seem so innocent compared to this...Peter Jackson is enjoying watching the TV series while sipping whiskey at home.

Where should I start?As a loyal fan of Tolkien saga, and having read all his books, I was looking forward to watch this show.I understand that LOTR was sublime and memorable. But we should not be comparing shows on a regular basis, this is a different time in Tolkiens world, different story, told from dif characters and angles.The cinematography is excellent, the locations so whimsical, and the acting is top notch. And the soundtrack is exquisite, the music moves with the story, that orchestra is unreal.Makeup, wardrobe all so well done, and each detail crafted so preciously.I love this show. Dont miss it!!!

Season 1 had me death scrolling through my phone and wondering when something might happen.Season 2 is so bad I burst out laughing uncontrollably at random moments in every episode. It's so tedious it's funny.There's just nothing appealing about any of the characters. They're more wooden than the talking trees!I'm struggling to remain focused on the storyline and I like this kind of shit!I guess they thought we'd make do and be overwhelmed by the mountains and CGI looking landscapes and worlds they've created and forget the need to engage with actual humanity, even if it is a tree.I'm going to soldier on to the end but I wouldn't recommend anyone else do the same.

This is very selfish and disrespectful to the original source. Not only does the result not correspond to anything remotely close to the Tolkien world, but it does not even try to pretend to care about it. I'll never understand why anyone should have defiled something beautiful. The authors have no rights to anything related to the age listed in the series (not counting the appendix with names, honestly, they could have made up their own names and no one would have noticed). It is pity, because stories of Simallirion are something millions of people would like to see and now Sauron has reason to laugh. The strangest question is: where did all this money go?

This serie has nothing in common with the works of Tolkien, the play the script everything has nothing to do with Tolkien and the acting is horrible a total lacj of respect for Tolkien and the actors who play in this serie. It would be better is some people who a little bit understand tolkien an read a book about it would be in play to help out this epic dissaster. For now i dont think it is possible to resolve this dissaster. Maybe the Valar will help the screenwriters al little bit and maybe Eru himself will watch at this horrible series and strike the actors and everybody on the set with some sense.

ipc-title__text: The Rings of Power Strays from Tolkien's Vision
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I watched The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power and, unfortunately, it fell short of my expectations. The series diverges significantly from Tolkien's original work, introducing characters and plotlines that were never part of the established lore. This departure from the source material felt like a disservice to the intricate world Tolkien meticulously crafted. The newly invented characters often seemed unnecessary and disconnected, failing to capture the essence of the story. As a devoted fan of the books, I found this adaptation to be a disappointing and unfaithful representation of Tolkien's legacy.

Lush costumes, elaborate sets, earnest performances, high resolution special effects, interesting cast. I hesitated initially but once I took the plunge I was hooked.Haven't read any Tolkien books. Have only seen Peter Jackson's most excellent Lord Of The Rings trilogy. Knowing that trilogy, I can see where this series is headed.The reservations I have about this series are the same I have for all non-limited series, of which there is an abundance like never before.First problem - I already know how things turn out. As exciting as many of these set-pieces are, at the end of the day there's no real risk because I'll always know the ending before it occurs, more or less. This dampens the drama & excitement.Second problem - the show could get canceled at any time. We've all seen it happen. I mean, I've heard this show is friggin expensive to make (it shows on screen). Surely it's forever on a knife edge for its survival. The moment the ratings drop questions will arise over its viability. Although, they could always reduce the production values to match declining viewership.In all, this doomsayer was swept away by the magic of it all, notwithstanding aforementioned caveats.

ipc-title__text: Actaully not as bad as Tolkien Purist made it out to be
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Just watched the series after ignoring the series due to so many disappointing reviews. Finally forced myself to watch it and was pleasantly surprised.The series is nowhere as bad as some die-hard Tolkien fans made it out to be.It definitely is nowhere near as good the LORT movies - but really, who thought they would be?The movies are close as perfection as a movie could be - even then PJ altered the narrative for his own purposes.The acting was generally good - especially the dwarves and Harfoots. Loved seeing Khazadum before its decline. Loved seeing Numenor, loved the mystery surrounding the stranger (Gandalf) - loved his relationship with the Harfoots - beautifully explains Gandalf's soft spot for the future Hobbits.Some said the Series was too slow - I disagree, I even liked Galadriel's character - I can understand her drive and frustration considering the attitude of all other elves regarding the pending doom.If you have avoided watching it due to bad reviews - I would definitely give a go - with low expections - you will be pleasantly surprised. Looking forward to the second series.

I had very low expectations to begin with, having followed the development and marketing before it came out.Somehow they managed to do even worse. A couple of decent visuals, which is the least they could do with the budget they had, but other than that it has no redeemable qualities.If I take into account that this is not a parody or a B-level production, it had to be literally the worst writing I ever saw in my entire life. The lack of worldbuilding, basic storytelling, any even remotely complex and well thought of character is astounding. Hard to believe 'professionals' were paid for this, but can't say it wasn't expected.

It is clean, you can sit with ease and watch it, no vulgarity, nudity or such language. Also the visuals and Galadriel's and Arondir's action is quiet brilliant, I loved casting and acting too, I am truly looking forward for the second season, although there are a few things different from the original story but I can not say much until I watch the second season, which I hope will happen, and yeah, the location and everything even if it was all CGI I loved it because it was mind freshening. Waiting to see more of Galadriel's fighting, honestly I can not wait anymore, but if you are watching it only in sense of judging then you should not watch.

I admire their dedication to Tolkien's emphasis on the romance of friendship rather than sexual tension. Despite the opportunity for the romantic tropes taken advantage in most other franchises, they maintained the allure of modern characters as well as adding fresh love of humanity through new female characters (who always pass the bechdel test may I say haha) and new characters of color.Although romance is present, it holds a deep warmth and is not easily taken for granted as the main player as so many other shows do when they are trying to make something cheaply entertaining. Instead, it is presented with fondness, trust, and deep passion, not fleeting glances and first kisses, but deep true bonds. The same is true of friendship. There is nothing lacking in how they present the means of brotherhood and bondage to one another through oath of both word and presence.Despite the modern plot devices that are not always perfect, there is still a deep sense of continued world building that is extremely impressive given the quantity and quality of the material available. These characters and this world that have so long belonged to Tolkein, are preserved through the imagination and true creation of those who care most deeply for them and all of Tolkien's work.

Bad writing, bad script, bad direction, mediocre acting, cheap-looking sets and costumes. Where did the millions of dollars go to?Even if viewed only as fan fiction because it's not even respectful of the established lore of the biggest fantasy world in literature, it's still bad and boring to watch.I really wanted to like this series and even waited until September to re-subscribe to Amazon's Prime Video for this even though I was jonesing to watch The Boys' latest season when it came out.Honestly, the first 2 episodes are snooze fests that I literally fell asleep watching both and I had to rewind multiple times just to finish the 2. Then episode 3 wasn't much better, but I still kept hope that this series would get better. By the time I got to episode 4, I lost hope and finally accepted that this is a poorly-written series and the show runners need to go back to the drawing board and not release a 2nd season but rather find something else to do with the IP, maybe something that is more lore-accurate because Tolkien did not create this wonderful fantasy universe just for some hack writers to mess with and change to their liking. Drop the hubris and respect the genius that is J. R. R. Tolkien.

ipc-title__text: From here, reboot is the only option.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Since I am fearful that my dedication and hard work that I usually put into writing proper reviews will be dismissed and deleted in this case, I will keep this review shorter and lacking on details.For starters to understand where I am coming from and the way I judge the product : I am huge Tolkien fan, I have read the books and I have seen the films and have spent countless hours refining my knowledge of the mythology and world that the author has built. Since I am keenly aware of the stories of the second age and have the knowledge of what was changed and what was the potential of the source material I can judge this TV show on those parameters.Usually I don't rush to give low scores to films, since films have a lot of different aspects that built up the final product whether it is the work of the CGI department of the practical effects, or whether it is the actors and how they carry the script or the writers which write it ... plenty to judge a film by.There is no doubt a lot of effort was put into certain aspects (not only money) of the film whether its the landscape building or the visuals of the great city of Numenor, however there are plenty of evidence of cheap work put into the title that is unexpected out of an expansive project such as this, seen as the low quality of armor and more. Despite all that surely the show stands overall on a rather high ground in that regard, however since the other aspects of the show are really lacking the score drops significantly, between the bad acting and the horrible screen writing the show can't get much points and in fact get detracted points for that aspect of the show - mostly because not only the writing is bad but also its actively harm the source material the show is built upon.I had seen the show from the first episode to the last for the hopes of seeing Tolkien's world once again revived, not only I have not seen it but I have seen it degraded and butchered to the point that it doesn't not resemble the author's world. The only way to fix it which I will be glad to hope on in case it will be fixed in that manner , is to reboot the show and replace actors, writers showrunner and directors alike.There is plenty of talented people out there who laid out beautiful and faithful foundations for a show for free on youtube, I would highly recommended finding the right ones and drawing inspiration from them. The story of Numenor the faithful and the King's men, the line of Isiludor, the massive colonies in middle earth, the wars with Sauron and the perspective of the elven realms under the guidance of Gil Galad - all of those give plenty of priceless material to work with I suggest adapting it instead of making a new.The show as it stands is irredeemable - nothing will get me to recommend it or pay to watch another season of it. Big studies put a lot into reboots for the past decade - here is your opportunity to jump on this trend but actually for the better and not for the worst.Good luck rebooting and adapting the source material faithfully !

ipc-title__text: Great if not perfect, I'm satisfied
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I'm a Tolkien fan and I loved it. The show isn't perfect. Has pacing and writing issues. But the score and visuals are mind blowing. Great casting and acting by most actors. I can't believe I have to wait till 2024.I don't mind the differences from the book. Middle earth is a very complex universe and it's impossible to adapt everything word by word. I enjoy the original characters as well as a new look at the old ones.The show runners and cast need to ignore all the negative backlash take only sane experts advise about how to improve writing and pacing. The show has a lot of potential and I'm sure season 2 is going to be even more awesome. I can't stop listening to the music. It's one of the best soundtracks I have listened to in years.

This show is a visual treat. There was a lot of investment in graphics/animation, backdrops, photography etc. And it clears shines here.The story telling, however, is a plain bad. Random events happen in different parts of the world in each episode. They do not come together to form a cohesive story though. This makes the audience to tune out.It is surprising that someone thought - riding on the back of a popular series with cool graphics is a success recipe without investment in story writing. This first season will go down as a failed attempt even when the huge budget was spend on production.

I adore just about anything from Tolkiens middle earth. And I have hoped beyond hope that fans of his work would one day get more from that world. THE RINGS OF POWER delivered that. I love the deep dive into Galadriels back story, which makes her much so more relatable and likable than in the original films. I am also enjoying all the new characters, the harfoots especially. And I don't mind that the creators took liberty in the casting or character creation. The characters they created, add to the story, and fill in gaps that would have been difficult to tell without the full license to use Tolkiens written work as a source.

ipc-title__text: Why did they even bother to make it?
A good show that I hope develops into a great one
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The writers and/or Amazon are fairly risk adverse; the show is too closely modelled on early Game of Thrones and they feel the need inject all the major elements from LOTR proper for the more causal fans. (i.e., the balrog, the likely identity of the stranger). This often leads to basic plotting and characterization. The storyline engages but it is a bit rote. I also think the writers could have stuck closer to Tolkien's intent but they clearly prioritized linking up to the Jackson's films. And I think the show *does* do that well. The show on the page is merely competent as a piece of fantasy. I hope they bring in some new writers in the future to punch up the script. That said the big reveal of where Sauron was really worked for me.The show ends up being better than its scripts because pretty much every other aspect of filmmaking is so good. The production values are great and the direction is strong enough to transport the viewer into Middle Earth. I really like the cast-I especially like the blokes who play Elrond and Durin IV. It is a shame that bunch of reactionaries have drowned out sincere criticism because of the cast.I will be watching the second season. I hope the writers take more risks.

ipc-title__text: A Laudable Return To Middle Earth
ipc-html-content-inner-div: There are some fairly fierce criticisms of the show on here so I thought I'd balance it out a little: I thoroughly enjoyed it! Granted, the first few episodes are a little slow but I was so pleased to be back in Middle Earth that I didn't mind, and it picked up brilliantly in the back half of the series, particularly episodes 6 and 8.Not every performance worked in terms of style but on the whole I was more than satisfied and had grown fond of many of the characters. I cared about their relationships, mother to son, Elf to Dwarf and human, even Uruk to Orc in a weird fashion - the chap playing Adar was excellent, sadness and horror intertwined in the best Middle Earth idiom.It looked gorgeous, and one would expect that with the money spent (although that is far from a given), but I was also impressed with the material used. It didn't feel heavy-handed, allowing the story to flow without sledgehammer references to the LOTR films as the pretty horrible Hobbit films did - this is much better than those.All in all, a great effort. Not outstanding but a hugely promising beginning. Bring on the second series.

This is such a great series. It has been made really brilliant and it is stunning to watch. It is a must have for everyone with a fantastic sense of this kind of genres. I am also really interested in how it has been made O.o
I hope for everyone of us that a second season will be launched as soon as possible so we can dive deeper into the world of middle earth. The best is that we have never read or watched enough about our loved fantasy worlds.

Watching this series made me feel I could have written and directed it myself. But I wouldn't, because I have respect for the brilliance of the universe and wouldn't want my lack of talent and experience to ruin the opportunity for someone else to actually do a great job. I would have said no.Admittedly there were a few good moments. But the dialogue was mostly completely off and the storyline jumped from too fast in some areas to painfully slow in others.If you reframe it as an amateur theatre comedy taking place in a beautiful computer game universe with awkward references to the lord of the rings, it goes down easier.

So far this 1st season is just poorly written. The dialogue lacks depth and doesn't make a lot of sense. I often find myself asking, 'wait, what just happened?' The story seems to change direction randomly and it doesn't seem intentional. Almost as if they were writing as they went along and realized, oops! That didn't work. Let's try this instead. Lots of dead ends which leave me wondering why they did it in the first place.Regarding the costumes and make up, the actors and actresses look more like they belong in an expensive children's play rather than a nearly 1 billion dollar series. Over processed hair, too much stage make up, gaudy outfits, etc. The wardrobes seem to focus on showing off and accentuating bodily features of the women rather than being functional. For example: Bronwyn is wearing a loose racerback apron-style dress (that's just a hint too low in the front) while there is snow on the ground. She looks freezing. Long sleeves underneath would've made much more sense. The Numenor outfits look like Halloween costumes inspired by Byzantium. Eärien's pleated dress looks like a maternity gown, but it accentuates her bust so it's obvious why they chose that style. And the Harfoots, the most endearing characters so far, look like they raided Michaels and Joann Fabrics for their synthetic leaf and plastic acorn hair ensembles. I imagine lots of hot glue was used. Using natural foliage and less hair wax would've created a more realistic hobbit.Oh and then there's Galadriel... she is anything but likable. In fact I found myself rooting for the dark forces over her. Her character is demanding, arrogant, and irrational revenge seeker. She seems like she's in a constant state of irritability. Frankly she's tiresome and I can't imagine how she becomes the Galadriel portrayed by Peter Jackson.I have other grievances with this series, but since it's still the 1st season I will wait and hope it improves... overall it doesn't live up to the hype.

I want to know where all the money went. Everything in this show is like that low tier direct to VHS movies you found on TV on Sunday but with nice backgrounds, and it manages some times to be worse.You feel in every scene the difference in transition between the CGI filled backgrounds where there are open spaces, thousands of people, etc... and the live action scenes with claustrophobic scenery recycled from episode to episode and a handful of people.The plot is embarrassing, the acting is atrocious, the dialogues are so pompous that seems like all where made for the trailer so they could simply randomly choose between them.A disgrace.

A butchery of Tolkien's work. This atrocity is not even loosely based on anything Tolkien wrote regarding the second age. Why would you buy the rights to LotR, appendices, and the Hobbit to make a show on the second age? Might it be more useful to obtain the rights to books like the Silmarillion?Worse, nothing happens in this show. The writing is terrible and goes nowhere. There are more Amazon created characters and side plots than any of characters we want to see. Characters that should be present, thinking of you Celeborn, aren't and the characters that are present are made into complete buffoons or are completely repulsive.I was cautiously optimistic that maybe this could be good until I saw Amazon's adaption of Wheel of Time. At that point, I was almost positive they were about to trash Tolkien in the same way. How can you spend this much money on a show and have it come out as such garbage? The fans will literally tell you what they want to see, but you somehow take a 180 and head the opposite direction.

People that knock this series are people that will never be happy with anything in life
This is actually pretty great. Galadriel is a total bad a**
The characters and the relationship building between them is outstanding and the brewing orc war is coming.So much good stuff is happening its hard to understand why people are down on this. My only disappointment so far is that it's only 9 episodes.But I guess with movie quality episodes each week it would be hard to ask for more. I really cannot wait until the next episode. Each week makes me want more and more. Next week is middle earth, I'm so excited about that.

I have to say that Amazon pleasantly surprised me. The first episode introduces us well to Middle-earth, introduces the characters and outlines the threat. And no matter what anyone wants to say, he manages it well. So far, the main driving force of the series is Nory, who is inquisitive, childish and a bit naive. Close behind are the young Elerond and Galadriel, where she in particular arouses embarrassed reactions with her arrogance. Personally, I think it's intentional. After all, we are in the second age.........thousands of years before the events of The Hobbit and LOTRA. In the Silimarillion it is written that Galadriel participated in many battles and I suspect that she has yet to learn many things here as well. However, what struck me the most is the world in which the series takes place. I read a few comments where it was written that the tricks are weak. I ask...where? The visual is breathtaking. In this direction, Rings of Power has no competition, and anyone who doesn't see it is blind. Another plus is that the world is alive, something is happening, being built or outlined everywhere. And now to the problems. Rings of Power has had Mastermind lore since its announcement. This is partly to blame for Amazon itself and partly to blame for the viewers. In my opinion, they prepared their comments in advance just purely for the heist. And that's not fair. I'm not saying it's a perfect series. For 1) There are currently 3 episodes out and for 2) Nothing is perfect. But the fact that someone is not able to read Silimarilion (while learning that the second age is not so well mapped and everything is traced through the appendices) and solves things that could easily be guessed and then criticize it is downright embarrassing. And the climax is when Tolkien is indirectly called a racist. The series should not be evaluated in advance, let alone watch it with self-denial.

ipc-title__text: LOTR is a hard fantasy to live up to.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I've watched up to episode 3. This show unfortunately I feel like fails to live up to the scale, the unique character development, and the epic conflict between good and evil as shown in the original Peter Jackson trilogy.The characters are somewhat interesting but not as engaging as those in the fellowship of the ring. I feel like I'm not very interested in the characters; compared to GoT House of Dragon for example where I care more.There is this unseen force of evil, but the show doesn't present the conflict in a way that feels to me very engaging or at an epic scale or challenge like the original trilogy. This is okay but problem is combined with other aspects leaves the show less engaging. I think the problem lies with this powerful elf already searching for this evil to begin with, so it's like there's not much to go from beyond that.The Hobbit trilogy was also probably better- the one problem with that trilogy was it was just too long for the material.Finally, the show doesn't really feel that much like Lord of the Rings but more-so a generic fantasy. I would say insofar the orcs/goblins are the only thing that feels like LOTR because they are as simple, cruel, threatening, animalistic as before and depicted well so far in that way. The elves meanwhile seem too much like humans.

ipc-title__text: Not as bad as expected but that's not saying much
ipc-html-content-inner-div:
I'm a Tolkien fan and so right out of the gate I was forewarned. I did decide to give it a chance anyway, even a little bit of Middle Earth is better than none, right? Wrong, after three episodes I think I'm done.The worst slap at Tolkien in this is the portrayal of the Elven race. Sticking pointing ears on a character does not make them an elf. Elves are the badasses of Middle Earth, these Elves, with the exception of "Galadriel" of course, are somewhat bumbling and not at all regal or intimidating. They're not elves.Meanwhile, they try to make fake Galadriel so badass that she just comes off as unlikable and annoying. Really unlikable and very annoying.And I'm not sure why the Hobbits have been turned into homeless people who apparently don't bath and wear rags...I keep waiting for them to roll into a village and start panhandling.But you know what, I knew this wasn't going to be LOTR's coming in, I knew the writers here wouldn't know Tolkien if they tripped over him, so I may have been able to overlook that. But what can't be overlooked is bad acting, bad writing....very bad writing, bad pacing, unlikable characters, all of them, and a bad story.Prior to release they made a big deal out of the first female dwarf to appear in a Rings story, she wasn't but hey, let's not quibble over something as pesky as facts. What they didn't warn anyone about was how absolutely terrible the actress in the role was, forget gender or race, she's just a horrible actress. So is the woman playing fake Galadriel for that matter. And if you're going to cast an actress to play an imposing badass perhaps you should find someone a little more physically imposing, someone who isn't shorter than most twelve year old children. Just a though....
What a waste or a great opportunity, and a boatload of money!

ipc-title__text: Pretty, but boring with poor character development.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Slow pacing doesn't have to mean a show is boring, however in the case of RoP, it is very boring, has poor character development and I have no interest in any of the protagonists.The show could have really done with more experienced showrunners and writers. When set pieces do occur, they are very cheesey and poorly executed (alley fight anyone?). Some scenes are very pretty, and Khazad-dûm was pretty cool, but that's about it.With the LoTR part of the story was that heroes, braverly and courage can come from the most unlikely places, but RoP seems to miss that nuance and instead goes for the low hanging fruit of trying to make protagonists look as cool as possible (the original trilogy had that problem with Legolas)There is a possibility the show can improve, but so far it has been woeful.

I really enjoyed Peter Jackson's interpretation of LOTR, but it failed to fully capture my own understanding of Tolkien's work. Peter Jackson focused on the horror of the story and missed much of the humour Tolkien offered in the dialogue and interactions between characters.I was dreading the release of this series from Amazon, but have been pleasantly surprised. It's visually stunning and they have faithfully captured the atmosphere of Middle Earth, offering compelling characters with humour and dignity. This is really one for the hardcore Tolkien fans... It lacks the funfair and bloody drama of shows like GoT, so anyone who comes to Middle Earth with only Peter Jackson's interpretation to guide them may be disappointed with the slower pace.

Dreadfully boring though. I was shocked by how boring it was. I don't know if it was the Batgirl level acting or writing but getting through that first episode was a chore. I had to take a break for a few days before I started the second episode. It wasn't any better. I didn't help that I watched House of the Dragon in between. Now that's fantasy done right. They really should have added some established actors, and people that have written fantasy before. It doesn't help that no one involved is an actual fan of Tolkien. They actually fired the guy that was and it shows. If they wanted to tell their own story why not create a new one from the ground up instead of wearing the skin of an established one? Bummer because I really wanted to like this.

ipc-title__text: The lost art of story telling
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Visually impressive but that's not enough. The writing is simply not at the standard required, the plot is not driven forward by events but rather gets lost in inane subplots and cringey dialogue.The dialogue reads like a B grade GCSE students attempt at drama, and as a results every conversation has a soap opera feel to it. Who thought "knife ears" was a tolkien-esq slur?? Talking of which the writers have some weird obsession with elf ears - these are not a defining characteristics of Tolkien's elves! Tolkien's elves are ethereal, graceful yet powerful - these elves are just another fantasy deviation of human, or human-like, they completely misunderstood Tolkien in this aspect... and indeed every aspect. The original characters aren't original, and they certainly aren't relatable or likeable. Are we supposed to feel sorry for the elf who received the aforementioned slur? It feels like the show is desperate for us to sympathise and we don't.Unfortunately this series is already doomed, if they can get new writers and a stronger cast for season 2 then it might be worth a second look.The soundtrack and visuals are good but it is the STORY that matters and the art of story telling is well and truly lost.

Let's set aside the fact that this isn't Tolkien in any way and the cringe worthy wokeism they're pushing.This show is so uneven. It's not entirely bad 'cause there is a few highlights but mostly it doesn't really catch my interest. The dialogue is bland, the acting less than believable and things like Galadriel the superhero makes it just... dull.I mean, an icetroll takes out 5-6, what I gather is, seasoned elf warriors and Galadriel attacks it, all by herself, and kills it? Did those elf warriors just suck at their job? Why wasn't it a hard fight, where everyone had to do their part, and where Galadriel delt the killing blow making it a real fight while lifting her up to being a real leader AND a hardcore fighter? And how come they're fighting against the ice cold winds in one second while moving around quite unbothered by it the next? It's just bad... I truly feel sorry for the actress playing Galadriel 'cause she's being portraid as a really unlikable person with no leader skills and a serious problem with everything around her.I could've continued watching this series even though it's not Tolkien at all, and I still might, but I'll probably binge it some time when I'm really bored and there's nothing else to watch. I won't be one of those eagerly waiting for the next episode.

ipc-title__text: Big budget and fancy VFX are not gonna cut it
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I will assume I am speaking for every true LOTR fan. This show has failed spectacularly at simply being part of the LOTR universe.That means the creators of the show's notion of the LOTR universe is fancy language (came out artificial), VFX (almost cartoonish). That's an insult to every fan of the franchise!I wasn't very disappointed after all for I have sensed the poor craftsmanship as their trailer wreaked of nothing but taking pride in their riches and grandeur. True fellowship of the franchise shall elude despair should they take to the movies and pretend as the show is not akin to their beloved.

ipc-title__text: Great start to a promising series
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I love the first couple of episodes. It's setting up for a long run story line but I knew that coming into it. I'm hooked. The visuals are stunning. It carries the same awe factor that the movies did. I can't wait for more.The storyline may not be action-packed but it does build a good up some suspense and excitement for what's next. The characters are all well cast also. My friends and I are trying to decide who we think the stranger is. I'm going to have to brush up on my middle earth history and lore.The scenery is breathtaking. They have gorgeous panoramic shots that give you a sense of just how vast middle earth is.

I find "Rings of Power" incredibly frustrating. The inconsistent and terrible writing is evident in the dialogue, which often feels shallow and fails to capture the richness of the source material. Plot points are delivered in a way that feels patronizing, as if the creators assume the audience can't engage critically with the story.The pacing is poor, with some storylines rushing through important events while others drag on without purpose. This creates a disjointed viewing experience where it's hard to stay invested in what's happening. It often feels like the series is trying to cram too much into each episode without giving any single plot line the time it needs to develop.Character development is disappointing, with many characters feeling one-dimensional. Their arcs lack depth, making it difficult to form emotional connections. Instead of exploring rich backstories, we get stereotypes that don't evolve.The acting adds to this frustration. I feel like I'm developing muscle fatigue seeing the main characters use the same close-up facial expression for every situation. This repetitiveness detracts from the performances and makes it harder to engage with their emotional journeys. Overall, these issues contribute to a viewing experience that feels unsatisfying and uninspired.

ipc-title__text: Excellent addition to the LOTR cannon!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I was tempted to give this 10/10 to offset all the people moaning, but actually I'd say it's a 7.5.For me I don't particularly mind when liberties are taken with a text - when you change medium, it's inevitable. I'm probably a fairly casual Tolkien fan but I have read Silmarillion etc in the past.Getting to see characters i'd previously only read about was cool. Seeing origin stories play out was wonderful. I think if you're the type of person that can hold all the books and movies in your mind, and cross compare, you will likely find something to be disappointed about.Personally I loved the trilogy but was nonplussed by The Hobbit, this for me sits between those, occasionally reaching the heights of LOTR but never sinking into the lows of The Hobbit.Loved it and can't wait for S3!

This is such a great series. It has been made really brilliant and it is stunning to watch. It is a must have for everyone with a fantastic sense of this kind of genres. I am also really interested in how it has been made O.o

Watching this series made me feel I could have written and directed it myself. But I wouldn't, because I have respect for the brilliance of the universe and wouldn't want my lack of talent and experience to ruin the opportunity for someone else to actually do a great job. I would have said no.Admittedly there were a few good moments. But the dialogue was mostly completely off and the storyline jumped from too fast in some areas to painfully slow in others.If you reframe it as an amateur theatre comedy taking place in a beautiful computer game universe with awkward references to the lord of the rings, it goes down easier.

So far this 1st season is just poorly written. The dialogue lacks depth and doesn't make a lot of sense. I often find myself asking, 'wait, what just happened?' The story seems to change direction randomly and it doesn't seem intentional. Almost as if they were writing as they went along and realized, oops! That didn't work. Let's try this instead. Lots of dead ends which leave me wondering why they did it in the first place.Regarding the costumes and make up, the actors and actresses look more like they belong in an expensive children's play rather than a nearly 1 billion dollar series. Over processed hair, too much stage make up, gaudy outfits, etc. The wardrobes seem to focus on showing off and accentuating bodily features of the women rather than being functional. For example: Bronwyn is wearing a loose racerback apron-style dress (that's just a hint too low in the front) while there is snow on the ground. She looks freezing. Long sleeves underneath would've made much more sense. The Numenor outfits look like Halloween costumes inspired by Byzantium. Eärien's pleated dress looks like a maternity gown, but it accentuates her bust so it's obvious why they chose that style. And the Harfoots, the most endearing characters so far, look like they raided Michaels and Joann Fabrics for their synthetic leaf and plastic acorn hair ensembles. I imagine lots of hot glue was used. Using natural foliage and less hair wax would've created a more realistic hobbit.Oh and then there's Galadriel... she is anything but likable. In fact I found myself rooting for the dark forces over her. Her character is demanding, arrogant, and irrational revenge seeker. She seems like she's in a constant state of irritability. Frankly she's tiresome and I can't imagine how she becomes the Galadriel portrayed by Peter Jackson.I have other grievances with this series, but since it's still the 1st season I will wait and hope it improves... overall it doesn't live up to the hype.

After all, we are in the second age.........thousands of years before the events of The Hobbit and LOTRA. In the Silimarillion it is written that Galadriel participated in many battles and I suspect that she has yet to learn many things here as well. In this direction, Rings of Power has no competition, and anyone who doesn't see it is blind. Another plus is that the world is alive, something is happening, being built or outlined everywhere. ipc-title__text: LOTR is a hard fantasy to live up to.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I've watched up to episode 3. This show unfortunately I feel like fails to live up to the scale, the unique character development, and the epic conflict between good and evil as shown in the original Peter Jackson trilogy.The characters are somewhat interesting but not as engaging as those in the fellowship of the ring. I feel like I'm not very interested in the characters; compared to GoT House of Dragon for example where I care more.There is this unseen force of evil, but the show doesn't present the conflict in a way that feels to me very engaging or at an epic scale or challenge like the original trilogy. This is okay but problem is combined with other aspects leaves the show less engaging. I think the problem lies with this powerful elf already searching for this evil to begin with, so it's like there's not much to go from beyond that.The Hobbit trilogy was also probably better- the one problem with that trilogy was it was just too long for the material.Finally, the show doesn't really feel that much like Lord of the Rings but more-so a generic fantasy. I would say insofar the orcs/goblins are the only thing that feels like LOTR because they are as simple, cruel, threatening, animalistic as before and depicted well so far in that way. The elves meanwhile seem too much like humans.

ipc-title__text: Not as bad as expected but that's not saying much

Elves are the badasses of Middle Earth, these Elves, with the exception of "Galadriel" of course, are somewhat bumbling and not at all regal or intimidating. They're not elves.Meanwhile, they try to make fake Galadriel so badass that she just comes off as unlikable and annoying. Really unlikable and very annoying.And I'm not sure why the Hobbits have been turned into homeless people who apparently don't bath and wear rags...I keep waiting for them to roll into a village and start panhandling.But you know what, I knew this wasn't going to be LOTR's coming in, I knew the writers here wouldn't know Tolkien if they tripped over him, so I may have been able to overlook that. But what can't be overlooked is bad acting, bad writing....very bad writing, bad pacing, unlikable characters, all of them, and a bad story.Prior to release they made a big deal out of the first female dwarf to appear in a Rings story, she wasn't but hey, let's not quibble over something as pesky as facts. What they didn't warn anyone about was how absolutely terrible the actress in the role was, forget gender or race, she's just a horrible actress. So is the woman playing fake Galadriel for that matter. And if you're going to cast an actress to play an imposing badass perhaps you should find someone a little more physically imposing, someone who isn't shorter than most twelve year old children. Just a though....
What a waste or a great opportunity, and a boatload of money!

ipc-title__text: The lost art of story telling
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Visually impressive but that's not enough. The writing is simply not at the standard required, the plot is not driven forward by events but rather gets lost in inane subplots and cringey dialogue.The dialogue reads like a B grade GCSE students attempt at drama, and as a results every conversation has a soap opera feel to it. Who thought "knife ears" was a tolkien-esq slur?? Talking of which the writers have some weird obsession with elf ears - these are not a defining characteristics of Tolkien's elves! Tolkien's elves are ethereal, graceful yet powerful - these elves are just another fantasy deviation of human, or human-like, they completely misunderstood Tolkien in this aspect... and indeed every aspect. The original characters aren't original, and they certainly aren't relatable or likeable. Are we supposed to feel sorry for the elf who received the aforementioned slur? It feels like the show is desperate for us to sympathise and we don't.Unfortunately this series is already doomed, if they can get new writers and a stronger cast for season 2 then it might be worth a second look.The soundtrack and visuals are good but it is the STORY that matters and the art of story telling is well and truly lost.

ipc-title__text: Great non-canon adaptation of Lord of the Rings
ipc-html-content-inner-div: First I'm going to start off by saying that literally no one else is making an original story based on the beginning of the story, Peter Jackson is too busy working on his Gollum trilogy which is going to be the next epic all the hardcore edgelords can gossip about. This is a tv show. There is supposed to be inconsistencies. I remember Peter Jackson getting criticized for his work, somehow turning a tiny book into a 10h video masterpiece? Haters gonna hate.Very high production budget (akin to Game of Thrones), good actors, diverse cast (despite everyone hating that other races of actors exist in our universe), good story, nice twists, all in all everything you need to piece together a good tale. I actually look forward to watching it every week because everything else on tv absolutely sucks balls.I love a good non-canon story, just like The Witcher, and all of the adaptations. Some people just can't enjoy something for what it is? For anyone who isn't a hardcore edgelord of the books, give it a watch, you decide, it's free on Amazon. It's a pretty good show for how much hate it gets, I thought it was going to be terrible despite the hardcore review bombing?Season 1 can be a bit dry, but Season 2 is where they piece it together. I love LOTR, just enjoy it for what it is. It's literally the back story, thousands of years before The Fellowship of the Ring. History fades with time. Close enough.

They spend all the money on the rights and CGI, there was nothing left for casting, actors, costumes, screenplay, makeup, story .... . It shouldn't be allowed to carry the name of TLotR!Ridiculously bad mistakes, plotholes and logic errors.I'm a huge Tolkien fan and this is an insult to his legacy.Never relate this grotesque overpriced TV show to the world and lore Tolkien created and we have cherished. It is not a letdown as you should never hold expectations and hope it would turn out good in the slightest. But it is dishonor, an embarrassment and utter disgrace! No offense to all the actors and actresses I'm sure they tried to do a good job portraying, only whatsoever else they trashed in the show.

ipc-title__text: Rings of Prime - Lord Bezos the Defiler
ipc-html-content-inner-div: "Rings of Prime" is a deeply disappointing attempt at fantasy that feels like a hollow, corporate shell of the genre. Lord Bezos the Defiler's production is a pathetic example of postmodern fantasy that deserves to be cast into the fire.There is nothing remotely Tolkien-esque about this adaptation. From Guyladriel's unlikable sneering to the poor writing, it's a struggle to endure. The dialogue is clunky, the characters are shallow, and the plot is riddled with holes. The nonsensical world-building fails to capture even a shadow of what Middle-earth should be.This show is "NotTolkien" in any shape or form. A waste of time for true fantasy fans.

ipc-title__text: Great...if you like generic fantasy that has no real attachment to anything tolkien
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Had this been their own generic fantasy series, it would be an okay-ish show with pretty good visuals for a TV show, but its not, its supposed to be diving into one of the greatest classic fantasy literature's of all time, a subject and world built with such incredible artistry, nuance, detail and intellect, that you can study it as a PhD. Unfortunately it is clear the writers are not fans of this work, likely think very little of Tolkien, and wanted their own fantasy show but couldn't get the budget for it without shoehorning it into middle-earth. This show left me more disappointed than I have ever been from any form of entertainment in my life-time. I had been exceedingly excited for this series from the moment it was suggested as a possibility, checking in on the progress on a near monthly basis, I went in cautious but hopeful, came out utterly gutted.

After watching the first season, I really hoped they would somehow do a better second one (because how could they do worse??). But unfortunately, I had to be amazed by their ability of ruining such a good screenplay, all set and written by Tolkien.Ninety millions of dollars for each episode to basically do a "Hercules" levelled tv show from 1995 (without even a funny character like Iolao in it) with CGI effects coming from Final Fantasy VIII at most.Do not make me talk about the awful actors, the embarassing dialogues, the unpleasant music and the incredibly cringe "plot-twists". Absolutely dreadful.Years after the great, epic movies which gracefully matched the energy of the book, we have now to witness this obscenity which is pure disrespect for what Tolkien has given to us and to the entertainment industry.Probably the worst insulting tv show of all times, even more considering the budget they spent to realize it and the time they wasted to produce this despicable jumble of episodes that they have called The Rings of Power.I have to admit my vote was influenced by my love for the Lord of the Rings, if this had nothing to do with the book and the story, infact, I would have given a 2/10.

I have no words for how horrible this show is. Therefore, I will waste your time with the rest of this review in the same way that the show wasted my precious life energy. This show has made me dumber for watching it. I may never recover from this abysmal display of fan fiction masquerading as grand fantasy. Currently my brain is deteriorating as I write this because of the terminal repercussions of such a stain in our collective experience on planet earth. I didn't think it was possible to bore me at the same time as torturing me - but Rings Of Power did it. Good Lord, if I have to waste another word on this sorry review ... ok word count met. Good bye forever.

ipc-title__text: Everything except Lord of the rings
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Visually, the series is stunning. The cinematography and special effects are top-notch, creating an immersive experience. The episode lengths and pacing are well-balanced, keeping the viewer engaged.However, the series deviates too much from the original "Lord of the Rings" lore. Many changes don't make sense and there are too many side plots, making the story feel scattered. It seems like the writers and directors aren't true fans of Tolkien's original work. There's no passion in the storytelling and it shows. Despite its visual appeal, the series misses the mark on capturing the essence of Tolkien's world.Compared to Peter Jackson's masterpieces, "Rings of Power" is a complete disappointment. What we're left with is mindless entertainment, far from a masterpiece. For me, it's a disappointment and a waste of the project's potential. Amazon should seriously reevaluate the mishandling of this project.Sorry but Two stars for the great cast and the visual presentation.

ipc-title__text: Not sure why there's so much hate.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Okay, so I haven't read all the LOTR or JRR Tolkien's "masterpieces" but I have read The Hobbit and The Fellowship and I've seen all the movies multiple times. I love this world. The reason I don't finish all the books is because of the pace of reading and the songs, but other than that the character building is phenomenal and I've done a lot of TLDR learning from the internet. What im getting at is that I'm not an expert, but this show is really entertaining and enjoyable. The acting is well done, set design is beautiful, the costume design is good, not great, but so was the costume design in S1 of GOT. They're still figuring it out. For an original story set between the original war with Morgoth and the rise of Sauron, this is really good. It's fun to revisit a world we all love and get to meet new characters and old ones when they're young, as well as the Easter eggs, too.There are a lot of people review tanking this because they never liked LOTR in the first place, and there's a lot of fanboys review tanking it because it isn't slow, and full of songs and lore explaining. But at the end of the day, if you're familiar with JRR Tolkien, like LOTR and want something to watch when you're done binging GOT or HOD, this is a great show to fill your time with.

I am a 44 year fan of all things Tolkien. One thing that is not in the books is a lot of details about the Second Age of Middle Earth. We get a little bit in the Akellabeth in the Silmarillion and some allusions here and there in other books but, unless you dive deep into Christopher Tolkien's writings about his father's creative process, you'll find little about who did what with whom and when. Sure, there's high level outlines, but nothing of substance.So, to actually see someone take those few sketchy details and build a series on them makes me joyful. The plot is faithful to those tantalizing notes and the characters are faithful to what we know about them. Are there liberties taken with things like timelines and non-canonical characters? Sure...because you can't make a sure that spans literally thousands of years of time and make it coherent without having to make adjustments.Are there things that I would have done differently or that I think could have been improved upon? Sure...that's why 4 stars instead of 5. But this Tolkien nerd is very happy with what I'm seeing and can't wait for the next episodes to drop.

ipc-title__text: Cheap acting in a high budget fan fiction
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I just cannot focus on the show because of the bizarre pronunciation of proper nouns. It's like they all took a group class on rolling their "R's" and they somehow think that makes what they're saying more interesting. It grinds my gears and sets off my misphonia.The design of the elves is disappointingly underwhelming. I know they were given a very small amount of source text to go off, but many of the creative choices are upsettingly wrong.I'll push through and watch it all because the cinematography is beautiful and I enjoy fan fiction and Middle Earth hypotheticals.But it's going to be a struggle...

ipc-title__text: 2 stars for music and some visuals
Could have been worse, but should have been better
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I would expect a Lord of the Rings TV series, properly done, to be must-watch entertainment. Somehow Amazon didn't get there. The visuals are breathtaking, and the acting was good, but the script and storyline are the problem.I understand why some of the Tolkien lore was broken. For example, you can't spread the story of the Second Age over multiple centuries in a TV series, because the non-elves would be continually dying off and replaced with their children. But for every logical change to the lore, there are ten that were unnecessary. Sometimes they even do the exact opposite of what the books say. A lot more effort could have been made to make the show respectful of the Tolkien text, if that had been important to the showrunners. That would have appeased so many Tolkien fans with zero downside, and probably would have reduced numerous plotholes.I also think the showrunners need to stop worrying about connecting the series to the modern world. Tolkien didn't like allegory, instead recognizing that a good story will have archetypes that apply to every era. Instead we have men worried about elves taking their jobs, which is very silly, especially since there was only one elf there. We have the character of Galadriel designed by modern feminism, instead of the wholesome feminism Tolkien wrote into his strong female characters.All in all, the series just seems small when it should have felt big.

The show is not faithful to the source material, there are many creative liberties taken by the show writers and runners which make no sense to me or many who grew up reading lord of the rings by JRR Tolkien.There are loads of plot holes in the show which makes no sense.If you are new to the middle earth world and have not read the LOTR books or you are not a fan of the LOTR films then you can maybe still enjoy the show as a fantasy story but if you are big fan of the magical and adventure world which was visioned and created by JRR Tolkien, then you will most probably be disappointed by The Rings of Power.

ipc-title__text: The Goodish, the not-so-bad, but not ugly
ipc-html-content-inner-div: $Billion Dollar production, $250M for the rights.... Too expensive to fail? - probably. Is season 1 any good? Sort of, for me it is a decent 7.5The fact that the writers have essentially a blank page as to plot, just a starting point and a number of knowns that they cannot contradict seems to have been as much a curse as a blessing. I hope they are just getting into their stride, the Halbrand reveal was nice though.As beautiful as Numenor was, the proto-hobbit / stranger sections felt, by comparison, twee and absent the production values. Now that that plot section has moved on, hopefully they will get on with it.Overall, I expect to enjoy S02 even more than the first.

ipc-title__text: Kind of slow to start but worth it.

ipc-html-content-inner-div: Watching this show feels like stubbing your toe, hard. Every episode, the more the pain grows and with it your disillusionment with a worthy payoff at the end. Money was spent on a beautiful score, great make up, sets, costumes, and sometimes capable actors. However, every expense was sadly spared when it came down to the harsh truths of what makes the medium of film worth the time one spends watching it, the story. Which is surprising since there are literal Ph.d's in the Tolkien mythos. However, the writers and show runners decided they weren't impressed and could do better. Character arcs are flimsy and motivations brittle. All I can say is, don't bother stubbing your toe on this one, steer clear.

ipc-title__text: Less the Spirit of Tolkien and More the Letter of the Blockbuster Law
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This was created for those who have seen the movies but not read the books. It shows in the writing. It is a prequel to just put everything in its place for the movies. It has all the blockbuster tropes. Many of the lines seem to be picked right from the worst of the movies: "We have no time/there is time enough". And those trying to be poetry fail. More ought to have been invested in having a real story. As it is, it merely acts like a forward; telling you rather than showing you a story.Of the 4 storylines, the hobbits storyline is the worst and seems to be here just to have hobbits. They seem to be related to the wandering gypsies.The elven storyline, led by Galadriel, is poor because, rather than a story of repentance it is a story of revenge.The best storyline is the Dwarven storyline. But again, the scripting is poor, trying to capture the best of Lord of the Rings but encapsulating it poorly.Peter Jackson's interpretation of Lord of the Rings had a story to tell. Yes it differed from the canon, but it was interesting. This strives to be a prequel to that story, which of itself is not bad. But the writing doesn't tell a story, it just moves the pieces about to say: and here's this, and here's this and here's this. It's sloppy blockbuster scripting and not storytelling.

I'd never have thought, that it is possible to defile something like the "Lord of the Rings", or "The Wheel of Time". Well, Amazon did it! Even worse, they slaughtered it.I am not sure, if I had the privilege to watch 1 or 2 episodes, as I left the room several times, to do more entertaining things, like cleaning my dog's poo in the front yard.The bits which I watched with my friend, were ... bad. And I mean really bad. What exactly I did not like? Well, I even do not know where to start, so let me list what I did like: the colors were nice, and the actors moved.That's definitely better than black and white stills. Though, the longer I think about it, the less sure I become about that.Well, let's stop here, and be serious: It is not fair to blame the actors. They had to follow the script & director(s), dress in the costumes etc... I am just really, really disappointed, as I like both franchises a lot (and spent lots of money on them...yes, I am talking to you amazon/audible). I will not do that again.There's a word n German "verschlimmbessern" - and you did exactly that. And yes, it is as bad as it sounds.

I've been waiting years for this with big expectations. Sadly I have to say that it's a terrible show. I've read all of the books and I'm a big Tolkien fan but this series has little to nothing to do with the works of this great author. It's an abomination and it's light years away from House of the dragon.They've ruined the story and have changed it in what ever way they've wanted. ipc-title__text: Take some notes from "House of Dragon"
ipc-html-content-inner-div: It has its moments where it shines, mainly that it looks expensive. Between the lavish costumes, beautiful landscapes and sets, and the quality of the orcs, you can tell that Amazon spent a pretty penny on production. What I don't understand is how such an epic story with beautiful scenery and mythical species can somehow manage to be so dull. It feels out of date in a strange way, like it has all been done before between the LOTR and Hobbit trilogies. Maybe if this came out back in the early 2000's it would be a hit, but it feels like it has past its prime. Too many shows have come out with the same feel since the release of the first movies, and have gotten more complex (GOT, House of Dragon, Wheel of Time, etc.). Maybe that is why it feels so dated. It's like loving a movie as a child but when you watch it as adult, it just isn't as good as you remember. Ironically the topic that seemed to cause the biggest controversy seems to be its strength. So many were complaining over casting of an "elf of color". The scenes with the "ethnic" elf are by far the most entertaining. His appearance is striking and his acting is believable. The others seem to be acting in some Shakespearian play. The drawf segment with Elrond was just so difficult to get through. I felt the same with the Hobbits. I'm sorry Amazon, but I think this was a miss. Move the actor that plays the elf to House of Dragon and shut this down and save some money.

Given the quality of some streaming shows that are being pumped out like they're on a production line, some of the reviews are far too harsh for the quality of The Rings of Power. Sure, the story isn't as strong as the original LOTR or The Hobbit, but it's a pretty good takeaway from unfinished stories and "histories".Each episode is more and more visually stunning than the last, the story is progressively delving deeper into an intertwined history with what we know, and the acting is phenomenal from every character. While some plot points are easier to spot than blue in the sky, it's an easy watch that leaves you wanting more each week to confirm if your theories are true. It's definitely worth a watch, even if you're a die-hard LOTR fan.

The cinematography, the soudtrack, the ambience, the costumes, the visual effects, are all excellent. But most importantly the soul of each species is very well conveyed. The story is gaining momentum and the characters are strong. One could argue that more should be happening bit I disagree. The whole work benefitsbfrom this steady pace and the whole series will age very well.It is a great challenge to create Tolkien's world on this age only from appendixes, and one bound to fail. But so far it is succeeding.From here a whole range of possibilities arise. The Silmarillion and the Fall of Gondolin are spectacular future options.

There are several ways of evaluating this series. As a true adaptation of Tolkiens work, as a LOTR-inspired adaptation or an epic-fantasy.As a true adaptation of Tolkien; 0/10, -F, no go.A more lenient interpretation as a LOTR-inspired adaption, I'll say it is veeery heavy on the artistic license(whats up with the short hair on elves?), making up central characters, removing crucial characters, some characters cannibalising other characters story arch. A lot of modernization is included, understandably to try attract a larger audience, but comes at a cost of immersion. I cannot in all honesty give it higher than 2/10, which will be my rating of the show - as this is the way I wanted to view it, as a LOTR-inspired adaption.But as an epic-fantasy, when you disregard tolkiens work completly and come into it with an open mind and no persumptions - it is better. Some of the open background visuals are beautiful, indoors less so. The crowds feel very artificial. The information thrown at you is relatively bitsized and easy to consume. Some of the actors/actresses seem very green, hopefully they'll mature in later seasons.Your suspension of disbelief will be tested, mine failed; I'll try keep it spoiler free but saying 1 character decides to jump into the ocean and persumably swim for hundreds of miles alone. The same character, a female of small frame, without any real physical strain, weapons or tools, physically dominates 4-5 armored men by simply pushing them around and opening a closed jail cell (yes it was closed, probably an error they missed), and closing it behind them.A teenage boy gets injured in his leg and falls down constantly due to pain, but is still able to outrun a band of orcs in terrain.Orcs are not able to hit their targets with arrows, because obvious plot armour - but the attempts are pretty piss poor considering the distance. In fact in one scene, the arrows are so slow, another character is able to catch a slow moving arrow and return it ( as seen in a trailer).The first episodes intro had a visually cool battle between armies, but when you wreaks of hollywood, when you look how silly it actually is that there are no formations and just a giant mush pile.Overall I'd give it as an Epic-Fantasy ; 4/10.

The show runners made up their own story, instead of adapting the existing material. Most of the events are completely invented, and even the ones that appeared in the books, are changed almost beyond recognition. If it was their own fantasy series it would be one thing (even though these first to episodes had other problems) but the fact that they shamelessly slapped Tolkien's name on it, that the show runners kept spatting that they always "went back to the books" only to completely change the cannon is what makes me give it this harsh review. ipc-title__text: Please no more, terribly bad and drawn out... Boring!!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: After 10 years of using this app I finally created an account just so I could rate this show. Now I am far from a Tolkien expert, but I have been a fan for decades and have spent a good amount of time with the movies, books, soundtrack, etc... That being said this series is woefully and completely inadequate for the immense world that Tolkien created. I started watching knowing that it's not going to be spot on with the storyline in the books, but the creative freedom taken with some of the characters is beyond comprehension. The dialog is forced, the acting is bland and the storyline so far leaves me scratching my head or most times falling asleep in the middle of an episode. They spend so much time trying to build intensity with the characters using empty spaces with no dialog, but itjust feels like the writers didn't know what to have the characters say so they just play music while the actors stare at each other. There is no chemistry between the characters and their "love interests" and the main characters lack depth. The Visuals look cheap and are laughable compared to the original movies and the overall darkness of the settings makes it seem like it was shot with and old home movie VHS camera. Their attempts to make the fight scenes "epic" are a waste, and apart from a very short list of fight sequences, the story would have been better if they just skipped some fights/battles altogether. The build up to the final episodes are just pathetic and leave you wondering why do they need 8 episodes just to get here. As is now all of seasons 1 and 2 could be compressed into one season, if not like 6 episodes. I'm trying my best not to give any spoilers but if you are expecting a 1/2 decent series based on your favorite LOTR characters or storyline this is NOT it! This is just a testament to the fact that it takes a lot more than just money to make good content. They need to either go back to the drawing board or just cancel the series altogether. This is truly an egregious reproduction of Tolkiens work and needs serious work if they are going to keep true fans interested.

Season one was okay but good lord (no pun intended) seasons 2 is terrible. Meandering a nonsensical. No effort to create relationships between the audience and the characters. The crazy thing is this is an Amazon funded show so we all know it's to run for 30 years. They can afford to put some content into this season without risking that people won't watch in the future. People are literally a captive audience to the show because they pay for a prime membership. They don't need to slow play it but my Lord (no pun intended) is this slow. ipc-title__text: Take some notes from "House of Dragon"
ipc-html-content-inner-div: It has its moments where it shines, mainly that it looks expensive. It feels out of date in a strange way, like it has all been done before between the LOTR and Hobbit trilogies. Maybe if this came out back in the early 2000's it would be a hit, but it feels like it has past its prime. Too many shows have come out with the same feel since the release of the first movies, and have gotten more complex (GOT, House of Dragon, Wheel of Time, etc.). Maybe that is why it feels so dated. It's like loving a movie as a child but when you watch it as adult, it just isn't as good as you remember. Ironically the topic that seemed to cause the biggest controversy seems to be its strength. So many were complaining over casting of an "elf of color". The scenes with the "ethnic" elf are by far the most entertaining. His appearance is striking and his acting is believable. The others seem to be acting in some Shakespearian play. The drawf segment with Elrond was just so difficult to get through. I felt the same with the Hobbits. I'm sorry Amazon, but I think this was a miss. Move the actor that plays the elf to House of Dragon and shut this down and save some money.

There are several ways of evaluating this series. As a true adaptation of Tolkiens work, as a LOTR-inspired adaptation or an epic-fantasy.As a true adaptation of Tolkien; 0/10, -F, no go.A more lenient interpretation as a LOTR-inspired adaption, I'll say it is veeery heavy on the artistic license(whats up with the short hair on elves?), making up central characters, removing crucial characters, some characters cannibalising other characters story arch. A lot of modernization is included, understandably to try attract a larger audience, but comes at a cost of immersion. I cannot in all honesty give it higher than 2/10, which will be my rating of the show - as this is the way I wanted to view it, as a LOTR-inspired adaption.But as an epic-fantasy, when you disregard tolkiens work completly and come into it with an open mind and no persumptions - it is better. Some of the open background visuals are beautiful, indoors less so. The crowds feel very artificial. The information thrown at you is relatively bitsized and easy to consume. Some of the actors/actresses seem very green, hopefully they'll mature in later seasons.Your suspension of disbelief will be tested, mine failed; I'll try keep it spoiler free but saying 1 character decides to jump into the ocean and persumably swim for hundreds of miles alone. The same character, a female of small frame, without any real physical strain, weapons or tools, physically dominates 4-5 armored men by simply pushing them around and opening a closed jail cell (yes it was closed, probably an error they missed), and closing it behind them.A teenage boy gets injured in his leg and falls down constantly due to pain, but is still able to outrun a band of orcs in terrain.Orcs are not able to hit their targets with arrows, because obvious plot armour - but the attempts are pretty piss poor considering the distance. In fact in one scene, the arrows are so slow, another character is able to catch a slow moving arrow and return it ( as seen in a trailer).The first episodes intro had a visually cool battle between armies, but when you wreaks of hollywood, when you look how silly it actually is that there are no formations and just a giant mush pile.Overall I'd give it as an Epic-Fantasy ; 4/10.

ipc-title__text: Please no more, terribly bad and drawn out... Boring!!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: After 10 years of using this app I finally created an account just so I could rate this show. Now I am far from a Tolkien expert, but I have been a fan for decades and have spent a good amount of time with the movies, books, soundtrack, etc... That being said this series is woefully and completely inadequate for the immense world that Tolkien created. I started watching knowing that it's not going to be spot on with the storyline in the books, but the creative freedom taken with some of the characters is beyond comprehension. The dialog is forced, the acting is bland and the storyline so far leaves me scratching my head or most times falling asleep in the middle of an episode. They spend so much time trying to build intensity with the characters using empty spaces with no dialog, but itjust feels like the writers didn't know what to have the characters say so they just play music while the actors stare at each other. There is no chemistry between the characters and their "love interests" and the main characters lack depth. The Visuals look cheap and are laughable compared to the original movies and the overall darkness of the settings makes it seem like it was shot with and old home movie VHS camera. Their attempts to make the fight scenes "epic" are a waste, and apart from a very short list of fight sequences, the story would have been better if they just skipped some fights/battles altogether. The build up to the final episodes are just pathetic and leave you wondering why do they need 8 episodes just to get here. As is now all of seasons 1 and 2 could be compressed into one season, if not like 6 episodes. I'm trying my best not to give any spoilers but if you are expecting a 1/2 decent series based on your favorite LOTR characters or storyline this is NOT it! This is just a testament to the fact that it takes a lot more than just money to make good content. They need to either go back to the drawing board or just cancel the series altogether. This is truly an egregious reproduction of Tolkiens work and needs serious work if they are going to keep true fans interested.

ipc-title__text: Take Lord of the Rings out of the title
ipc-html-content-inner-div: First off, for anyone who says they a fan of LOTR and they enjoy the series but bash on people who are also fans but don't enjoy the series, that is called an opinion and not gate keeping.I had high hopes for this series when it was first announced. Even when it was revealed that they didn't have rights to The Silmarillion and only the actual LOTR books and the appendices i was excited. I have been a fan of Tolkien since I was a child, watching the animated Hobbit movie and later reading the books and watching LOTR when they released in theaters. I'm a fan of the world Tolkien built. To me, RoP seems as though someone gave first time script writers a list of characters, a start plot point, an end plot point and a bunch of lines from the movies that would "please the fans" and told them to write a potentially 5 season series. They write as though they were forbidden to actually read the source material that the series is based on as characters in the series do things that their lore based character wouldn't do. While it is fun to see characters that were left out of the movies or only received mention, their actions or lines are so random or poorly done that you spend more time thinking "wtf was that" than you are spending trying to enjoy the show. While there is a lot of beautiful scenery and costume design, it would have made the series better if they spent money on script writers who actually onoe the source material and lore and would respect it. If they took Lord of the Rings out of the title ND changed the lore based characters names so this was strictly just a fantasy series I would probably enjoy it more. But when you say it's based on Tolkiens works and then change everything but character names, you disrespect his legacy.

ipc-title__text: This is not about Heart-stopping visuals but about the History of Middle Earth

Who is Sauron, what are his origins? Who are the other protagonists and what part do they play in this historic unveiling and what impact does this have on the future narratives.If you want your entertainment and action punctuated with high tension and contrived violence, then perhaps look elsewhere.Granted this production does have its shortcomings, perhaps due to financial constraints, but it is a must-see for those devoted to this universe.

Read the books as a teenager and loved the Peter Jackson LoTR trilogy. Found the three Hobbit movies too fluffy and drawn out, but oh well.I was really looking forward to Rings of Power! With such a big budget, huge backing, modern movie making technology, and claims of Tolkien's work coming alive - I was quite hopeful.Man was I disappointed. Watched it with my wife and son, also LoTR enthusiasts, and they were also very disappointed. While cinematically impressive, it lacked character development, the pace was excruciatingly slow, and I couldn't cultivate a reason to care about any of it. Then it would jump to a different location with different characters and the cycle would repeat.The entire time, we truly *wanted* to love it, and we kept trying. We suffered through the first few episodes (and I do mean suffered) and asked each other and ourselves if there was any point continuing. We decided to persist and continued to get together when we could to watch another episode. It became more of a challenge to get through it than a true desire to see what happened next. And that's kind of the point... *most of the time, nothing ever really seemed to happen*. Long drawn out and uninteresting exposition... excruciatingly slow scenes that seemed largely pointless... fight scenes that felt very monotone... and no particular reason to root for any of the characters. It became a running joke how hard we had to fight to keep from falling asleep while watching.After all episodes - 10+ hours of viewing time - there were only two or three fleeting moments where I was genuinely interested or pleased. Thats hard to believe. Especially considering I was truly trying to like it the whole time.I sincerely hope they are making drastic changes in writing and editing for season 2. We'll have to hear reputable buzz that things are improved before giving it another chance. Because, for us, season 1 was a huge miss.
