ipc-title__text: If you are a Tolkien fan, don't bother.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I gave this two stars for the cinematography. I took away eight stars for the arrogance to think they could re-write this story..We often say that no one makes anything original anymore, but the truth is, original scripts, movies, TV, and books come out every day. And then someone attempts to cram that original into an old mold, so people will recognize it.This could have been an original, if it had used different character and place names, it is it's own story. It would not have been as good as Tolkien's, but so what?If you're looking for a companion show to the Hobbit an LoTR, this is not it. It's just a waste of time and money.

This show, just like my review title says, is disrespectful in every sense. It is disrespectful to Tolkien fans who read the books, it is disrespectful to fans who only like Tolkien cause of old video interpretations, or to those who meet Tolkien for the first time. Simply it is a bad, very bad show. The worst thing about the show is how badly it is written. The second worst thing is lies. They lied to us that this show has something in common with Tolkien and his books. I am putting this as a second worst thing cause some people only want a good show and they don't care about authenticity. But I do! And I feel like this show wants to denigrate Tolkien on purpose and to replace his vision with modern and temporary agenda.

First off, I get it, this is not a show aimed squarely at Tolkien fans who obsess over every element of the LotR appendices and the Silmarillion (more power to those people btw, I'm not one of them but I know several). Instead what we have is a reinterpretation or an abstraction of the events of the second age presented in a style more reminiscent of Jackson than Tolkien, and while that might turn some viewers off (others may be turned off by the slooowwww start) I think the series is all the better for it.What starts off as a slow, meandering (though visually stunning) story with too many scenes of nothing happening (presumably to establish the world but really, those early episodes are a bit of a drag) becomes quite brilliant about the time a certain event (no spoilers here) happens, and from then on the show really find it's footing so to speak.What's bad?The "mystery" of the identity of the stranger, pretty sure everyone knew who they are (although the bait and switch I the season 1 finale was fun).The Harfoots take FOREVER to actually DO anything, which wouldn't be a problem if this was a show about hanging out with the harfoots (Brilliant performance in particular by Lenny Henry) but their story early on slows thr whole show down.Basically pacing early on, though byvthe time everything kicks off it's forgivable.What's good?The show looks amazing. It makes House of the Dragon look cheap and miserable by comparison. It makes Peter Jacksons Lotr movies look dated. It makes The Hobbit movies look like an amateur school production. It makes marvel movies look like bad comic books. Seriously, this show is Beautiful.Performances all round in my opinion. While some relationships seem a bit rushed, I get it, story needs to happen but as a whole everyone is giving it 100% even while spouting nonsense Tolkien dialogue.Action scenes? Incredible. No surfing on trolls and backflipping rubbish here, action scenes are grounded, breathtaking, gritty and violent.All in all, left me wanting more.

ipc-title__text: it failed to live up to the hype.

ipc-html-content-inner-div: Having persevered with eight episodes of this show and now feeling pretty dirty, I am trying to redeem myself slightly by creating an account and posting a review here for the first time ever.I've given more than one star as the CGI was obviously well done in parts - the wider landscape shots looked amazing, although think some scenes (e.g. Khazad Dum) still had a Hobbit look to them, overused CGI and lacked depth.But thats about as good as it gets. While I have no doubt that some of the actors are genuinely woeful, no one could possibly salvage the Hollyoaks-level script and direction. Its like they were attempting to make every single line sound profound and epic, and ended up with a load of wooden exposition and poorly ripped-off quotes from the trilogy.The poor writing is clearest whenever an elf is on screen, which is unfortunate as they take up a lot of screen time. Amazon elves are so far removed from the ethereal beings Peter Jackson created, and more like listening to students in a school Shakespeare play. Galadriel is the closest thing this show has to a protagonist, but as it transpires they managed to conjure up the most one-dimensional, arrogant, unlikeable character in Middle Earth which is also an achievement in itself.I could slightly forgive the plot's divergence from the source material if it was any good, but its laughably thin. Foolishly, I did begin to wonder why half the storylines were even included, but quickly remembered they want to pad this out into 4+ seasons. Superb.A prodigious waste of a billion bucks.

So why is she called Brandyfoot?Also in the opening scene where we see Galadriel as a child, she was not yet called Galadriel. The name Galadriel was only given to her by her husband, Celeborn. Speaking of him, where is he? Galadriel should, at the time of the series, be thousands of years old and married, but I guess that wouldn't be relatable enough for modern young adults.Galadriel in general is just completely different than in Tolkien's writings. For example, a very important plot point is Galadriel sailing off to the undying lands. This sets off a long chain of events. The real Galadriel however, was forbidden from going back there! She was only allowed to do so at the end of the Lord of the Rings because she helped defeat Sauron.Judging by the title of the series, we will eventually see the forging of the rings happen. As it turns out however, this takes part more than 500 years in the future from where we are now. Unless there is a massive time-jump mid series, they plan to condense half a millenium into a few seasons.Also, that meteorite guy better not be Gandalf!I could go on and on, just from these first two episodes. This really is just the biggest fanfiction ever written, the writing skill also fits.

The writing and creativity are genuine to the spirit of the original stories as I read them forty years ago (and several times since), the lands, speech and costume details so carefully etched, the expressions and thoughts conveyed through eye contact between the actors deeply felt, and the cinematography so striking and lovely...or doomily. I already feel such an affinity for this show - I eagerly await the release of the coming episodes.

For anyone whose skeptical JUST GIVE IT A GO. If you don't like it nothing lost. If you do like it then enjoy.As a fan of the lord of the rings trilogy and someone who was disappointed with the hobbit trilogy, this is a very well deserved return to middle earth of which I was sceptical at first but have fallen in love with it.Only 2 episodes in and I'm already sold on the story that's being teased, our new and familiar characters and the scope and scale in the terms of the production.This series has the same feeling that was evoked with Peter Jackson's take on the material. Even to my surprise the series is faithful to Jackson's films in terms of design in its locations, creatures and characters, making it feel very much like a prequel to his films as opposed to a LOTR reboot.Hopefully this show will continue to grow on its own and be on par with Game of thrones and house of the dragon.

Long ago in memory distant, there was the story of "The One Ring". "One ring to rule them all." Arguably the first assembly of comparable medieval acclaim since T. H White's "The Once and Future King", the adaptions of Tolkien's "Lord of the Rings" novels are a daunting task.The casting, set pieces, and stuntwork show high competence well into the second season. Though there are moments true Tolkien fans will no doubtedly lament as being unfaithful to "scripture", the special effects, wardrobe, and make-up design truly do deserve to stack the Emmys high as Celebrembor's fateful forge. Of how varied people's wants and tastes are, is the rating on this series...a real love/hate phenomena...i'm very much in the former aspect...
i don't care about the Tolkien works...i always try to take any work on its own merits...and i loved many things about this series...the second season reminds me a bit of the second(Empire Strikes Back) Star Wars movie...but specifically saying why would definitely be a spoiler and i don't do spoilers...

there was one episode in the second season that i considered to be weak, to the point of it being cringeworthy....but then it recovered. But these, of course, are just my opinions...still i'm glad to be enjoying this epic work...

ipc-title__text: A wonderful return to Middle Earth
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This show delves into the last decades of the Second Age, and it is a brilliant and visually stunning adaptation of material from the appendices in LoTR.It explores how the Rings of Power came into being and how Sauron rose to power, following characters such as Elrond, Galadriel, Elendil, Isildur, Durin and the ancestors of the Hobbits to tell this story.I have read the appendices and The Silmarillion and thoroughly enjoys this way of using the material to set the stage for what we know will happen thousands of years later of LoTR.Each episode feels like a movie in its own right, so I am here for all the planned five seasons.

I started watching The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power last week, and I'm officially hooked! I ended up binging both seasons, and honestly, I could watch this series forever. It's like being swept back into Middle-earth, but in a way that's even more immersive than I expected. The visuals are absolutely breathtaking, with stunning landscapes, intricate costume designs, and scenes that bring Tolkien's world to life in vibrant detail. Every frame feels like a piece of art, and it makes the viewing experience that much richer.The storyline is also everything I hoped it would be. It's both thrilling and heartfelt, a perfect mix of excitement, humor, and moments that pull you in emotionally. There's this special charm to the show, especially in how it weaves in various characters' journeys. I'm a huge fan of Durin, Disa, Nori, and "The Stranger" (the wizard). Each of them brings something unique to the table. Durin and Disa's relationship is pure joy to watch-Durin's humor and Disa's strength are so relatable, and their banter always makes me laugh. There's this playful energy between them that's both funny and heartwarming, especially the scene when Durin says, "I love youu!"Nori's storyline with The Stranger is another highlight for me. Their bond is unexpected, but it's what makes the journey feel fresh and magical, adding to the show's sense of adventure.Cant wait for season 3!!!

ipc-title__text: Thanks for filming, but the story is difficult to understand

ipc-html-content-inner-div: Full of characters that serve no purpose. Full of destroyed characters that had the biggest potentials. I'm seriously just feeling more and more disappointed by the minute. Season 2 is a bigger let down than season 1 was... and that says something.

ipc-title__text: Honestly... it is really good. Especially season two
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I think the overall rating for this show is perhaps from people who have only watched the first season, or perhaps even only part of season one. ipc-title__text: Amazing!, why is it getting so much hate?

ipc-title__text: Worth to watch, just try and judge!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I honestly don't understand the haters of this second season, unless they are totally conditioned and blind. Ignore the haters!I'm a huge fan of Tolkien and I absolutely love this 'version' of events. The purists are hating on it because it's not 100% true to the Lore but I think they've done an amazing job nonetheless. Superb scenery and CGI, the well known and well loved characters are all there, it's well casted and the script is well written IMO. I'm not sure what the Tolkien nerds want but, production wise, I doubt they'll ever get anything as good as this that even comes close. I hope they manage to keep this going for a few series, long enough to reach some form of conclusion anyway (Saurons defeat at the hands of Isildur perhaps?).

Unnecessary , long and nonsense dialogs ... Several storylines that most of them are Boring . Sometimes I think this series is made by a drunk man or a person without any knowledge of art or cinema . Who cares about depth of dialogs , who cares about charismatic characters , just film 10 minutes of each storyline and make an episode and let it go , this is how they think . Honestly, the best thing about the show is how freaking gorgeous it is-the score, the costumes, the set design. The cinematography is virtually seamless when compared to LOTR making it very believable we're living in the same world, albeit millennia before.Yes, there are broad liberties, but this was never going to be a direct adaptation of anything. That allows it a lot of freedom as long as the films are respected, and they've pulled this off very well. And for a relatively unknown cast, much like the films, they're committed to their characters.It can get a bit long and serious, and you must devote attention to it-and familiarity with Middle Earth lore is helpful-so it isn't something you can just check in and out of with little thought, expecting to be dazzled. Be patient, don't expect Lord of the Rings, and just enjoy it for what it is.Critics have nicked it for not capturing the fervor of Game of Thrones. GoT was thrilling, gory and full of sexual taboos that are likely a huge reason people devoured it. It also broke the rules with shocking deaths of main characters while the villains ran free.You won't find that here. You don't need it with Middle Earth. I feel it would come off as a sellout if they even tried. Let Westeros be Westeros and Middle Earth be Middle Earth.

Initially I joined the many fans that complained about lore and the moany nature of a certain elven woman, but after a rewatch..Cinematically this series is beautiful and there's no doubt about that!Cast where good within their roles and very much helped with emerson.This series got better over time, when you realise the restrictions imposed on the creative side of this production where pretty harsh actually the end production isn't bad at all.The character do seem to follow the same arcs but, again overlooking these facts I still feel this series in comparison to many other first series is a solid 7/8-10.

This product has nothing. In common with Lord of the Rings. Nothing. It's like a badly written, even worse acted fan fiction, by someone who clearly hates the source material. Unfortunately that someone was given money and they used that money to express their loathing of Tolkien's works, actively refusing to even read it, but just hate it on principal. It belongs in the dust, forgotten, buried and never to be spoken of again. And that is what is happening.

ipc-title__text: Not as bad as everyone thinks.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The show wasn't that bad, the sets, actors and costumes were really good and it's definitely setting up the next seasons. But thats my biggest issue with the plot of the first season. Because the entire season is dedicated to setting up the story it feels slow. On top of that some of the characters are very uninteresting, most notably Isildur who is destined to be the one who defeats sauron during the second age. Everything with the Harfoots bored my to death with the only redeeming quality being the Stranger. The shows best episode ûdun was the only episode that I really enjoyed watching. I feel as though most of the overly negative reviews I've seen are from the Tolkien extremists who hate the fact that something original is being done with the franchise. This is especially not a cash grab like the final hobbit movie because it would be the most unethical cash grab in history if that were the case considering they spent hundreds of millions of dollars on this show. If you love LOTR and are willing to trudge through the rough parts of this story then I recommend it.

ipc-title__text: I am having a hard time finding anything good

ipc-html-content-inner-div: The show gets better after a few episodes. You need to persevere. I appreciated the music, the effects and the quality of the visual experience. The acting isn't the best, but it is entertaining and leaves you wanting to know the rest of the story at the end of the série. The world created is fascinating. I wish I had such a good imagination. It is good to watch something that brings you entirely elsewhere and makes you dream.I encourage everyone to watch it and make its own opinion. It may not be for everyone, but it should distract you from your busy life. I know I will certainly watch the next season if there is one.

Here is my main problems with the show:1- Terrible writing: ROP feels like it was made by amateurs that were given a large budget. The characters are corny, dull, and boring. The plot/pacing were all over the place, and the dialogue was horrendous.2- The Elves: Tolkiens elves are supposed to be beautiful, ethereal, wise, and do not age past their prime. The elves in ROP are not good looking, are played by actors who are way too old/well past their prime, and do not act wise like beings who are 100s-1000s of years old. - In the original LOTR trilogy, Frodo and Sam are amazed just by seeing elves pass through the woods because they are otherworldly and beautiful. In ROP elves are literally humans with pointy ears and that is not an exaggeration.Those are my main two points but there is also many other issues with the show that I don't feel like writing on here. If a show is bad I usually just don't watch and move on, but since I am a big Tolkien fan and a half BILLION dollars was spent on this show I felt like I had to write a review.

I'm not a LOTR expert, but I've read my fair share of its universe books. So coming from a LOTR fan, this series was such a disappointment.But I tried to let this side go and try to enjoy this new media with an unbiased view. But even like this, I found myself unable to enjoy it. Because not only from the world building viewpoint, but characterization, dialogues, pacing... The problems pile up and after finishing the series you won't want to ever look at it again.The word "cringe" come to mind from time to time while I watched the series and part of me didn't want to blame the actors and actresses for it, but rather the bad writing. The production feels cheap as well, despite me knowing how much it cost, I truly cannot believe it the end product ended becoming like this.

ipc-title__text: What a messy and horribly written adaptation.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: To start off; I was positive the entire first season. Being a huge Tolkien fan I was just happy that someone was making a show about the second age. That quickly became impossible as the "story" progressed.Right out of the gate they made it obvious that the story was only going to use characters and places from the books, no stories or timelines would be kept. Being a fantasy show that is allowed, however this was a great example of "if it ain't broke don't fix it".Lastly, this show feels like a jab at Tolkien fans written by someone that has never heard of Tolkien. Why? You had great source material to use, a great many resources at your disposal and what emerged was something that makes zero sense. You crammed so much into a show and still nothing happened. Its sad that the show turned out like this as I was really looking forward to a good show about a story that I deeply love. Now I hope they cancel it completely or they destroy the first season and start over. If you watched it and enjoyed it, great.I'm thankful to Amazon for the attempt, but this was not even close to good. I am out and I will not be watching any further seasons connected to the first season.

This is what happens when you get 'unlimited' budget and oceans of time to tell a story. Absolute yawn fest. Dull, Dull, Dull. Sometimes it's better to have limits and be forced to make hard decisions. Not only does it move at a glacial pace, but it is a straight rip off of Game of Thrones. The city settings, the duelling families, it is genuinely hard to remember whether you're watching LOTR or GOT. Such a disappointment after the great LOTR films (not too sure about the Hobbit films - more yawn festa trying to squeeze all the last juice out of Tolkien's material). Have it 7 episodes, then gave up. Life is too short.

ipc-title__text: Boring wit a the script that flawed everywhere
ipc-html-content-inner-div: From a Tolkien fan point of view, the work not only ignores Tolkien's writings but in most cases radically contradicts them. The series has disappointed me more and more to the point of only being able to finish it imagining that it was a generic fantasy serie with nothing to do with Middle-earth, but even so it has seemed unbearable to me, the script errors are enormous, often bordering on the comic . As for the actors, the casting and characterization is appalling. The characters lack depth and personality, even going on to act completely contrary to how they had been presented to us at the beginning. Most characters become obnoxious and unfriendly. It is a shame that with the budget that Amazon had and with the best fantasy story ever written, the result is so poor.

I thought this was a worthy entry in the LOTR world. I found it better than the Hobbit movies and almost as good as the LOTR movies. The acting, the writing, the special effects and just the overall look were all top notch. I watched the entire show in 2 days. Couldn't wait to see where it went and I wasn't disappointed in the slightest. I'm honestly stunned that the show doesn't have a much higher rating, but we live in a society that loves to tear things down just because that's the way the wind is blowing at the moment. I think there was a rush to judge this quickly and it deserves much more praise than it is getting.Can't wait for Season 2!

ipc-title__text: Captures the spirit of Jackson's LOTR trilogy
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This is not the masterpiece that is Peter Jackson's original trilogy, but it is a fantastic and gorgeous series that captures the spirit of those films. It's a slow-burn, for sure, but intriguing and captivating in its own way, nonetheless. I like it very much so far.There isn't one bad actor in the entire cast. The production design, cinematography, and costumes all harken back to the look of Jackson's films very well, and it all feels like a cohesive whole. Also, I've been a fan of Bear McCreary's since Battlestar Galactica, and his work here doesn't dissapoint. I sincerely hope the series contiues for a while. I like it much better than the vulgar, incomprehsible mess that is Game of Thrones and it's spinoff.

ipc-title__text: The family is really enjoying this
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Great family show. Loads of fun, suspense and beautiful cinematography! We are anxious to see each episode as it comes out. We really like Lord of the Rings and the context gives us enough to understand some of the nuances and what is being referenced. We aren't as caught up in how accurate it is to Tolkien as some but I don't feel there are glaring holes. I've read all of the books 15 years ago and seen every movie at least twice - so I'm more than a casual fan but not over the top. I do feel like Galadriel isn't as clever as I would expect for a centuries old elf and doesn't seem to know how to navigate her way around a social situation. Other than this, I don't really take issue with the characters. I am so excited to follow this for the next five years and hope that some over the top fans don't dissuade Amazon from their long term plans here.

I was really anxious for this show, and it exceeded my expectations. The story is rich in details from Tolkien's universe, even though the writers only had rights to the appendices. Of course they had to adapt some parts, but still, it's so much better than shows like GOT - a "fantasy" copy of House of Cards, with interesting dialogues but a mediocre universe. The acting and soundtracks are also great! The characters' makeup is the only thing I didn't quite liked, especially the elves' - too exaggerated lol. Anyways, I hope all the next episodes are as amazing and full of details as the ones already released!

ipc-title__text: Great budget squandered on a made-up fan fiction where the creators clearly lack experience
Nice scenes but characters make no sense
A strong beginning to a new adventure in Middle-Earth
ipc-html-content-inner-div: A breathtaking and absolutely marvelous show handmade for the pure-hearted Tolkien fans that used to daydream about adaptations while reading The Silmarillion and Unfinished Tales and for those who loved the movie trilogy and wondered "is there more to this tale?"With strong writing, even stronger acting and characterization, and literally the best visuals ever seen on the small screen, The Rings of Power is a feast for all those with a passion for fantasy.Although the plot does contain its share of new characters and storylines they are very in line with the themes and writings of Tolkien and do their best to enhance the narrative and keep the plot moving forward. A special compliment to the charming harfoots and the mighty dwarves that shone even brighter on these 2 episodes!

It's been a long and nervous wait for this long time Tolkien fanI l could breathe a sigh of relief and say that this series surpassed my expectations and really delivered.The humour and charm of the hobbits, the grandeur of the dwarf kingdom on display and finally what joy to finally see a dwarf lady! Great to see more of the elves... and even no Orlando Bloom cameo! :)Lands of old, we only heard off made real, beautiful and epic landscapes a feast to the eyes. Movie quality action scenes that were as good as any I've seen.Great story telling and great actors delivered on a show with such impossibly high expectations to meet.Well done to the Amazon Prime and the whole production team on what must have been a grand labour of love.

Evil cannot create anything new, they can only corrupt and ruin what good forces have invented or made.The show is a as bad as you think it is. The acting is poor and the choice of actors for every single character could have been better, you know what im talking about... im not an actor myself, but sometimes these people maybe should consider if this is the right job for them and how they will be remembered. But who knows what i had choosen if some guys with litteral bags of money offer me to ruin a beloved franchise for fans i absolutely don't care about...?The CGI, considering the gargantuan budget, you rarely have an opportunity to use this word in a sentence, is loveless to its core. It looks so bland and boring that it could be used in any modern superhero movie. Nothing new, nothing original.The same goes for the props. Be it costumes or the background decoration. The Rings of Power, Amazon's highly anticipated and massively budgeted entry into J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth, promised to be an epic expansion of the *Lord of the Rings* universe. Unfortunately, despite its stunning visuals and ambitious scope, the series fails to capture the magic, depth, and spirit of Tolkien's world.One of the most glaring issues with The Rings of Power is its writing. The plot often feels disjointed and lacks the cohesive narrative flow that made the original Lord of the Rings trilogy so compelling. Many episodes drag on with little payoff, and key moments that should be emotionally resonant or suspenseful fall flat due to clunky dialogue and underdeveloped character arcs. The attempt to weave multiple storylines together results in a lack of focus, with none of the narratives being as gripping or immersive as they could be. As a result, the series often feels more like a collection of disconnected subplots rather than a grand, unified tale.Character development is another major weakness. Many of the central characters, including Galadriel, are either poorly fleshed out or inconsistent in their motivations. Galadriel, a fan-favorite from Tolkien's works, is depicted in a way that seems out of sync with her established character. Rather than a wise, ethereal figure, she's often portrayed as a stubborn and overly aggressive warrior, which feels like a significant departure from the nuanced character fans know. Similarly, other characters are written in ways that make it hard to empathize with or invest in their journeys, leaving viewers feeling detached from their fates.The pacing of the show is also problematic. The series frequently moves at a snail's pace, particularly in the early episodes, where long stretches of exposition and world-building fail to build tension or excitement. While world-building is important in a show of this scale, it often feels like The Rings of Power is more interested in showing off its impressive production design than telling a captivating story. The gorgeous visuals, while undeniably stunning, can't compensate for the slow-moving plot that never quite seems to go anywhere significant.Another point of frustration is the handling of Tolkien's lore. While it's understandable that some liberties would be taken in adapting such a complex mythos, many fans of the source material have been disappointed by the changes made to key events, timelines, and characters. The show often feels like it's using Tolkien's world as a backdrop for a generic fantasy story rather than respecting the rich history and themes of the original works. This disconnect from the lore not only alienates die-hard Tolkien fans but also contributes to the feeling that The Rings of Power lacks the heart and soul that made The Lord of the Rings so iconic.In the end, The Rings of Power feels like a missed opportunity. With its massive budget and access to one of the most beloved fantasy worlds ever created, the series should have been a triumph. Instead, it struggles to balance its ambition with coherent storytelling, compelling characters, and respect for the source material. While it may still appeal to viewers who are looking for a visually spectacular fantasy series, those hoping for a worthy addition to Tolkien's legacy are likely to be left disappointed.

With that in mind, I can only really know if it falls into the Universe well based off of the movies and other fan made content that I've viewed, and in my opinion, it follows the established lore just fine. Likely, if you are a more casual viewer like myself, then you will think it's fine, too.If you notice anything, it's likely going to be that the elves have very different hairstyles and some carry themselves more casually than they have in LOTR and The Hobbit. I personally did not agree with that change, but it's not a deal breaker.Moving on, the costumes, cinematography and special effects are also really well done. It is a well made show that has been invested into accordingly. You will not be left visually wanting when it comes to this series.Lastly, the story line. I have read reviews stating it's too predictable and others saying they have no idea what the writers are trying to do. Again, I think the writers have done well with this series. Each episode follows the last and it builds up the storyline until you reach the ultimate finale. Each character is slowly developed and established as well, so it does invest that time in each episode. This is not a topical series where it's just trying to get from point a to point b and throw some action in between to keep the audience engaged. While it does have action and excitement, it still takes the time to create a story for each unique character that is being used within a larger plot.

If you do not intend to make a Tolkien story, that is fine, but then don't call it The Lord of the Rings.

ipc-title__text: Big letdown, yet not a bad show
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I've enjoyed watching the show so far; however, you have to lower your expectations to enjoy it.Amazon boasts that this show will cost close to a billion dollars in production. Yet - somehow - it is so much smaller than (i.e.:) Return of the King, which had a production expense of roughly $150 million if you adjust for inflation.I have seen nothing in the show so far that would explain this unprecedented cost. The show is fun and entertaining, but if you go into it hoping for anything similar to the battle scenes within Lord of the Rings you will be disappointed. It is very small scale and lame if you don't manage your expectations.The dialog can get very corny. I'll admit that the LOTR trilogy could get corny with its dialog as well, but Rings of Power lacks the sentimental, poetic feel that Tolkien's words had. It's typical fantasy show dialog that assumes using cryptic and awkward vocabulary adds drama to the story.Tolkien's books have so much wonder and beauty to them. Apart from the plot line involving Elrond and Durin, this show does not have very much of either. I hope that I am proven wrong as the show progresses.

ipc-title__text: Don't believe the Haters,make up your own mind.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Having watched first 5 episodes now I feel I can give an reasoned well rounded review.I myself am a big fan of middle earth and its stories, from the books to the Peter jackson movies.I am apparently lucky enough to be able to enjoy a series adapted from a book by seperating the two in my mind knowing that the showrunnners have to make changes from the book, but as long as they keep the core essence and don't stray too far, I'm usually OK with most changes if I can understand why they did that.Rings of power might seem to stray alot from the Tolkien source if the TV show had the rights to silmarillion and unfinished tales etc. However they don't, they have the rights to the Lord of the rings and the appendices, which have a condensed history of middle earth.So with all that in mind placing the story in the 2nd age just before the forging of the rings of power is very clever, as not much beyond the dry facts in the appendices is known, I look at these as markers for events that some may or may not happen depending on the importance to then story that the show runners are writing.All this give plenty of things that the writers of the show can invent and include to surprise and amaze audiences, and they do, whilst keeping the spirit of the lore and feel of the book world in mind.One of the main gripes people seem to have is about one of the main characters galadriel, again not much is actually written about her as to her activities in the 2nd age 3000 years before she is the serene powerful galadriel from the book. They have given her an story arc. She starts the rings of power in a different state of mind with a different role, giving her a journey.There's also plenty of new characters which are grounded in the lore, but as not as not much is written gives a lot of scope for the writers to be creative.Overall this reviewer believes strongly that the hate for this show before it even aired is completely unwarranted, and in general we should all stop clicking on YouTube!/news articles that want to show us everything wrong with X Show in an attempt to subvert our opinion before it's formed for ourselves.In conclusion, keep an open mind and give it a watch, as the the world they have created is steeped in middle earth lore, rich in costumes and scenery and the acting is excellent.So this viewer is really enjoying the show. Make your own mind up!

Nobody, not even the elves, would say such a embarrassing line like that.After 6 episodes, It was nice to going back to Middle Earth, but is like nothing happened so far. I hope to be suprised by the end of this season, otherwise, Rings of Power will be easily forgotten.

The writing for the characters is really poor. They write what I call "payoff" scenes/dialogue for characters without putting in the work building up to the moment. If you want your character to be epic and cool, don't just show then doing epic and cool things. Show them being a kind, likeable, relatable; give the audience a personal connection with the characters. THEN you get to do a payoff scene with some epic action or dialogue. Otherwise you're epic and cool dialogue just makes your character look cringe and arrogant, aka galadriel.More importantly, plan some actual character development, instead of planning events and putting in characters whose sole purpose is getting us to the next event/character reveal of the story. Character development is what's important. Not your boring predictable plot points and "epic" (cringe) action/dialogue scenes.There are some entertaining scenes. Elrond has good moments. It's not terrible, so not a 1/10, but it's not very good so not close to a 7/10. 4/10 seems fair if not generous. The intro to episode 1 has an epic and exciting exposition and then everything else falls flat.

ipc-title__text: Don't believe the Haters,make up your own mind.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Having watched first 5 episodes now I feel I can give an reasoned well rounded review.I myself am a big fan of middle earth and its stories, from the books to the Peter jackson movies.I am apparently lucky enough to be able to enjoy a series adapted from a book by seperating the two in my mind knowing that the showrunnners have to make changes from the book, but as long as they keep the core essence and don't stray too far, I'm usually OK with most changes if I can understand why they did that.Rings of power might seem to stray alot from the Tolkien source if the TV show had the rights to silmarillion and unfinished tales etc. However they don't, they have the rights to the Lord of the rings and the appendices, which have a condensed history of middle earth.So with all that in mind placing the story in the 2nd age just before the forging of the rings of power is very clever, as not much beyond the dry facts in the appendices is known, I look at these as markers for events that some may or may not happen depending on the importance to then story that the show runners are writing.All this give plenty of things that the writers of the show can invent and include to surprise and amaze audiences, and they do, whilst keeping the spirit of the lore and feel of the book world in mind.One of the main gripes people seem to have is about one of the main characters galadriel, again not much is actually written about her as to her activities in the 2nd age 3000 years before she is the serene powerful galadriel from the book. They have given her an story arc. She starts the rings of power in a different state of mind with a different role, giving her a journey.There's also plenty of new characters which are grounded in the lore, but as not as not much is written gives a lot of scope for the writers to be creative.Overall this reviewer believes strongly that the hate for this show before it even aired is completely unwarranted, and in general we should all stop clicking on YouTube!/news articles that want to show us everything wrong with X Show in an attempt to subvert our opinion before it's formed for ourselves.In conclusion, keep an open mind and give it a watch, as the the world they have created is steeped in middle earth lore, rich in costumes and scenery and the acting is excellent.So this viewer is really enjoying the show. Make your own mind up!

Nobody, not even the elves, would say such a embarrassing line like that.After 6 episodes, It was nice to going back to Middle Earth, but is like nothing happened so far. I hope to be suprised by the end of this season, otherwise, Rings of Power will be easily forgotten.

The writing for the characters is really poor. They write what I call "payoff" scenes/dialogue for characters without putting in the work building up to the moment. If you want your character to be epic and cool, don't just show then doing epic and cool things. Show them being a kind, likeable, relatable; give the audience a personal connection with the characters. THEN you get to do a payoff scene with some epic action or dialogue. Otherwise you're epic and cool dialogue just makes your character look cringe and arrogant, aka galadriel.More importantly, plan some actual character development, instead of planning events and putting in characters whose sole purpose is getting us to the next event/character reveal of the story. Character development is what's important. Not your boring predictable plot points and "epic" (cringe) action/dialogue scenes.There are some entertaining scenes. Elrond has good moments. It's not terrible, so not a 1/10, but it's not very good so not close to a 7/10. 4/10 seems fair if not generous. ipc-title__text: The haters don't have a clue

I even remember thinking: 'those boring books?' when word got out LOTR was going to be brought to the big screen. But Peter Jackson did a fine job on editing the source material. He ommited many elements (like Tom Bombadil) and rearranged the timeline (there's a big stretch between Bilbo's departure and Frodo leaving with the ring.) But Jackson also did a lot of things ROP is accused of. There are so many lenghty scenes (like the last half hour of 'Return of the king') and there are also many additions or deviations of the source material (Arwen's role), some for the better, some for the worse. Rings of Power doesn't do anything LOTR hasn't done before.Yes, Rings of Power had a slow start. Some stuff could have been told more fluently. But Rings of Power is great at expanding the LOTR universe. The creation of Mordor was a bull's eye. Gandalf's origin story clarifies his relation to the hobbits. And Sauron's character got the depth he never had in LOTR.I admit the second season was better than the first, but of course: every series needs an introductory phase. But the series has just as many grand battles as the movies and the story line is much better than Tolkien's. Rings of Power is on a roll now. Let's hope next season will be just as great.

ipc-title__text: Filled with contempt for Tolkien, his fans and general audiences

ipc-title__text: A Missed Opportunity: The Rings of Power Falls Short of Tolkien's Legacy
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" initially promised to delve deeper into Tolkien's mythical world, pre-dating the famous trilogy. However, as the season unfolded, it proved underwhelming, squandering its rich narrative potential. Throughout its first season, it entangled itself in convoluted storylines that did little more than frustrate and confuse viewers.The finale aimed to answer the pivotal question, "Who is Sauron?" Yet, it felt more like an unwelcome puzzle rather than a compelling narrative arc. Despite the show's potential, many characters and plot points felt half-baked, with performances that often lacked consistency. Some actors, like Morfydd Clark, did provide occasional glimpses of depth, but overall, the inconsistent tone and weak direction left much to be desired.Additionally, the visual effects, though backed by a hefty budget, failed to impress, further detracting from the immersive experience one expects from such a storied franchise. Amazon's attempt seems more a misdirected effort to enhance its branding than a genuine tribute to Tolkien's legacy. Despite the initial hype, I am skeptical about the continuation of this series, which has yet to prove if it can rise to meet the expectations set by its illustrious predecessors.

The elves of Lord of the Rings remain the best screen depiction of elves aside from the Shannara Chronicles in my opinion, having greatly disliked the depiction of elves in the Witcher series (despite that series being alright). I would gladly sign on to watch another season, and I particularly like that they had nice cozy 1 hour 20 minute episodes that felt like an epic series of mini-films, they were just the right length to enjoy on a work night while leaving me with the fulfilled feeling of having watched a feature. Overall, a very impressive product from Amazon Studios.

Amazon's attempt seems more a misdirected effort to enhance its branding than a genuine tribute to Tolkien's legacy. Despite the initial hype, I am skeptical about the continuation of this series, which has yet to prove if it can rise to meet the expectations set by its illustrious predecessors.

ipc-title__text: When a mail order company produces a fantasy show...
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Did you ever wonder what fantasy streaming television series developed by an online mail order company would look like? "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power'' is the answer. Visually stunning in parts it falls short in almost every other aspect of filmmaking. The story is only sporadically based on what J. R. R. Tolkien has written in the appendices of the Lord of the Rings books and sometimes even contradicts it. While the newly invented story lines and characters of the show are somewhat interesting at times, they are mostly boring and more importantly, they do not really fit into the Middle Earth Tolkien has described in so much detail and that people have been delving into for over half a century. The pacing and time compression is confusing and often nonsensical. While there is attention to detail in some places other times you cannot overlook gross inaccuracies and inconsistencies. Among all its deficiencies the writing is probably the show's greatest weakness. Even if you ignore the lore of Tolkien's universe, the way characters behave and interact appears clumsy, contrived and often devoid of logic. Generally the story feels exactly like that: a story. Characters act and events unfold to fit the narrative but there appears to be no organic development of the plot. Even in a fantasy world the basic laws of physics, psychology and biology should apply at least sometimes. It is puzzling why a company would buy such a valuable and beloved intellectual property and then waste it on an unimaginative show like this. If you want to look at beautiful computer-generated imagery, or you have trouble falling asleep, watch "The Rings of Power". If you want to learn more about Middle Earth, or enjoy a gripping fantasy story, stick to the books or at least watch the movie adaptations by Peter Jackson.

Even the making of the rings of power is portrayed here fundamentally at odds with the books in a way which shatters the logic of the story arc. If you want that spelled out point by point, consult endless long-form YouTube analyses.Is the above a nerdy quibble in the face of great character building, excellent dialog and compelling portrayal? This makes the hubris of disrespect for the source material all the more galling: there's evidence of money being spent but scant evidence of creative flair. It ultimately feels like a hollow indulgence by created by self-regarding second-raters.

A bit of aging should sort this out easily enough.All in all, I'm excited to see where this show goes and how other major players are introduced.

ipc-title__text: It's mostly good, but oh how great it could have been.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Yes there are flaws. Yes, it is too slow. But does it take you to middle earth? Does it help create the history you imagine, but do not know? Is it getting better as it goes on? I would say yes, and that is worth an 8 in my book.The real question is, could it have been a 10? Unfortunately, that is a yes too. The creators really need to step up their game and make more of this opportunity. It should be far better than just watchable with some good highlights, it should be amazing with some mind-blowing moments.

ipc-title__text: Not even slightly resemblant of Lord Of The Rings

ipc-title__text: THE RINGS OF POWER deliver, are solid and highly entertaining
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Like most Fans of Peter Jacksons fantastic and unsurpassed movie trilogy I was sceptic about another Tolkien-Product, especially since THE HOBBIT seemed rushed and bloated. And also because Amazon is always about the money and seldom about the art.And yes: THE RINGS OF POWER is nowhere near as groundbreaking as the movie trilogy.But it's highly entertaining and a good addition to the cinematic Tolkien-universe - especially if considered that the producers didn't have the rights to use all of the authors materials - just THE HOBBIT and THE LORD OF THE RINGS - as a basis for this prequel-story.A series like CLARICE which is based on the main character of THE SILENCE OF THE LAMBS but had no right to use the character or even the name "Hannibal" shows how this can go wrong.The world of THE RINGS OF POWER unfolds piece by piece - but it's clearly very early on that we are in middle earth. Characters are introduced and step by step there's a threat and the tension rises while story lines are connected.This might be to slow for some but considering some series are all about complexity and nothing about character-depth (DARK anyone?) THE RINGS OF POWER offers a welcome change.Plus: There's so many ties to the movie trilogy the can be discovered in plot twists that get bigger and bigger the more the story moves forward.The acting is great - especially Morfydd Clark as Galadriel - as well as all the other actors, some of which portrait younger versions of characters we've come to admire in the original movies - and no one disappoints.Go see for yourselves....

When I was a kid, I read The Hobbit and Lord of The Rings. Then the LOTR films came out and I was amazed. The Hobbit films came out and I was underwhelmed.I wasn't aware of the hype regarding this show. I think I read that it was in production a few months ago, but it was a bit of a surprise when I logged onto Prime a few weeks ago and saw it was there, with the first three episodes ready for viewing. I was looking for something new to watch, and nothing else really appealed to me, so I thought I'd just give this a go and see how I feel about it. At the time,I was instantly hooked! I had no idea what to expect, but everything about it was enjoyable to me. The scenery and cinematography are obviously unbelievable, as one should expect for such a high-budget show, but also the characters and storylines are all so well-written that I'm gripped.After watching the latest episode this morning, I decided to just check the user ratings, expecting to see something like a 9.5/10 or something similar. So to see 6.9/10 as I'm writing this seems strange to me, as though I must be missing something.I've read some of the negative reviews, and I feel as though I'm watching a different show to them. But each has their own opinions on the show, and my opinion is that this show is amazing. I can only assume that the people who hate it the most were either bought in by hype, which often disappoints, or are fan-boys and fan-girls of the Tolkein world and don't like the fact that someone other than Tolkein wrote a whole new chapter to the story.Me, I'm a barely-casual film & TV Show watcher. I probably watch a new TV Series about once a year, and a maximum of 5 films a year. So on the rare occasions I do watch something, I want to be entertained, and this I found to be very entertaining.

It's by far not the instant magic one felt with the original LOTR but I'm starting to feel optimistic about maybe getting there. I hope they can keep the pace going in this directions. As an ardent Tolkien fan I have so many issues with this show that to list them, after only 3 episodes, would be a longer read than the appendices the show has the rights to.But I could overlook them. The costume designs, the dire script, the juvenile dialogue. It would be difficult and frustrating, but it could be done, if it were not for 3 insurmountable obstacles:1) Anachronisms.The random insertion of events into the 2nd Age that in some cases upend pivotal events in the 1st Age that brought about its closure, and in others disturb the continuity into established events in the 3rd Age. And, as an insult, these anachronisms add nothing to the flow of the narrative of the show itself.Sloppy writing.2) The timeline.Where is the sense in squeezing the events into one lifespan? Many of the principle characters are immortal. They could have told the story with a different timeline each season and still had all the elves in it as carry-throughs to bind the narrative.We've already met Elendil and Isildur and Sauron has yet to (blatantly) make an appearance, yet alone craft his rings. They were forged 1600 years before Isildur was even born.3 and half thousand years of history crushed into one lifetime?Very sloppy writing.3) Galadriel.Cannot stand her. She is horrific. At this point the wisest and most insightful of Tolkien's creations should be ruling her own land. She and her husband had already founded the city of Ost In Edhil in Eregion, left there and went on their way to founding that other great elf realm of Lothlorien.Instead she's a petulant, arrogant, entitled blowhard in her own great nephew's army.What?Why?It's even more galling as I love Morfydd Clark. But Galadriel has me rooting for the orcs.A show where I actively want the main character to come unstuck has a big problem in my eyes.And that problem is extremely sloppy writing.Looks pretty, great musical score, interesting to see them tackling the birth of Mordor.But no.I hope Sauron (sorry, Halbrand) kills them all.

From the beginning to the end Amazon is paying homage to Tolkien and huge respect to them for this!

I have to say, I went into this without watching anything. I avoided the YouTube videos, the articles, the interviews and as much as I could. I went in with just my love and knowledge of the books and the PJ movies. And I have to say, I was very disappointed. A good example that Amazon simply doesn't care about the lore or anything is looking at one of the 1st established characters. Finrod. His story is one so close to the core of Tolkien's work, that one of the characters Finrod dies defending is on Tolkien's gravestone. Finrod doesn't die screaming while being hugged by an orc as people behind him simply wave their sword back and forth. He wasn't on some quest to hunt down Sauron. Amazon throwing this key story to the side so they could make up a fan fiction revenge story for Galadriel is a great example of how they want to bastardize Tolkien's work. I'm not going to sugar coat my review because a few scenes look nice. For every one good environmental shot, they ruin it with a dozen mishaps with everything from poor acting, to making it so you can loudly hear Elrond clumsily walk through the forest (amazon literally added loud footsteps, to an elf), to the armors looking cheap and often plastic (they even added printed "armor" designs on the shirts). You can tell that Amazon doesn't care. I would normally wonder along the lines of: Did they not know how important Finrod is? Or do they simply don't care and want to make fan fiction? Well, we got our answer, its both. They don't care and they didn't do proper research. Such a missed opportunity.

But episode 1 and 2 are filled with boring dialogue, plot with little direction, and actors that take "Elvish" to mean to talk monotone and move like statues. I didn't feel empathy for any character, or scared, or angry. I just felt bord. It is a bad sign when I started making "Rocky Horror" style callbacks at a movie I have never seen before. If they aren't going to introduce conflict, they could at least preform a musical number.I will probably watch episode 3, and if I don't feel anything on that I probably will stop watching the series.

This is a fun, adventurous, character focused take on stories during the second age. Some stories are changed and backgrounds are expanded on. But this is a combination of creating a more entertaining show, and making the characters more interesting. Having watched the first two episodes I am really excited to see where the show goes. I expect that the overarching history laid out by Tolkien will stay largely unchanged due to the focus of the show being about individual characters.It would seem that many people are upset about the changes but aside from a few specific events most of Tolkien's histories are huge amounts of time and largely unspoken of. It is perfectly acceptable to fill these voids with stories and characters that existed within the period as long as the known events occur with some level of accuracy with the allowance of the specific media constraints.

I think it will grow into its story as a little disjointed to start with and many will just be lost in the detail.

First of all, lets ignore all the lore butchering. The Movies also weren't exactly beacons of lore purity either, but ignoring that and focusing on it being it's "own thing". It's dull, boring and just straight up bad. Half of the actors can't act. The dialogue is incredibly cringy. The set pieces scream cheap CGI half the time. And a lot of the costumes feel like something out of The CW. There is a woman wearing scale armor, though when it zooms in, you can see the creases in her shirt. It's not scale, it's just a tight shirt with a scale pattern painted on.I mentioned dialogue - going deeper into that, they talk like it's some sort of Marvel garbage. It's so incredibly bad. I can't believe people might actually like this trash.

Apparently the makers of this show spent so much on costumes and FX that they didn't have much for the writers. I could have written a stronger story with a set of D&D dice. I watched the whole first season hoping it would get better, but it just kept getting worse.Galadriel is absolutely horrible. The actress doesn't do her character justice, but again, you can't blame her when the writing is so atrocious. I know the writers are limited in what they're allowed to use, but come on. If you're going to make up stuff, at least make sure it doesn't actually contradict any of the lore. For example, Galadriel and Celeborn are married at this point. Where is he? Their daughter is Elrond's future wife.Even if I weren't just some nerd whining about how the show doesn't align with the canon, the story just isn't compelling. My husband put it perfectly - it's like someone wanted to have people in a soap opera LARP. Not worth the watch.

Extremely weak, and I'm not talking about the actors or any dark elves. In this case, it's clear that the issue lies with the script and direction. They're taking it in a direction that makes the whole thing feel like a cheap soap opera, despite the visually stunning production. Kudos to the costume designers and cinematography team, but unfortunately, the directors and writers should be replaced - but the damage is already done.They really think they can rewrite stories better than Tolkien? I have to say, I went into this without watching anything. I avoided the YouTube videos, the articles, the interviews and as much as I could. I went in with just my love and knowledge of the books and the PJ movies. And I have to say, I was very disappointed. A good example that Amazon simply doesn't care about the lore or anything is looking at one of the 1st established characters. Finrod. His story is one so close to the core of Tolkien's work, that one of the characters Finrod dies defending is on Tolkien's gravestone. Finrod doesn't die screaming while being hugged by an orc as people behind him simply wave their sword back and forth. He wasn't on some quest to hunt down Sauron. Amazon throwing this key story to the side so they could make up a fan fiction revenge story for Galadriel is a great example of how they want to bastardize Tolkien's work. I'm not going to sugar coat my review because a few scenes look nice. For every one good environmental shot, they ruin it with a dozen mishaps with everything from poor acting, to making it so you can loudly hear Elrond clumsily walk through the forest (amazon literally added loud footsteps, to an elf), to the armors looking cheap and often plastic (they even added printed "armor" designs on the shirts). You can tell that Amazon doesn't care. I would normally wonder along the lines of: Did they not know how important Finrod is? Or do they simply don't care and want to make fan fiction? Well, we got our answer, its both. They don't care and they didn't do proper research. Such a missed opportunity.

ipc-html-content-inner-div: It's as if there are two different streams out there. One is streaming to a group with a romanticized idea of Tolkien's vision that no studio would ever be able to achieve. They hold Peter Jackson's version as perfection, whereas if you were to truly watch it again, you would find many of the same flaws in his masterpiece, and many of the same controversies they find in Rings of Power.The other is streaming to a group who is hungry for LoTR lore, and are willing to allow artists other than themselves interpret Tolkien lore ... and are ecstatic in what they see. This is also a visual and storytelling masterpiece like Jackson's with it's own pacing, it's own writing, it's own atmosphere, and it's own interpretation. Soak it in ... you won't be sorry.

It's simply great to finally see a visual depiction of what was in our mind all along while reading all the books telling stories of middle earth. ipc-title__text: Do not be quick to deal out death in judgment
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I made an account just to make a review.The hatred of this show is very sad to me. I'm staggered we have the chance for a show like this, especially from Amazon.I ask people give this show the grace they'd wish to get if they made one. It's lovely! One of my favorites. Impressive acting; remarkable filming and effects; characters and story are deeply thought-out. It is not Peter Jackson Lord of the Rings. But it is better than the Hobbit.For inspiring story and noble themes to so boldly flow from the most expensive TV show in history amazes me. There is no lewdness, no profanity, which speaks to the effect of Tolkien and the care for his work the makers show. Beautifully done.I greatly enjoy Kazad Dum, and I am continually impressed to find the writers searched out the lore and wielded it impressively.All to say, enjoy this show, and I hope people don't scare Amazon off from doing something praiseworthy. We are a spoiled fan-base and forget the dark days before the Lord of the Rings movie trilogy.

ipc-title__text: How can we be so boring?
ipc-html-content-inner-div: What the original LOTR did in 10 minutes (the intro to the Fellowship) Rings of Power has tried to accomplish in almost 20 hours of television.We already know what's going to happen, we have no clue how the rings are made or really what they do...it's just characters we don't really care about talking about things we already know.Nothing feels real either. The threat of the orcs is such an afterthought to all of this. There's no quest or an understanding of what the goal is. All we know is that there is an evil lurking and something needs done about it. How silly. These writers get the award for the most boring story line in the history of television.There's no magic, there's no emotion, there's nothing real to this at all. It's just talking and more talking and more talking. The spiders looked great though.

And all of a sudden queen regent decides to call everyone back to the palace and you say "ok sure". So you go to the palace and queen regent starts to rant about how fool the decision they gave a couple minutes ago and as she gets emotional every second at the peak of the speech Galadriel pops up from the curtains like a talk show.You would think "Man, did they just sneak the Galadriel behind the Numenor just to mock with me? ipc-title__text: Disappointing show, especially with all the hype and money spent

There are very few original thoughts and the ones that are original don't make much sense or are not explained. So many lines and scenes are taken from the movies with small adjustments and of course different actors. I'm no lawyer, but this seems like plagiarism.Most of the series feels like a cheap soap opera my mom had on the boob tube after school when we were less fortunate and had only one tv. I had flashbacks and during some episodes had to take breaks. Some were boring and I found myself either falling asleep and having to restart it or having to rewind as my mind wandered. Those two shows look so much better visually, have script and lines way leaps and bounds above this one, and the actors are a ton better.In summary, the show is far below average. Did they take experience and complete body of work into account before hiring? Or did Amazon look for the lowest wages seeker?This show reminds one of the answer by USA astronaut John Glen when asked how he felt while sitting in a space rocket capsule during the countdown for launch: "I felt exactly how you would feel if you were getting ready to launch and knew you were sitting on top of 2 million parts - all built by the lowest bidder..."

ipc-title__text: Guilty of being boring, which is the worst crime of all
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Like many others, I do not want to sound like a brainless reviewer who crucified this show before it even aired. However, all the people who said this was going to be a mess before even watching the show were completely right. It is a mess. I am LOTR fan. I read the books, I watched the films and I extremely enjoyed both. I admire Tolkien because of what he created, not only because the world he invented but also because of how he mastered the language to convey such a story. I admire PJ and his team because they were able to adapt the books in such a way that conveyed the same message but translated into something modern audiences were able to relate to. However, I am no expert on middle-earth lore, and therefore I cannot judge this show based on its fidelity on the original source material. I do not care either. This show did not have a complete trilogy as source material, but you should not need them to write a good show. Just a good understanding of the world, the language and the message. The show is boring. The storylines are predictable. The characters are not interesting, they are not fully developed and have almost no agency. The dialogue lacks any of the profundity and poetry that characterizes TLOR. And when they try to replicate Tolkien's poetry the result is just cheap and cheesy. There are even continuity mistakes throughout the episodes, and I am not talking about continuity and consistency regarding the original material. They are incapable of keeping continuity within their original storylines. Nothing that happens makes any sense. Most of it is just boilerplate. Filler. In the first season of a show. There is no rhythm, no mystery. The viewer cannot even theorize what it is going to happen in the season using as clues what they watch episode by episode because everything is just too stupid. Cinematography is great but not that great. Visuals are good but not brilliant. In fact, sometimes is a little bit uncanny. Everything is too bright. It does not matter the time of the day, the place or the weather, the lightning is always the same. The costume design is awful and there is no thought behind it. Character motivation is conspicuous by its absence. The show is a travesty. I do not care about lore or being faithful to the extreme to the source material. But if I am going to invest an hour per episode in a show, it better be at least entertaining. And The Rings of Power is not.

ipc-title__text: Not Tolkien, but not bad "fan" Fiction either

Simply put it can not claim any legitimate connection to Tolkien without being bad, if it stood on its own it could be great.The Ship of Theseus is a thought experiment that asks whether an entity that has had all of its original components replaced remains the same entity, but theses are not even original componentsThe entire time I'm watching, thinking of how much I would love to see what she actually did. Learning from Yavanna and Aule making lembas with Melian the Maiar =/ she has always been my favorite character in all of fiction and this feels wrong.FIRST OFF: Galadriel did not even gain that name till she met her lover Celeborn later in the first age -
elves have a complex culture of naming which is again ignored, they get three, 1 given at birth by the father (Artanis), 2nd acquired from the mother (Nerwen) meaning man-maiden referring to her height and strength, and a 3rd aquired through life (Galadriel)there is a point where one of the now bald elves says: "ya"..which is funny but wrong.The elves are part of a culture that values form over function, they are graceful and ethereal in their androgynous beauty. They live long and fight rare, they would not have short hair and shaved sideburns, and doing so does not assist in conveying the nuance of that loreThe young elves in the beginning "bullying" the Princess of Noldor (unlikley) are in Tolkien's world about 20 given their stature (elves physically age slower), her brother calls her by a name she has not yet acquired this scene is incorrect.Lady Galadriel breeches 6 feet in height- and does not in the show.The aesthetics lack grit, all the costumes look brand new- not a thread out of place, the CG is overwhelming.Frost troll fight seen look very unrealistic and cringeworthy- nothing but a flashy show of power that could have been executed far better.Hobbits, (Harfoots, Stoors or Fallohides) do not exist at this time in middle earthGaladriel needing to be saved by a human man is 100% garbage and super cliché and annoying.What the show does right:
She is shown to be wise are insightful beyond her years, almost a savant of elves.

ipc-title__text: Guilty of being boring, which is the worst crime of all
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Like many others, I do not want to sound like a brainless reviewer who crucified this show before it even aired. However, all the people who said this was going to be a mess before even watching the show were completely right. It is a mess. I am LOTR fan. I read the books, I watched the films and I extremely enjoyed both. I admire Tolkien because of what he created, not only because the world he invented but also because of how he mastered the language to convey such a story. I admire PJ and his team because they were able to adapt the books in such a way that conveyed the same message but translated into something modern audiences were able to relate to. However, I am no expert on middle-earth lore, and therefore I cannot judge this show based on its fidelity on the original source material. I do not care either. This show did not have a complete trilogy as source material, but you should not need them to write a good show. Just a good understanding of the world, the language and the message. The show is boring. The storylines are predictable. The characters are not interesting, they are not fully developed and have almost no agency. The dialogue lacks any of the profundity and poetry that characterizes TLOR. And when they try to replicate Tolkien's poetry the result is just cheap and cheesy. There are even continuity mistakes throughout the episodes, and I am not talking about continuity and consistency regarding the original material. They are incapable of keeping continuity within their original storylines. Nothing that happens makes any sense. Most of it is just boilerplate. Filler. In the first season of a show. There is no rhythm, no mystery. The viewer cannot even theorize what it is going to happen in the season using as clues what they watch episode by episode because everything is just too stupid. Cinematography is great but not that great. Visuals are good but not brilliant. In fact, sometimes is a little bit uncanny. Everything is too bright. It does not matter the time of the day, the place or the weather, the lightning is always the same. The costume design is awful and there is no thought behind it. Character motivation is conspicuous by its absence. The show is a travesty. I do not care about lore or being faithful to the extreme to the source material. But if I am going to invest an hour per episode in a show, it better be at least entertaining. And The Rings of Power is not.

ipc-title__text: A Perspective on Adaptation and Film Criticism
ipc-html-content-inner-div: As a cinephile with a deep love for the craft of filmmaking, I've often wrestled with the tension between source material and its adaptations. My passion for the cinematic medium stems not from a childhood spent reading the epics of Harry Potter, Game of Thrones, or The Lord of the Rings, but from immersing myself in the art and process of filmmaking. Over time, I've come to appreciate that a story's impact often depends on how it's first encountered-whether as a book, a film, or another form of media.Take Watchmen, for example. My introduction to its world was through Zack Snyder's film, a version I adored despite the backlash from fans of Alan Moore's graphic novel. When I eventually read the source material, I could see its brilliance but found my preference for the film unshaken. This isn't a lack of appreciation for the original; rather, it's a testament to the power of cinema and the meticulous artistry behind it-elements that, for me, surpass the written word.This perspective underscores a broader issue in how adaptations are received. Too often, fans of the source material approach adaptations with rigid expectations, leading to knee-jerk criticism when those expectations aren't met. Consider the practice of one-star reviews: a reductive, spiteful trend that undermines the effort, artistry, and technical achievement of filmmaking. When reviewing a car, for instance, one doesn't dismiss it outright for superficial reasons like its appearance. Why, then, should a film-created over months of grueling work-be reduced to a single star because it didn't align with someone's ideal vision of the source material?This brings me to the broader problem of modern film criticism. In an era of online reviews, platforms like Rotten Tomatoes and IMDb have become saturated with biased, uninformed opinions. Whether it's the racially charged backlash against The Little Mermaid or the dismissal of adaptations like The Rings of Power for perceived deviations from their literary origins, the critique often strays far from the film's actual merits. Such reviews are not only unhelpful but harmful to the art form itself, dissuading creators from taking risks or expanding beloved franchises in new directions.It's crucial to evaluate films holistically, acknowledging their achievements even when we may not connect with their stories or performances. A film's technical craftsmanship-its cinematography, editing, set design, and visual effects-should be recognized and celebrated. While The Rings of Power may not be a perfect series, it succeeds in evoking the grandeur and practical artistry of Peter Jackson's original LOTR trilogy, elements that were often lost amidst the CGI-heavy spectacle of The Hobbit films.Yes, some dialogue and performances might fall short, but even LOTR-hailed as a masterpiece-has its share of campy moments. Criticism should be measured, constructive, and rooted in an appreciation for the sheer labor that goes into creating cinematic worlds. After all, adaptation is not about replication; it's about interpretation, and that interpretation deserves to be judged on its own merits.Take Dune, for instance. While Frank Herbert's novel is an unparalleled literary experience, Denis Villeneuve's adaptation embraces the strengths of cinema to bring its sprawling universe to life. Even if I dislike certain elements, like Timothée Chalamet's performance, I can still recognize and respect the film's ambition and artistry.In the end, it's time for audiences to shift their perspective on reviews. Opinions are valid, but they must be distinguished from credible critique. Thoughtless ratings, born of personal grievances or resistance to change, do a disservice to creators and the medium itself. Let's move beyond our own biases, celebrate innovation, and foster a culture that values storytelling in all its forms. Only then can we ensure that the art of adaptation continues to thrive.

As a lifelong fan of the world of Middle-earth, I was eager to see how The Rings of Power would tackle Tolkien's rich tapestry. From the very first episode, I was blown away. Each episode is packed with tension, heroism, and moments of quiet beauty. It's clear that a lot of care went into ensuring the show fits into the grand mythology, and the result is an experience that pulls you in from start to finish.The casting is nothing short of perfect. Each character is not only well-acted but also brings a unique perspective that feels perfectly suited to the Middle-earth universe. The chemistry and interactions among the characters give a depth that makes the world feel lived-in and authentic. The performances are as layered and complex as the characters themselves, making you invested in their journeys and fates.Visually, The Rings of Power is stunning. The breathtaking landscapes, intricate sets, and seamless special effects make for a feast for the eyes that's a joy to watch. The show's production value is immense, and it feels like no expense was spared in bringing Middle-earth to life.Overall, The Rings of Power is a fantastic addition to the Lord of the Rings universe. It's everything you could hope for in a return to Middle-earth-epic, moving, and unforgettable. This series deserves a long and prosperous future, not only because it's a beautifully crafted show, but also because it reaffirms the enduring magic of Tolkien's world. If you're a fan of the books or the games, don't miss it!

ipc-title__text: This is an affront to the name of Tolkien!

These stories have always been about good vs. Evil, but they've also always been about the heros, and not about the villains. I don't want to watch a show about Sauron and the thousands of horrible things he does. I want a show that's focused on the heros, and that tells their story. The Marvel franchise has more lovable characters in it, and it's based on comic books. The world that Tolkien brought to life was vibrant, compelling, and full of light and laughter. Peter Jackson, Fran Walsh and Philippa Boyens are the only other writers who have proven themselves worthy of telling Tolkien's tales on the big screen. Their absence is felt sharply in this series.

Someone was given too much power they couldn't back up with talent. Or too much money was siphoned out.
