ipc-title__text: I want but I can not
ipc-html-content-inner-div:
I had high hopes, but in the end it was a disappointment:
-Poor and empty script.-They try to make epic scenes where there are none no matter how much music and slow motion they play
-Simple battles
-Absurd and boring scenes (not to mention the swimming scene that Galadriel does), the plot of the hobbits does not contribute anything, it produces drowsiness.With all the money they have invested (they always said this for a long time) something more entertaining could have been done, the battles of chapter 6 seem medium budget, at times it seems like a lot of people, and then 4 villagers against 4 orcs.We will have to keep the Peter Jackson movies.

No sign of magical world of Tolkien. And I don't mean seeing magic, but the mystical feeling by reading it.Lord of the ring movies were loyal to that basics, by playing musics where needed and avoid it where it is not. That applies to strong speeches and romantic scene as well. Here in rings of power, there are too much unnecessary dialogues and lame romantic scenes. Regardless of having a great story at hand, the storytelling in the show is about the average and Bad directing is obvious.Cinematography is good but could be better. Again it does not present the world that JRRT has introduced.As for the cast, acting are acceptable but actors are badly selected and regardless of them giving their best performance, still don't fit.So, overall, not worthy of a Tolkien work.

ipc-title__text: So far it's great but not for light hearted LOTR fans
So much production value - so little heart
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I went into this blind, having only seen the movies by peter Jackson. I really wanted to give Rings of Power a chance.......and whilst this show truly has incredibly production value with great CGI, stunning locations and more or less good acting the show simply has no heart. There's no one you root for, no one you hate...it makes you feel....nothing.The dialogues are forced, random and don't seem to fit the characters and even by episode 5 I have no clue what the hell this story should be about - it's all over the place, huge plot changing decisions are being made within heartbeats and we skip forward or switch storyline.The only thing this show made me feel is flashbacks to what shipwreck season 8 of GOT was. I feel very bad for all the people that worked hard on this show.... I wish the writers and producers would have put more effort in it to make it pay off.

After more than half the season (writing this after ep5) this show has gone from "wierd, but pretty" to "pretty, but awful".The visuals alone cannot make up for the poor writing, stiff acting and lack of pace. But the worst thing is that they have the most epic and fully fleshed out world and they still think that a group of "Hollywood-writers" could make it better. Imagine the sheer hubris of the writer(s) that came up with the whole mithril sub-plot? It's so completely out of place and contrived that it's pretty much unwatchable at this point.The only thing this show has going for it is the artwork, and that's far from enough for a show with a budget as big as the gdp of a small nation.

A few months later after reading the LOTR, Silmarillion & Unfinished Tales of Numenor and Middle-Earth I have dowgraded my rating for this series because it was very badly scripted and not true to the Tolkien books. My original and foolishly optimistic review was as follows:- I have read the Lord of the Rings books and watched all of the films so I am a big fan. It's great to be able to carry on enjoying the fantasy thanks to Amazon. The special effects are really good and the island of Numenor looks stunning. There are a number of sub plots going on in parallel which keeps things interesting. Women are given a more dominant role and there are more ethnic groups which I like. The Harfoots being the most common race of hobbit are loveable characters. The mystery visitor with them is intriguing and leaving everyone guessing. The dwarves characters are good. The humans seem insecure and divided. The elven characters Elrond and Galadriel are very poor. There is a mystery about who the leader of the orcs (Adar) is. Is it Sauron? Maybe not. Is Sauron hidden amongst the existing characters or yet to appear?

After episode 4 I think I'm done watching for now. As a book fan and original trilogy fan I've gotten over the numerous lore breaks. The writing and dialogue are just terrible and pointless. I know nothing of the lore of Game of Thrones but the show writing (at least for a good chunk of it) is really good.I know you can look up the writers and directors and I don't know much about there background but they were definitely not fit for the job. I'm in neither of these backgrounds but for the scale of this show the best should have been picked and it's certainly not the case here.At this point I'd either want to see the writing crew restructured and this season retconned and season 2 writing a new story. Maybe even just cancel the show for the sake of Tolkien. I'm gonna keep following but by listening to the Tolkien enthusiast go over it on YouTube which feels like a better use of my time then watching this show.

ipc-title__text: Like a Ren Faire skit, but worse
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Atrocious acting. Horrible writing. A main character you not only can't relate to, but you actually grow to hate well before the end of the first episode. A plot ripoff of the original LotR except done by people who apparently just graduated film school with a D- average grade. The show is supposedly going to last 5 seasons, and the only reason I think it might go that long is because the only people watching it plan on continuing to make fun of how dreadful it is or mine it for memes. Every big named celebrity associated with the CATS fiasco ran away as fast as they could to save their careers, but these actors are soon to be doomed no-names stuck for years now by contract in a project they can't hope to redeem and will become box office poison for a decade or more.

ipc-title__text: Great CGI, but lack pace and story.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: It's a beautiful show, but with no soul... inexpressive characters, devoid of charisma... but the true miss is the world, Tolken created LOTR with such a attention in detail that all the readers could imagine the place, feel the walking distance, the food, clouth, and all the things important in such a journey... all of that is missing in the Rings of Power, the Characters doesn't look real, and make a bunch of dumb decision that it's miracle that they could be alive in the end of the episode.In this first 2 hours episode there's a lack of focus, the story keep jumping from place to place that I think the showrunners spend all the money in great location, trying to make a waterfall scene, a blizzard scene, a meteour scene, etc and forget the dialogues... so after spend 2 hours I really don't care for any of the character, or I understand what is the plot because there's so many places/characters happening the same time, but without any developing that it's impossible to care... If one movie of Lord of the Rings has 3 hours, and could show all that chars, plots, scenes, it's really disturbing that a 2 hours episode doesn't desenvolved any conection with the show.

Well the show is here!! It's not a Peter Jackson film, but that's okay! It's a adaptation. It's a show that's nit made with a A list production. However, it has potential and the cast truly isn't that bad. We have gotten SPOILED on getting a high production due to games on X box. I grew up on C or D syfy movies 🎬 Abd they have a cult following. This adaptation will have following until Peter Jackson gets up does another version backed by A list production. It's slow, dialogs can be sharper written. And the editing.. well. But, it's a,good story. And the location shots are breathtaking to say the least. Tolkien wouldn't mind this version. More fans will buy his books and start up fan groups.

The graphics and fights are good. The characters though are bland and predictable. I've watch both episodes and found it cringe such as the Mary sue that shouldn't have been fighting in the second era to the weak male elves that were originally written to be great warrior. I have rated this serie 10/10 not because it deserves it , because 6.5 is way too low for unknown reasons , so i can balance this absurd rating .The serie is not bad at all , it actually gave me lord of the rings vibes since first minutes watching , it a slow start for sure but i see a big oppurtunity that this TV Show can be one the best series of all time , in my opinion after watching first 2 epsoides it deserves 8.5 Rating So far .-Maybe people are comparing it to other series , but you cannot judge a serie from first 2 epsoides , i actually like this slow start , Game of thrones started really slow aswell but it was worth it at the end .

This does not "feel" like a tolkien story; two episodes in. The characters are hollow and lore breaking, but lets see what happens, first two episodes does not paint a pretty picture thou.There was nothing that made me care about the characters, nothing memorable in the first episodes ....The dialog is really strange, like some of the sentences Galadriel says make her sound like a 30year old woman and not a century old immortal elf.If you compare this with House of Dragons, I remember great events that is affecting the characters in that show in two episodes...In this nothing happens in the first two episodes ...the CGI is beautiful thou .... Then I watched episode 7 and was not lost one single moment in the episode; I should had tons of questions, but I guess nothing really happens in those 3 episodes.

After seeing the trailer I still didn't know what to expect. But the first episode caught me from the beginning. The cinematography is great and the CGI looks better than the Hobbit to my opinion. At least the big budget is not wasted. That was something I was afraid for.Not all of the cast is familiar to me but also the overall acting is great until now.I am glad we can enjoy more stories of Middle Earth again even if it may not completely true to the works of Tolkien. ipc-title__text: I despise Lord of the Rings
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I've watched one Lord of the Rings movie and I absolutely hated it. Some friends talked my wife and I into watching it. Don't mind the 1 and 2 star reviews.Some had preconceived ideas, that's their fault.Let the story take you away, and enjoy yourself!Great fun, fabulous production, cast is great.I tried not to see much of the trailers and hype before the show started, and that paid off.If anyone is hoping that this show will be like the vision that they have in their mind of how to do this, good luck with that.But if you love Tolkien and respect that this production is carrying the torch which Peter Jackson lit 20 years ago...

Never trust critics. It's Christmas time so I went to buy some stuff on amazon and decided to see give this a see if it really is as bad as they say since I had prime trial going. This series been panned for years and it wasn't until now that I've watched this. Went through both season in a single weekend. Fantastic stuff. Even better than LotR movies which were a bit sleep inducing, especially Hobbit trilogy. Even better than Game of Thrones series, yes. Story and characters are plentiful and almost never a dull moment, some actors are great off the bat, others I started to like as show continued. Great acting. So give it a try.

This is brilliant and as an avid reader and a fan of the films, am in love with this series. I think Amazon spent every penny on this .The films are fantastic but revolves around the story of good guys and bad guys and not in depthThis series fills in so many gaps, their back story of middle earth and it's inhabitantsThings you merely thought you knew from the films are cemented on the screen, it's not massively over complicated or extremely high, but it what tv and film was made for .For the love of this series I can't wait for another season and I really hope they get to do all 5 season.

The second season of "The Rings of Power" was fantastic! The effects were super impressive and truly epic, bringing Middle-earth to life in a visually stunning and enchanted way. The character development deepened the story, allowing for more intricate relationships and dynamics. The pacing was well-balanced, building suspense and intrigue throughout the episodes. Overall, it expanded beautifully on the foundation set in the first season, leaving fans eager for more. The combination of rich lore, breathtaking visuals, and epic storytelling made it a standout season, filled with unforgettable moments.

As a devout fan of Tolkien's masterpieces for over two decades, I feel compelled to express my profound disappointment in the recent adaptation, "The Rings of Power." This series strays disastrously from the meticulous and nuanced storytelling that Peter Jackson achieved in his iconic trilogy. The producers have unfortunately missed the mark with "The Silmarillion," failing to capture the essence and grandeur of Tolkien's world. What should have been a carefully crafted homage has been reduced to a spectacle of tacky Hollywood tropes and mediocrity. The series lacks the reverence and depth that the source material demands. The result is an ill-conceived rendition that dilutes the rich narrative for the sake of visual opulence. While the cast delivered commendable performances, the series overall should be considered a blemish on the legacy of a beloved epic. This production is regrettably a far cry from the greatness it aspired to be.

All I can say is I am thoroughly disappointed. The magic of Tolkien, and even Jackson, is no where to be seen except in small glimmers. It was these small glimmers that led me to hope and to defend the show. I watched with hopeful anticipation as the story unfolded in both season 1 and season 2. I can no longer defend this show. It is a travesty and a disaster to the name of J. R. R. Tolkien. They have taken beloved characters like Galadriel, Gil-Galad, Elrond, and Gandalf and have diminished them to their lowest point. I cannot stress enough how disappointing this show is. My greatest wish is that the fans would rise up and cancel this show as it needs to end. We need director with love and vision for the true and authentic Lord of the Rings. The only positives to this show, and the only reason it even gets a 4/10, is because the cinematography was fantastic and the Sauron arc was interesting. Ultimately, this is not enough to continue watching this show. Please do better Amazon. We need better. Make the right choice and end this.

Season 2 of this production, purportedly set in the rich and expansive Tolkien Universe, is nothing short of a colossal disappointment. The interactions between characters are not only irrational but also lack any semblance of coherence, leaving the audience bewildered and disconnected. The motivations driving the characters are skewed, their ambitions, flaws, and strengths poorly developed and inconsistent. This results in a narrative that feels disjointed and superficial, failing to engage the viewer on any meaningful level.The production team had an immense reservoir of material to draw from, given the depth and complexity of Tolkien's works. Yet, they seem to have squandered this opportunity, opting instead for a hollow and disrespectful adaptation that does little justice to the source material. The characters, who should be the heart and soul of the story, are reduced to mere caricatures, their actions and decisions often defying logic and reason. This lack of character development is a glaring flaw that undermines the entire narrative structure.Even though visually stunning with a lovely soundtrack, and tremendous praise to the costume team(s) the overarching storytelling and narrative design was appalling. Unfortunately, Season 2 of this production is a glaring example of how not to adapt a beloved literary universe. I found this a deeply unsatisfying viewing experience.

ipc-title__text: Spectacular production giving life to Tolkien's Lord of the Rings appendices with some misgivings
The Rings of Power: A Disappointing Adaptation of Tolkien's Second Age

ipc-html-content-inner-div: The Rings of Power, season 1 and 2: a bitter disappointment.The series worsened the problems already present in the first season: fragmented plot, underdeveloped characters, disappointing Sauron and too many deviations from the original works. The special effects do not redeem a weak script and an open ending that leaves a bitter taste in the mouth. A wasted opportunity to explore such a rich universe, but the plot is often confused and without a common thread, characters with little depth and unsatisfactory narrative developments, little fidelity to Tolkien, too many creative liberties that distort the fictional universe.In conclusion, a series that disappoints expectations and does not do justice to the world created by Tolkien.

ipc-title__text: Great visuals, but the storyline? Just meh!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Most of the time I had no clue what is going on. The whole storytelling is confusing and incoherent. I just couldnt keep up (I am no die hard LOTR Fan) and it was difficult to stay invested in the story. I wasnt bothered about any of the characters since none of them was portrayed in a likeable way.I only liked the settings and the overall visuals. They got better the longer the show went on.Well, the whole series could have been amazing because unlike the movies there is not certain time frame the whole story has to fit it. They could have taken all time in this world to develop the story properly but everything was executed poorly and the story told losely. And even though the story of the rings itself has SO damn much potential, it feels like the storyline is going nowhere. Also there are are quite a few plot holes.So overall I am not happy with the series and I just hope it gets better with season 2. First episode started messy again and had me all confused in the beginning, but the visuals have improved.

Like probably the majority of people that watch this show i never read the books and only saw the movies. I thought it was quite entertaining and i wanted to know how it continues. I read that it's not 100% faithful to the Lord of the Rings lore ... yeah whatever, who cares. If you are not a diehard Tolkin fan that reads his books twice a year and follows the lore like it's a religion, i don't think you will notice or care. If you watched the movies and liked them you will probably like this show. Visually it's pretty good and most actors fit their roles. So don't pay to much attention to the lore fanatics and just enjoy an entertaining tv show.I hope there will be a season 3.

Doesn't deserve the nickname Lord of the Rings! It has nothing to do with Tolkien's books at all. The entire plot has no rhyme or reason. The elves are just stupid and totally annoying... terrible, just terrible... the only good thing: it looks good! But the script is simply the worst thing I've ever seen!After the middle of the second season, I'll stop now. I really thought you couldn't screw up Lord of the Rings, but Amazon somehow managed to do it.In summary:
Dialogues: 1/10
Screenplay: 1/10
Lore: 1/10
Plot: 1/10
Logic: 1/10
Music: 7/10
Visual Effects: 7/10
Orcs: 6/10
Elves: 1/10Just a huge shame!

Amazon should've hired experienced writers who take composing in-depth, compelling, and captivating stories seriously. I understand the garden variety alibis pertaining to rights, timelines, etc. Payne & McKay have taken too many liberties and ignored such extensive material to be screwing up such a show. Their responsibility as writers should be to work WITH Tolkien scholars who have much more knowledge of the lore instead of making this their own.(que eye roll) Reusing dialogue from the trilogy every episode isn't an ode to the franchise, it's lazy, turning loved characters in cheap cosplay.

ipc-title__text: Want to love it but hard to watch it...
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Season 1 was quite okay but since its Season 2 now, a lot is expected to happen and 4 episodes in, it gets more boring and boring.The layout of the storylines were planted with good intentions but the storytelling part is lacking and seems pointless and out of place. The giant and the 2 harfoots scene seems extremely boring. Can never reach the heights of Frodo/Samwise and too many cliches in the storyline.Apart from that, Galadriel looks pretty lifeless and emotionless, awful acting by a mile. All the costumes, locations, and CGIs were on point but the storylines and actors were not exciting and lacking. Not to mention the lack of action and too much yapping in a ultra-budget series like this.There are so much opportunities to make this show way more interesting, adventurous, and exciting when you have the Middle Earth at your disposal. The characters did not get much development into the storyline with all these non-sense, getting-nowhere dialogues. Could've been so much better!

ipc-title__text: Should be better, despite being the most expensive show
ipc-html-content-inner-div: If the LOTR Trilogy is a 10 and the Hobbit Trilogy is a 7.5 then this would be around a 6. If it wasn't connected and this was a stand alone tv show then it would probably be a 7.5 as there are parts that are entertaining.The visuals and sound are still amazing and have breathtaking views. ipc-title__text: I think maybe I was supposed to watch the films first
Overall a visually pleasing, poorly executed, "loosely inspired by" not an adaptation of the events of the Second Age.
The forgot story or interesting characters
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Just finished the series and I would recommend to anyone to save your time and not bother.Any possible story or naunce is instead replaced with vague attempts to be poetic that are really just meaningless ramblings about "the light" and "the dark".Shows like this often don't put any justifiable motivation for "the bad guys", which can be okay, but this case was particularly bad. It felt like when planning the show they had two moments they cared about and included filler for the entire season in order to get to those spots.For a fantasy universe it was surprisingly uncreative. I know they're using an established series so there less room to move but part of the appeal of LOTR is the interesting universe. This world was tedious. It closer aligned to a glorified screensaver than an actual world you could be emersed in.Fair respect, the Harfoots were pretty decent, and the dwarves weren't bad. Anything with humans or elves was pretty much garbage.Quite disappointing. Don't waste your time.

ipc-title__text: Surprisingly good. Visually, it's an achievement.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: It looks incredible and the story flows well. That makes Rings of Power more than worth a watch. The Dwarves are fantastic, halflings are engaging despite their justified fears, Men are both evil or good & we finally see the Elves in their glorious past but well in danger of losing that glory. What more could one ask for? Plenty, according to some that went hyperbolic in their hate.Rings of Power doesn't deserve that hate. I've seen arguments from purists about how it doesn't fit the lore, however said lore in turn is sketchy and mostly the subject of LotR's appendices and not written as a dramatic narrative. I find I am less committed to finding fault when there isn't much of a real story to deviate from. That earns RoP a lot more breathing room in terms of the liberties it can take in my book.Personally speaking, there's more to take issue with for the narrative departures in the egregious Hobbit. Even LotR The Two Towers has significant story deviations that don't do the characters or the story justice, yet fans turn a blind eye there for some reason.So ignore the hate, keep an open mind & enjoy the show.

ipc-title__text: Did the writers use ChatGPT to write the screenplay?
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Did the writers use ChatGPT to write the screenplay?I knew something was wrong from the first few minutes when Galadriel's brother was trying to explain how boats float. I really tried and twisted my brain in knots trying to understand. The more I think about it, the more it seems like one of the weird explanations that ChatGPT generates.Despite really looking forward to the first episode, I fell asleep half-way through it. That was another warning sign.I finally made it through the whole first season. There were some scenes that tried really hard to be inspiring, poignant and deep with meaning. The writer just could not convince me.This is a pale facsimile, a knock-off product that missed the mark.

ipc-title__text: A slap in the face if every Tolkien fan
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This show itself could have been not that bad and the sets like Khazad dum or Numenor are awesome. The problem is that it chose to take on the Tolkien legacy, which it just can't. The pase is just bad, the characters are hollow with the exception of Helbrand who appears to be the only capable character if you rate their leadership-, social- and politic skills.Also it is just given that the most antisocial and revenge driven character, who even suggests a orc-genocide, is the good one?The music itself is good, but in the most scenes it just doesn't fit what you see. A lot of times I was like "ah the music says it's a mourning scene, but why should I care?".The dialogs are on a totally other level of writers incompetence, like a teen trying to sound deep.All in all I'd say this is my new Sharknado, seasoned with ridiculous amount of memberberries (reeeeeally cheap ones)

I just have to say it's really bland. I thought at first it's simply a slow burn, learning the characters and understanding their roles, however I found the only characters with any kind of depth are Adar and Durin.Everyone else just seems out of place, this is a big problem considering the main character is rather unlikeable. The rest of the characters, despite the insane budget, feel lost with odd costume and personality choices.By the end of the first season there isn't much to unpack to want to continue, at least for me, if this didn't have lord of the rings in it's name I can't help but wonder how much worse it could have done. It's a shame, the budget alone cannot not hold up it's faults.If you can move past the fact that this is lord of the rings, you may get something out of this and enjoy it for what it is, a mediocre fantasy adventure.

ipc-title__text: It's Mostly World-Building... Hopeful It's Worth It
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The reviews are not wrong. It's both beautiful and slow. So you could go either way.Those who think it's slow probably wanted to see more action, more magic, more intricate plot dynamics.Those who think it's beautiful appreciate the world building... the elves, the Numenorians, the orcs, Sauron, the rings...I'm of the latter.You see, during Lord of the Rings, and the Hobbit, we were thrust into a fight or flight situation in this magnificent Fantasy world. ipc-title__text: After three episodes, could care less about the characters

So, with no plot movement and too many threads, "Rings of Power" is just boring and confusing. After three episodes, I would expect to start to connect with one or more characters. Instead, I have not connected with any of the characters. In fact, I actually dislike the Galadriel character. She seems mad all the time. You would think after living as long as she has, she would be more at peace. I also think it is just bad writing when a character does something and the viewer cannot understand the motivation, or it just makes no sense to the viewer. For example, when Galadriel jumps off the ship in the middle of the ocean. Just didn't get it.

This series, let alone the basterdizarion of tolkiens masterworks, is a hard D- in every conceivable facet. The writing is dismal, the choreography is beyond childish, the characters are underdeveloped and beyond unlikeable. This entire project should have been scripted post principal photography had anyone working on this travesty had any inkling of artistic integrity, in either thier own work or tolkiens. Beyond shameful. Don't even concede a view to this irredeemable train wreck that makes game of thrones season 8 look like the Peter Jackson Trilogy. The only possible quality to be found anywhere in this entire billion dollar project is the landscape cgi (the only video effects that can rival the 20 years older forementioned trilogy as all creatures and orc cgi makes Kevin smiths Howard the duck look like Avatar) which is wasted on a narrative that has absolutely nothing to offer any viewer capable of critical thought. An absolute dumpster fire that should have canceled before before so much as a rumor of this shows existence was leaked for hype generation.

I Offer my sincerest gratitude to Amazon Studious for making millions of fan-dreams come true in our lifetimes with the brilliant work and hard-won excellence you forged in this intricate and time-honoured production. ipc-title__text: Would give a longer review but I had to wait a week....
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The environment looks good, music is great. The characters and story are terrible though. Shallow would describe them best. Barely anything happened in three episodes. What do we know about Galadriel so far? She is a warrior...and wants revenge. Arondir? He is a soldier...and in love with a human female. Nori? She is adventurous and headstrong...three hours of character development.Everything in this show is a mystery. What do the dwarves have in their box in episode 2? Don't know! Will have to see the rest of the show for that! What does Miriel mean when she says "The elf has arrived"? Don't know! Same thing! Who is that guy, that crashed down from the sky? Maybe later! Who is Sauron? How should I know!I feel like this show is the embodiment of the devolving the entertainment industry has suffered, since Marvel has become the new norm.

If you like me are tired of all the marvel-ified and GoT-ified shows out there and just want some proper fantasy without too much gore, violence, and today seemingly compulsory adult content then this is the show for you. It captures perfectly the feeling of older fantasy literature where the action is slower, story is first, and no forced unecessary nudity. This is what I have been missing in fantasy. I am also shocked by how well this show captures the feeling of the three LOTR movies without any overlapping actors or music. This is, in feeling, a lot closer to the LOTR movie adaptions than the hobbit ever was. It is not as fairytale as Tolkien's literature, and I am sad that the dwarf ladies are without beard and that the elves aren't constantly singing like in the books. But it is a great watch, both for weekend nights and as a comfort watch with a cup of tea.I have seen too many arguments that it is not following "canon", but neither does any other adaption. But no one flies up in arms about the lack of singing elves and the radical changes to the plot in the original LOTR, neither was there an attack on the hobbit movie trilogy despite it radically changing the entire genre of the story (some of us do complain about it to our friends though). This show is not further from canon than any other adaption, so don't let it keep you from watching a great fantasy show.

To have invested almost 2.5X more money just for the first TV season than was invested in all three of the movies combined, maybe I was expecting more? Yes, great film work, but there really isn't many actors to cheer on. Other than Galadriel, one lone female warrior, what do you have? There were so many characters and stories happening in the trilogy it was easy to be invested in their fate. In the tv series I found myself falling asleep many times. It has taken me six days and I still haven't completely finished the second episode yet. Is there a reason why there seems like there is no male heroes? Look at the top eight billings on the actors and six are women. Of the two male leads, one of them is a villain. I wanted this to be good so badly......

ipc-title__text: It's so exciting to get more LOTR after all this time
Amazing for what they have the rights to.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: With Amazon only having the rights to the trilogy, the Hobbit, and the appendices, but not to the Silmarillion or any of Tolkien's many extended works, it's impressive what they have done without breaking the rules. With that said, I have only a few minor grievances, but overall the show is beautiful, it looks more like a film than a series. It is amazingly acted and I have found myself liking the characters that I had reservations about before seeing the show. Bear McCreary created a wonderful score, and the production level is insane. The set and costume designs are 99.9% of the time phenomenal with only one exception (Celebrimbor). There are also deep lore references that the book fans or any of those who have studied the appendices will appreciate. The Harfoots, however, seem slightly unnecessary as of now, but I'll wait till the end of the season to make my ultimate decision on that part of the story.

This show has it all - visuals you'll want as wallpapers, costumes you'll want to cosplay, characters you'll fall in love with and cry when they die (spoiler alert lol), music you'll listen to constantly on Spotify, and stories that will inspire you and bring you heartbreak and joy. It's just getting started, so strap in and enjoy the ride :)About me: I'm a 20+ year fan of the books, Tolkien's writing and the movies. I studied literature and spent my weekends reading dissertations on Tolkien's work. I'm a total LOTR nerd, complete with every boardgame and digital game. My family watches the trilogy three times a year and uses the music as dnd background music. So I'm so excited to return to middle earth.Am I disappointed they don't have the rights to much of the stories that are needed to make certain characters more relatable? Absolutely. But I'm choosing to have faith in the creators, actors and crew that they will deliver a wonderful show that will further the fandom for the better!This season one is going to be amazing! I just wish Amazon released everything at once. I think it's detrimental for the show to only have an episode at a time.

ipc-title__text: This is GREAT! - How can it have such a low rating?!

I would recommend you to start watching the series with a clear mind and no expectation. Just get on and enjoy the ride!The Visuals are stunning and the story is great! Can't wait to see more!The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power gets a 10 out of 10 from me!

Really boring. I got through the first 25mins of the first episode and started skipping forward 10 secs here and there. The dialogue is basic and predictable. The age of the characters plus this basic way of story telling makes it clear this show is intended for people below 17yrs of age. This is somewhat confirmed by showrunners who said they didn't want to make it "too scary" because they intend for kids to watch it. The way they keep changing from one area and people of middle earth to another also keeps the show and plot basic. I've always loved fantasy. It is a shame to see a story appropriated and so much time and money spent on it for it to be reduced to kids tv series.

A perfect show...for my children. The characters are very child friendly and two dimensional. Especially Galadriel. She is like a Disney character , Young, brave, very childish-looking and with zero charisma. At least The kids are cheering like crazy when she swings her Sword.Middle earth is threatened by the Dark lord Sauron and its up to Galadriel to hunt him down.The visuals and music are good. But the show isn't true to the books at all. The creators have disrespected Tolkien in every way possible here. The disregard for the original work is shockingly ignorant.Good thing Amazon got The Terminal list to watch instead of this garbage.

If we attend only the technical part of the show it stand alone in the very best of tv entire history.It is an evidently thorough masterpiece in design production, sounding, musicalization, VFX, editing and directing. At the end of the show we will know if that care for details is translated to a writing and acting masterpiece too.How is in adaptation terms?That depends how you think adaptation works. If you are the lost boy who think that a good adaptation is copy pasting an existing work (from books or comics) then you will probably benmor inclined to put 6-7 stars because there are some changes to the book closest references.But if you are the guy that know perfectly that an adaptation is an inspiration with core elements of the NARRATIVE, not the phisical characteristics of individuals, you will be delighted by how deep is the understanding of this core elements in RoP.It feels fantastical at the same time at it feels deep, grim and dark when is required.I hope this show continue in this way and keep showing to us that Tolkien's work is in good hands.

ipc-title__text: I didn't like it at first but I learned to appreciate it.

This show is visually stunning, but it lacks in everything else. Casting is horrible, poorly written, complete disregard for established lore and content created by J. R. R Tolkein and Peter Jackson. Is seems as though the creators of this show are doing everything in their power to ruin lord of the rings. The show is lackluster from beginning to end. If you continue to watch this show with the hope of it getting better, you are wasting your time. The show miraculously gets worse with every episode release. It is a complete dumpster fire of a show. This show will only get worse with time, so I wouldn't even begin to watch this show if you haven't started.

I am not going to analyze this show as an adaptation of Tolkien's work because it has already been done several times and the final result is the same: it is shameful; for people like me, who have read all his books and love the universe he created so much, this show is a sinful creation; it completeley butchers the lore, inventing plots and characters, eliminating others who are really important to the story, and so on.However, this is not the part I am going to talk about, as I said, as I approached this show as common, original fantasy; not as an adaptation. In this regard, I can say we find ourselves in front of a good show: not fantastic nor flawless, but good. It is entertaining, at least for me, which is something every show or movie should always achieve. Its strongest points lie on its visuals, soundtrack and cinematography, and the plot is developed quickly enough to keep you going. But, as I previously mentioned, it is not a fantastic piece of entertainment. Moreover, it has some huge flaws.Starting with big holes in the plot, added to a lack of explanation of some parts which play an important role in the story but are suddenly cast aside. Then we have reference characters from the original work, as Galadriel or Elendil, who are horribly portrayed and with a poor decision-making capability; not to talk about their charisma, which is practically inexistent.Nonetheless, I felt entertained enough to binge-watch the show in less than a week and keep my interest on for the second season, which, hopefully, I expect to be more loyal to the books. Just a bit.

I have been a huge fan of Tolkien's work before the movies. Read all of his and his son's books. Loved Peter Jackson's movies as well. When I heard Amazon was making a series, I kept my excitement to a minimum. I am very glad I did. It is a horrible rendition to Tolkien's work. Yes the environments/scenery is absolutely gorgeous, but that is about it. I loved Durin III and Disa they were the saving grace but that alone was not enough to save this godforsaken dumpster-fire. Morfydd Clark
did what she could with the terrible story they gave her. She is getting a lot of flak but it was solely the writing and her story. Every actor besides them was subpar for their roles. Especially the elves; Elrond was disrespectfully portrayed and watching water boil was more entertaining than Cordova's performance. Amazon should be ashamed of themselves for producing this. They have great shows but they took Tolkien's work and took a big .... on it.

The main problem of this show, from my point of view anyways, is that they've bet all of their money on computer effects. The show is overflowing with them, you can see their presence in almost every shot...Everything else harshly lacks the quality expected from both the invested money and from the LotR world, starting from nonexistent storytelling, over emotionless and rather skill-less cast, all the way to changing key factors of the movies success.Contrary to PJ's movies, which changed side characters and events but maintained the basic phylosophy and features of everything, this show did exactly the oposite thing.The biggest NO for me was depiction of Galadriel, both from the acting view and from character creation view. Out of beautiful, kind, wise, magic gifted woman they created an arrogant, spoiled, ninja weilding katana instead of magic power, who cares bout nothing but herself, lectures others about how they should act yet doing the same thing as them. This isn't a 'character developement', this is 'character destruction'.Even the race-dispute could have been settled peacefully and possibly even accepted if only they would create an interesting and well-permormed characters instead of just mediocre ones.Effects do not make a good shows. Stories and characters do.

A visual feast for the eye, and visually the series stays true enough to previous Tolkien work and my personal imagination. I love how the series explains or elaborates on Tolkien work, through all levels of the production (overall plot, visual design,
Poetry, etc) and continues the main themes of the books, so there seems to be a lot of love for the source material with the production team, which was completely lacking with for instance the Witcher series plot writers.Still the series isn't perfect. The story is rather slow, and the characters remain rather shallow despite that, in part due to mediocre quality of the dialogs. A lot of the scenes are entirely predictable. If you are not a total Tolkien nerd, a lot of this love is wasted on you. The story is mostly true enough to the source, but this doesn't make for the most effective plotline. In these aspects, the series pales in comparison to House of the Dragon.All in all, positively surprised, happy spending time with it, will definitely keep watching.

I am losing interest in this series episode by episode. Completely ruined the lord of the rings experience. They need to get rid of writer and director involved in each of the episodes. I am feeling sorry that this very good content being converted into this garbage. Might not watch season 3 at all. Númenor is the most boring part of all. I have now started forwarding all elf scenes. Dwarfs was interesting but they stretched it too much. Series has made a joke of Galadriel, now she comes off as plain stupid. Sauran scenes are just so predictable. Skip an episode and nothing changes in plot lines. I am probably skipping rest of the season now. Absolute waste of time. Sad to see such pathetic implementation of tolkien work.

ipc-title__text: Big budget epic with fantastic storyline and characters
ipc-html-content-inner-div: A fantastic, sweeping, epic show with enjoyable depth of character to the goodies and badies. Loving season 2 more than season 1. 10/10 quality story and character development.The development of Sauron is so satisfying. Each world is given a good amount of attention with mystery and suspense intermixed with beautiful scenes and visual effects.Can't wait for each new episode to be released.I know some people are critical of the way lore is upheld with some highly specific gripes, but give the producers a break and just enjoy and appreciate the huge effort and clever writing that goes into epics like this.

Visually stunning, but admittedly I'm having a hard time following (as I'm not a die hard). Then there are those scenes when I look at my TV it's pitch black - why are these scenes so dark? Is it my TV or is it made like this for certain TVs. My TV is 4K capable, but when these dark scenes come on my TV all I hear is sound and cannot see a thing. But admittedly not only this production. I won't stop watching this series by any stretch of the imagination, it's very interesting and I'll try to be patient to try and get a better understanding of the story lines as they unfold over each episode. Maybe I need to only watch at night, I'd really love some feedback to my review/post.

I am into season two and I cannot figure out what the actual hell is going on. I am so bored and I've forgotten characters that were in season 1. There are so many forgettable characters and the writing is utter garbage. I don't blame the actors, they are actually pretty good but this is a far cry from the movies we have seen. I keep watching hoping it gets better but I just get more lost and more bored. Only saving grace is the music by Bear because that guy freaking rocks. Visually it's spectacular but can there be one good story line and a character I actually care about. I wish there was at least one episode that I can say well that was actually entertaining. So far 4 stars and if season two doesn't get better I am going to stop watching this borefest.

This show is visually stunning, but it lacks in everything else. Casting is horrible, poorly written, complete disregard for established lore and content created by J. R. R Tolkein and Peter Jackson. Is seems as though the creators of this show are doing everything in their power to ruin lord of the rings. The show is lackluster from beginning to end. If you continue to watch this show with the hope of it getting better, you are wasting your time. The show miraculously gets worse with every episode release. It is a complete dumpster fire of a show. This show will only get worse with time, so I wouldn't even begin to watch this show if you haven't started.

I am not going to analyze this show as an adaptation of Tolkien's work because it has already been done several times and the final result is the same: it is shameful; for people like me, who have read all his books and love the universe he created so much, this show is a sinful creation; it completeley butchers the lore, inventing plots and characters, eliminating others who are really important to the story, and so on.However, this is not the part I am going to talk about, as I said, as I approached this show as common, original fantasy; not as an adaptation. In this regard, I can say we find ourselves in front of a good show: not fantastic nor flawless, but good. It is entertaining, at least for me, which is something every show or movie should always achieve. Its strongest points lie on its visuals, soundtrack and cinematography, and the plot is developed quickly enough to keep you going. But, as I previously mentioned, it is not a fantastic piece of entertainment. Moreover, it has some huge flaws.Starting with big holes in the plot, added to a lack of explanation of some parts which play an important role in the story but are suddenly cast aside. Then we have reference characters from the original work, as Galadriel or Elendil, who are horribly portrayed and with a poor decision-making capability; not to talk about their charisma, which is practically inexistent.Nonetheless, I felt entertained enough to binge-watch the show in less than a week and keep my interest on for the second season, which, hopefully, I expect to be more loyal to the books. Just a bit.

ipc-title__text: Watch House of the Dragon for your fantasy fix
ipc-html-content-inner-div:
I have been a huge fan of Tolkien's work before the movies. Read all of his and his son's books. Loved Peter Jackson's movies as well. When I heard Amazon was making a series, I kept my excitement to a minimum. I am very glad I did. It is a horrible rendition to Tolkien's work. Yes the environments/scenery is absolutely gorgeous, but that is about it. I loved Durin III and Disa they were the saving grace but that alone was not enough to save this godforsaken dumpster-fire. Morfydd Clark
did what she could with the terrible story they gave her. She is getting a lot of flak but it was solely the writing and her story. Every actor besides them was subpar for their roles. Especially the elves; Elrond was disrespectfully portrayed and watching water boil was more entertaining than Cordova's performance. Amazon should be ashamed of themselves for producing this. They have great shows but they took Tolkien's work and took a big .... on it.

The main problem of this show, from my point of view anyways, is that they've bet all of their money on computer effects. The show is overflowing with them, you can see their presence in almost every shot...Everything else harshly lacks the quality expected from both the invested money and from the LotR world, starting from nonexistent storytelling, over emotionless and rather skill-less cast, all the way to changing key factors of the movies success.Contrary to PJ's movies, which changed side characters and events but maintained the basic phylosophy and features of everything, this show did exactly the oposite thing.The biggest NO for me was depiction of Galadriel, both from the acting view and from character creation view. Out of beautiful, kind, wise, magic gifted woman they created an arrogant, spoiled, ninja weilding katana instead of magic power, who cares bout nothing but herself, lectures others about how they should act yet doing the same thing as them. This isn't a 'character developement', this is 'character destruction'.Even the race-dispute could have been settled peacefully and possibly even accepted if only they would create an interesting and well-permormed characters instead of just mediocre ones.Effects do not make a good shows. Stories and characters do.

A visual feast for the eye, and visually the series stays true enough to previous Tolkien work and my personal imagination. I love how the series explains or elaborates on Tolkien work, through all levels of the production (overall plot, visual design,
Poetry, etc) and continues the main themes of the books, so there seems to be a lot of love for the source material with the production team, which was completely lacking with for instance the Witcher series plot writers.Still the series isn't perfect. The story is rather slow, and the characters remain rather shallow despite that, in part due to mediocre quality of the dialogs. A lot of the scenes are entirely predictable. If you are not a total Tolkien nerd, a lot of this love is wasted on you. The story is mostly true enough to the source, but this doesn't make for the most effective plotline. In these aspects, the series pales in comparison to House of the Dragon.All in all, positively surprised, happy spending time with it, will definitely keep watching.

ipc-title__text: It's not great, but it's not as bad as you've heard
Watch the whole series before reviewing
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Let's get one thing right, this isn't in the same ball park as Jacksons cinematic genius productions BUT visually and the way the story built and especially episodes 6 & 8 was executed, it really felt like the series had purpose.I'm surprised at the ratings but if you got all involved in the hype prior to it coming out or if you expected Peter Jackson level LotR's you'll be disappointed but if you go into it with an open mind, you'll really enjoy it.Some characters I just couldn't connect with, some were arguably bad casting but some absolutely took it apart and really delivered.Really looking forward to how it develops in season 2 and what it has in store for certain characters.

I've always kind of thought of Tolkien as kids' books - loved them when I was young but outside of the ley of Turin Turambar there's not a ton of complexity and nothing to surprise me. That was not the case here. Many seem disappointed by Galadriel and the elves. If you're looking for Elves to be invincible wise tall Mary Sues and you really need them have long hair, well, I guess watch something else. If you're interested in a story with less awfulness and more hope and goodness than HOTD (which I also love but it gets heavy) but still plenty of intrigue, temptation, and fantasy... I highly recommend Rings of Power. Less than ten stars because some of the failures of logic and logistics sometimes took me out of being immersed in Middle Earth. Why are there so few people in general? We're watching battles of like 20v20.

ipc-title__text: Awesome! Big shoes / hobbit feet filled!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: If you, like me, are a LOTR trilogy obsessive, you will appreciate this series.Beautifully shot, nicely paced (if at times the pace seemed slow, I am reminded that at times in the original trilogy and the subsequent Hobbit films, there were slower, more gentle, moments) and the actors themselves had big shoes/hobbit feet to fill - and fill them they did!Testament to the sheer enjoyment of this series, my family and I, long after the end scenes were done, are still discussing the minutiae of the characters, the plot and pondering the question 'so who is he/she?'I especially enjoyed seeing more of the dwarven Kingdom and its people, a little bit of the history of hobbits and the creation of key places in LOTR, as well as the fallibility of those who seemed above mundane things like jealousy, greed and arrogance.I would whole heartedly recommend this series and I would watch it all again!

The story is great, however all action scenes and emotional scenes are too cliche. You can predict the lines they say and why is there always the cliche of the slow murderer and then the savior appears out of nowhere just in time? Its too cheap directors come on.Too much forced emotion between the characters. Also, why is the language so formal? A little formal is okay but it was too much. It was great they showed maps, but they could have shown more.However, great graphics, good music. A beautifull Galadriel to see. Great story, great references to LOTR and the lore of the entire world of Tolkien.

I watched it with low expectations since there were a lot of bad reviews, but now that it's over, I must say I loved it. Good episode structure, when one ends we are quickly put up to speed as to what's happening in the different storylines in the beginning of the next. The cast is perfectly OK, diverse but not in an annoying quota-making way. The dialogs are rich and remind me of LOTR, the characters always had wise words to say in the show's more reflective moments. Visual effects are good. Music and creatures match the LOTR feeling. We get a chance to see Hobbits being Hobbits, elves being elves and Sauron being Sauron. None of it disappointed me. Can't say there were many "duh" moments, maybe one or 2 throughout the entire show, which is more that I can say for Stranger Things or GoT. Looking forward to season 2!

This first season takes a while to get going, building slowly until episode 6.I'm alright with the slow build and there was enough happening to keep me interested, but I do understand some of the criticism about it been dull.The final 3 episodes really deliver on what may come in seasons 2 and 3, and certainly have me interested enough to want to watch more. And there were a few surprises at the end that I did not see coming.As to be expected considering the large budget it looks stunning, but personally I would beef up the action more, it really does seem incredibly tame after shows like Game of Thrones. There was always going to be comparisons with GoT, and the LotR's films, and unfortunately with this show been 12/pg rated it was always going to fall flat in comparison. It's a shame really because although I enjoyed it, it could have been show much more.

Review written during end of season 1I'm sure we were all pretty worried as the first few episodes rolled around, it felt soulless, and you could tell a big company like Amazon created it.However, the more and more episodes came out, the better it got. At first, it felt like a chore to watch this show, but, as they finished introducing their characters, the more time they could spend on this world.When Lord of the Rings came out in the early 2000s, there was a lot they had to do to appeal to the Hollywood meta of movies, like the over exaggerated slow motion all 2000s action movies HAD to have. And in this show we don't get that at all, this is a very modern feeling show, which I think is one reason people say how different this show feels to the Jackson line of films.While I can't really say this show FEELS like Lord of the Rings, theres some things I actually think is improved on.The cinematography... oh my god. This show is beautiful. Whoever the director of photography is needs a raise, everyone needs to take notes from this person.Most of the actors are very good, and I think every actor does the best they can given the dialog, which as well is very impressive. I like how the characters talk and interact with each other, it feels realI think there's a lot of promise for this show, we have a compelling story here, good actors, and very pleasant to look at. I'll be watching the next season, I'm excited to see what's in store for Lord of the Rings as a series.

ipc-title__text: On par with once upon a time
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Okay hear me out, the visuals of this show are gorgeous, sometimes breathtaking even, but no glitz and glamor could make up for the insufferable writing. Every. Single. Episode. I've had to strain myself to stay awake. IT'S THAT BORING. The dialogue is on par with CW's once upon a time, sure it's cool seeing all your favorite characters live action but as soon as they open their mouths I'm already tuned out, same with this show. I don't understand how you can have every single resource at your disposal seemingly unlimited budget and STILL make such a godawful show. I understand only having the rights to the appendices but there's still so much lore to delve into. Clearly that doesn't help when you fire your "Tolkein scholars". I mean what were you thinking?? Should've just been some run of the mill fantasy show then MAYBE it could be better. But comparing it to a worldwide beloved trilogy that holds the record for most Oscars won? Honestly id rather watch the Rankin Bass version which holds true to the lore far better than this. A few things to address that completely took me out of the show.. very first episode when Galadriel picks up the helmet to place in the pile of hundreds more, it BENDS when she picks it up clearly fake made of plastic. How can this supposedly be the most expensive show produced and yet Peter Jackson (weta workshop specifically) made THOUSANDS UPON THOUSANDS pieces of REAL armor and weapons and I struggle to find anything genuine in the show. Having made chain mail myself, the chain mail in the show is laughable, it's so painfully obvious that it's some frilly mesh fabric. Don't even get me started on Elendil's man boob armor SMH. I mean seriously what even is that?? Oh god and the elves.. what have they done to the elves!?! I don't mean diversity, that's great and everything, I mean they look so bland and boring and buzzcuts??? They're supposed to look ethereal with long hair and well over a billion dollars spent and not one elven wig. What so we can see their ears? Wouldn't need that if they even tried to make them look ethereal but okay. And why aren't the dwarf women bearded? Why are the harfoots so evil? The orcs are the only saving grace, I find myself cheering them on. You know your writing is bad when you're rooting for the bad guys to win. Rant over going to rewatch LOTR trilogy to cleanse my eyes from this absolute dumpster fire.

I was a bit skeptic at first, after seeing LOTR and Hobbit, but the show keeps getting better and better and adds new layers to the story. I'm impressed how the writers can keep the mystery and suspense at a high level, making you to come back every time to see what happens next. This exact feeling I had only when I read the books of Tolkien. So, I can say that, despite some flaws the show is closer anything could be to a Tolkien story.True, some characters were a little weak at start, but let's not forget they were so young and unexperienced at the time and probably they will get more attention as the show continue.

This show is quite impressive the writers took an interesting fantasy world rife with interesting lore that was already written for them to pull from and made perhaps the one of the most tedious shows ever made. I had no idea that a war with dark wizards and orcs fighting for the fate of the world against men and elves could be so mundane. I must admit, it has the side benefit of motivating you to at least fold laundry or unstack the dishwasher when characters start long winded speeches about what it would be like if they were a boat or how a man's best friend is his horse.Every week my friends and I generously called each new episode a "set up episode" in the hopes that it was building towards a greater narrative. However, we were deceived. It would be unfair to other shows with actual set up episodes to state that is the case here. 90% of the shows dialogue is pure filler. It's written like a story your senile grandad tells you when you ask him to pass the salt and 30 minutes later you are still listening to his beguiling tale of what 50 cents could buy you back in his day whilst forgetting entirely about the salt he was supposed to have passed.This feels somewhat like the Hobbit in the sense of there was perhaps an interesting tale to be told (although this remains to be seen) but it has been greenlit for 5 seasons already so that tale is going to be padded out for 4 seasons of stalling episodes. Almost like the writing had the script ready for a season of a show then were told at the last minute that same story needed to fill 5 seasons worth of screen time. There are legitimately tons of scenes that are just characters reading poor man's fortune cookies.The reason for the 3 star is that this is not the lowest quality show around and as other people have said it generally looks nice enough on the surface, sadly there is absolutely nothing waiting for you beyond that if you choose to dive in.

ipc-title__text: Shockingly bad - where did the budget go?!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: A list of my complaints:

I see how it can be the most expensive serie ever, whit all the money put into ads/social media marketing and other online marketing it should be. But a sad fact it's that it doesn't even come close to LOTR that is over 20 years old now. Whit the rings of power budget i expected way better costumes/acting/special effects/music and yeah just about everything. But everything just feels awkward whit music that doesn't fit into the scenes and slow motion cuts that's expected do grab you in and make you feel the intense moment does absolutely nothing more than alienate.There are 80's fantasy movies that are better than this.

There are several things that are changed in the Rings of Power that make Lord of the Rings not make sense. There is forced plot, they tell you instead of show you, the elves look like they're from "Carnival Row" instead of Lord of the Rings. It's frustrating as an actual fan. I don't mind that they compressed history, but they completely changed a ton of characters, forced the plot along, made it hard to follow in some places, but easy to follow and boring in others. It moves at a snails' pace. It looks beautiful, but the action scenes make it look like a high school student's choreography filmed with professional equipment. It feels like they spent a ton of time on all the CGI and most of the costumes, but neglected others and neglected the story. They make up backstory that makes the story feel weird. They did fan-baiting.

I bore through the first episode somehow. But halfway into the second episode, I could no longer put myself through the slow pain. Not slow burn. Slow pain. Being a pretty huge LOTR fan, this as huge a disappointment. Sub-par characters to say the least, and the protagonist, garadel whatever, has zero spark.They sold out I feel. For instance, prime video recently also saw wheel of time come out. New show altogether and setting and reaching expectations by last episode, all in one season. And this on the other hand, could not live up to even an ounce of everything lord of the rings stand for. If you can't make it better, at least live up to it. If you can't live up to it, just don't make it!!

Visually pretty and in places well-acted, The Rings of Power is a sloppy mis-telling of Tolkien's work. It's well known that Amazon could only draw from the contents of The Lord of the Ring's appendices - the choice, then, to muddle 1,600 years of a clear-cut timeline with confusing character changes is utterly baffling. Key characters are missing or entirely altered, clear-cut aspects written plainly in the appendices have been abandoned or twisted, and the plot meanders at a pace not even a snail would be envious of. The music is nice, however, and the first twenty or so minutes of the first episode are enjoyable.

The casting is not a real problem in this serie but the writing is really poor and weak ,is like put a wonderful dress on a rotten corpse, as much as the dress can be beutiful you can not see the rotten plot dragging down what could have be a enjoyable show.Very few character act in a natural or logic way , the story is full of contradictions and plot holes.They fail to get a proper target sometimes there are childish gags on screen or bloodles figth and after few minutes gore and beheading like a splatter horror movie.The only amazing thing they manage to do was to take something like Tolkien loved and readed by milions and make it boring.

ipc-title__text: Not amazing, not terrible, just average
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This is a very average run of the mill fantasy show that just so happens to have the Lord of the Rings name slapped on it. Yes the visual are great, but what do you expect for 1 million per minute per episode. No amount of visuals can make up for the sorry excuse of a script. None of the characters actions makes logical sense. They do and act in a way that just throws suspension of disbelief out the window... One of the most egregious is the main character jumping off a boat and attempting to swim thousands of miles back to land - what?!The dialogue is just plain bad, full of clichés and clunky attempts at epic dialogue that just never works.The pacing is not great and the sense of awe and scale is off. In 2 days, the dwarves build a massive forge that would have taken 6 to 12 months. Characters just go for a quick stroll in foot and end magically teleporting hundreds of miles away in an instant. Where are the days and weeks of hard travel across a challenging landscape?There's lots of filler. In a well written story, everything that happens should be to move the story forward or help the audience understand something of the world or the characters motivations, but half the running time is just pointless filler.Overral, a very average show that would have got cancelled by the end of the first season if it didn't have the lord of the rings name on it.

I don't get it. No character development, no fluent story telling, nothing to hang on to. Why is it 6. Something on your platform? And Galandriel maaan, she is annoying. They should have used an African american actress, at least they could have screamed 'racism' louder and cover all their bases.I understand the times are what they are, people need to be in conflict, divided and miserable but ruining older productions? Just create something, anything, it can be the worse drivel , but at least it's an original story. 77 more words to write : you could save it, just fire those writers and make season 2 without any of the chars from this present catastrophe.

This show has good actors, but the girl playing Galadriel is not one of them. It typically isn't a good idea to have the main focal point of your show be the most insufferable and ridiculous character in the entire cast.One of my main gripes is that the elves do not look anything like how Tolkien described or how Peter Jackson portrayed them. They literally just look like humans with pointy ears, nothing else. They are supposed to be beautiful, regal, and tall- and yet we have seen multiple so far who are unattractive, short, and just plain boring. I don't know why the showrunners thought it was a good idea to take something we already have an established and well-liked picture of in our mind, and then try to make their own adaption of it, which completely sucked.The black elf is really the least of the problems, as he is one of the only elves we see who actually feels a BIT elvish, in my opinion. A good choice for the casting of a black elf would be the girl who played Missandei from Game of Thrones. Arondir is just okay.The biggest issue so far is the fact this show cost $1billion to make, yet the writing and directing is subpar. The dialogue in this show seems like it comes from a bad wattpad fanfiction, the conversation with Galadriel and her brother being a prime example. I have no idea how that made sense to anyone. Not only that, but some of the cgi is extremely sketchy for such an expensive show. The scene where they are sailing into Numenor and staring at the cliffs was so obviously green-screened it was painful to watch.I found this show did a poor job of keeping my undivided attention. I caught myself checking my phone more than a few times during unbearable scenes with the elves and harfoots. Regardless, I will continue watching mostly because I want to see what they do with Halbrand. As a Tolkien fan, I feel obligated to continue trudging through this, even though it is a poor attempt at recreating his world. It's not completely terrible, but I would totally understand someone hating it and not wanting to watch further.

So far, the series seems to be "finding itself' and is struggling to do that.A host of new characters and new drives makes this interesting, if not a little trite at times.One has to wonder of they are going for a LOTR series, or a Game of Thrones vibe.It is visually stunning, introducing whole other worlds and dynamics, though it also seems a bit forced. Maybe that is because there is just so much going on at once it can be hard to recall everything all the time. Also seems that the visuals paper over character development at times, with lots of "noise" but little beyond that in terms of understanding the importance of what we are seeing.Looking forward to seeing how it develops, where the rings come from, whose "bright idea" that is, and a lot of other character development, but still is not as riveting as I was hoping. Then again, this all seems like one very long set-up, so I would imagine that could change as we get further along.

ipc-title__text: A beautiful mess. Looks gorgeous, but the story and acting is pretty bland and bad (And NOT Tolkien)
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Short summary: The show looks good, that's all the story is bad, dialogues are worst and the acting is more wooden than Fangorn Forest. If it were not using Tolkien's name it would be a good/mediocre generic Fantasy show...Log form review:I've got to admit that as a lifelong fan of Tolkien's books, having read them until the leaves would come out of the book seams, what I was seeing from the trailers was something that gave me second and third thoughts about this show... I disliked them changing the lore and the races of charactes, I admit it, I wanted it to look and feel as I had read it for decades... BUT, after watching the show, the race changes are the less of the show's lore disrupting troubles...The show looks awesome, as I've said before, but the changes done to characters as galadriel (not only her being transformed into Xena princess warrior, but her attitude, and actions... She's a Mary Sue, and also insufferable, and egotistical). She's the bestest, smartest elf out there, and everyone is just against her and does nonsensical stuff that is just there to justify her actions but that makes no actual sense.The parts with the Hobbits (Harfoots are just a subrace of hobbits) are boring and slow and change the style and seem totally disconnected with the rest of the actual plot.Arondyr and Bronwin's "Romeo and Juliet" sub-plot is totally unnecesary and boring, also poorly written and the acting, is one of the worst from the show so far.The general dialogues try to feel important, and profound but are just lame... There's a lot of telling, a lot of the stuff is just said by characters instead of shown... IT is a SHOW, show me what is happening.On the Story/Lore side: Just with how Galadriel goes to Middle Earth, most of Middle Earth's story would change soooo much, this is no longer based on Tolkien, it just uses the names an places...

ipc-title__text: I have expected more! But disappointed!
ipc-html-content-inner-div:
I was excited for years waiting the show to be released, And to be back to beloved middle earth... But after watching the 2 episodes i admit that i'm disappointed!.. The actors chosen for this havey task are belew my expectations! Especially the actress for Galadriel So called "The commander of Northrn Armies"! And Celebrimbor's Actor, nor his appearance looks like an elvish or his presence being received as a High Elf!.. And what's the problem with This so called Gil-galad who looks like a naive weak "High-King"!...
The dialogue is boring and the polt is pointless, And oh gosh an Elf with a short hiar cut, That's so annoying to me! Customs are okay, Nothing special!.But you know what's special and what i really liked about this show?! It's the Visuals, Yep! They are stunning! Wow for that!But Anything else it's not for me!!! Unfortunately!Taking all of that in consideration, I will keep watching the future episodes, perhaps i may find out something more interesting!...

ipc-title__text: If you're a Tolkien fan, you already know it's not for you
ipc-html-content-inner-div: As a fantasy series, it's fine. As a Lord of the Rings series, it's abysmal. No Lords or warriors here, it's a girl-power bonanza. Which begs the question, why bother affiliating it with Tolkien's masterpieces. Why not just make an entirely new fantasy series? How nonsensical and how disrespectful to the beauty of the original works. They wanted to turn Tolkien's work into their own 'patriarchy as a world-theory' manifesto. Casting is fine, writing is very poor but special effects are quite good, so still worth watching, just not for the action. It's not an action-packed kind of series (yet another insult to LOTR).

Currently. I had 7 here but warned it would be reduced, if doesn't get better and since Amazon didn't accept my scathing review - it is now reduced - Amazon must do better, and stop getting fixated over the Games of Thrones and give us something we can watch.The finale took it further down to 1 - this production is so bad and pointless - but why?There is not one single character that is interesting, the accents I really can't get my ears around and why is one of the funniest men in Britain, Lenny Henry playing such an insignificant part(now they have killed him off, why?). Please improve as we have been waiting a very long time for this and to be given such a bland start really did send me to bed, especially after watching Attack on Titan - this was so dull...It was duller than Wheel of Fortune, will people stop trying to make something that rivals Game of Thrones, and just make something of interest. The set design was poor.The acting in most parts wooden.

ipc-title__text: A genuine look and worthy of Middle Earth
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Only two episodes are out but man its engaging. The characters are mostly well defined. Some liberties have been taken to keep it simple and hence more appealing to the audience of today.The score fits perfectly. I really hope the script remains strong.The VFX and CG is minimum or atleast seems minimum which results in an organic look instead of the shiny plastic look. Think of LOTR vs The Hobbit.I really like that all the races have been shown in a state prior to what would be in the LOTR e.g. The hobbits or "Harfoots" are very wild in this age.
