ipc-title__text: series is inconsistent and lack of direction in story telling
ipc-html-content-inner-div: As a long-time fan of Middle-Earth, I had high hopes for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power. While I can't say the journey has been smooth in terms of storytelling, the sheer scale and ambition of the series are undeniable. The last episode of Season 2 really captured the highs and lows of this show.Yes, much of the story felt scattered, with some plotlines meandering or lacking the cohesion we've come to expect from the works of Tolkien. It's clear that the writers are building something big, but at times, the narrative has struggled to connect all its threads in a way that flows seamlessly. Still, the stunning visuals and world-building more than make up for any inconsistencies. The craftsmanship in design, costumes, and effects are nothing short of breathtaking.However, I do agree that the ending of Season 2 leaves a lot to be desired in terms of a promising setup for Season 3. It's as if the conclusion didn't quite live up to the buildup, and while I remain optimistic, it wasn't the most satisfying note to leave on. That said, this series continues to be a visual and immersive feast, and I'll be tuning in to see where the journey goes next. There's not enough magic in the air to give it even 1 star.

I swear, if Tolkien rose from the grave and was not offended by Amazon's series you would all question his sanity. And as another reviewer pointed out, there were critics for both The Lord Of The Rings trilogy and Fellowship Of The Rings trilogy claiming they were an insult to Tolkien too. And yet both have stood the test of time.I have watched many tv series, and movies, based on books, comics or games where 'canon' devotees are brutal in their reviews. Sadly when these same devotees are pleased with something, the productions can be so niche that they often lose the interest of the general audience. That's obviously because the audience is not familiar with the material on which they were based. It's pretty myopic to expect millions of dollars be spent to serve a small portion of a potential viewership. Plus I'm not sure anything, rocking the title 'Lord Of The Rings', could ever escape the heavy criticism that would be levied by those with unrealistic expectations of a masterpiece they deem worthy of Tolkien.But for the rest of us it's about was it entertaining, was it captivating, was the video/audio well done, the story intriguing, the characters relatable and acting respectable. If this series was not tagged with The Lord Of The Rings namesake it would have overall rated much higher by the general public. That truly is a disservice since this series has a lot going for it. So many series of much lower caliber, that did not have to jump through the hoops this one did, were rated much higher.As a non-hardcore Tolkien fan, I thoroughly enjoyed both offerings but I must admit more so when we upgraded to an OLED tv with Dolby Vision and added height speakers to give us Dolby Atmos. This series is really meant to be appreciated with the visuals and audio it delivers. It breathes life into it and makes it much more enveloping ... theater like. You can perceive the workmanship that went into its making and let the visuals/audio do a lot of the heavy lifting.If I find fault with this production it would be for that same reason. Not everyone is able to have the equipment necessary to take full advantage of those features. This can lead to the story feeling disconnected and weaker. In a made for TV series, not made for a Movie theater, it would seem writers and directors should take into account all the devices it will be watched on and adjust the content accordingly. Creators and critics don't watch on IPads, small TVs or listen in stereo so their detachment (maybe even arrogance) has made this series understandably fall flat for some.Nevertheless, if graded by theater standards, this series deserves the marks only given to productions of the highest quality video, audio and storytelling.

Characters teleport all over the place inconsistently and fight scenes have no real risk. The premise of the show is set thousands of years before Lord of the Rings and sees the different species try to survive against the dark forces of Middle Earth.Main Character
Morfydd Clark plays a young Galadriel and I did find it unfortunate that I really didn't care about this character. She is just really dull and the show doesn't do a good enough job of making you care about her or her character. Clark, does try and that deserves a bit of credit but with her being the clear protagonist of this show, she falls really flat.Supporting Cast

I think a lot of the performers were hampered by shoddy writing and poor storytelling which gave them little to work with.Robert Aramayo plays young Elrond and I really liked him. He doesn't really feel like Elrond but I can't deny that he is entertaining to watch and there is plenty of depth made to his character and I found the scenes involving him and Durin played by Owain Arthur to be the most entertaining of the show.Charlie Vickers plays Halbrand and he is alright, he actually has some charm and charisma to him which helps him rise above some shoddy writing for the character. I thought he did a good job and made me intrigued by his character.But the rest of the cast really suffers, Arondir played by Ismael Cruz Cordova is really boring. He is great in the action sequences, but he is so monotone and soft spoken that it was hard to care about him and he just falls really flat, especially with how much time we spend with him.The story involving Daniel Weyman as The Stranger and Markella Kavenagh as Nori is really dull and boring. It tries to be mysterious but it never really goes anywhere, it took till the finale to try and make them interesting but there characters were a sore part of the show.Story
The story really misses the mark. I saw it described as a fan fiction of JRR Tolkein's work and I am afraid that it does really feel like that. The show tries to force intrigue and interest by hiding a lot of information about the characters but that made it really hard to get invested. Then the final episode has a few reveals that feel rushed and not earned for the show and I hope the story improves in the future.Script
The show is unfortunately not written well. All the dialogue feels really forced and those bits that are good are due to the actors rising above this shoddy writing. Not much makes sense and making so many storylines that involve mystery makes things feeling frustratingly not complete.Style
Easily the best part of the show is the style. The show looks beautiful, you can tell it has a huge budget and for the most part it is really effective. Middle Earth looks great and I am glad that this show has the essence of the universe with both its looks and also its fantastic music choices. The action scenes are also great and have a bit more brutality which I definitely enjoyed.Overall
Overall, Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power Season 1 is a bad show and falls really flat of its licence. It is definitely an example of style of substance and I hope the second season is a huge improvement on this as the franchise deserves way better.Rating - 3/10.

What else can you expect from Amazon thinking it can really do justice to a work such as Tolkien's by simply throwing money at it? I really wanted to like this series but I just couldn't; that "suspension of disbelief" never happened. Full disclosure, I have read the Silmarillion, Unfinished Tales, etc. So yes, I know the lore and no--absolutely no--this series does not follow the stories Tolkien wrote (the writers borrowed actual character names and then threw the rest of the source material in the bin) but pretending that I went into this series without all of that background, I still found the series difficult to enjoy.First, too many concurrent storylines. Each episode jumps among up to four different plots and since each episode is only about an hour, this makes it difficult to "get into" something after only about 10-15 minutes.Second, the storylines themselves fall flat. So much is being crammed into these almost bite-sized chunks of aforementioned storylines to move things forward but why? Why not take things more slowly and focus on letting the audience get to know the characters before rushing to the next thing? Which leads to my third complaint:
Third, the characters are either flat, unbelievable, or unlikable, with a few exceptions. Durin and Elendil are the best cast and acted characters in my opinion. Galadriel... Why was she written and acted to be so pugnacious and unlikable? She's still thousands of years old in the second age so the reason of "this is in her younger years" is absolutely trash. But that's getting into lore so moving on. The elves themselves were very disappointing both in their appearance and acting. Different skin tones for elves? Yes, bring it on. But short hair? No, come on. Did the costume department not get enough $ for good wigs? That's what it feels like, and also not enough money for more convincing armor for the Númenoreans.Bottom line: Not the worst show to ever be made but it's also pretty boring in a lot areas. I didn't care about any of the characters, never teared up with them, didn't have any anxiety when danger was imminent. As the experience was all just "meh", again, it's pretty disappointing when you think of what could have been done with a billion dollars.

ipc-title__text: Visually outstanding, but melodramatic script lacks subtlety
ipc-html-content-inner-div: As I watched the first season of LOTR: TROP I was amazed at the scope and beauty of the production. Incredible environments, vast landscapes and sweeping shots. Meticulously made sets, designs, props and costumes, and fantastic top-of-the-line special effects, CGI and animations. A real treat for the eyes.The script on the other hand, is problematic. While the overarching main plot is reasonably good, the problem lies with the tempo and gravitas of the scenes that build the individual scenes. Specifically, every scene, and almost every single line ever spoken has the weight of life-and-death, good versus evil, fate of middle earth and all races in it.And I do mean every scene.A character cannot say hello without a dramatic pause, followed by a line such as: "in our language, we don't say hello. We say fluggely-mugguly, which means 'may the light of dawn show you the way of righteousness' " followed by meaningful looks, cinematic music and a sweeping shot.Now repeat that same vibe a thousand times.Every. Scene.It gets tedious real fast.I understand that LOTR is about epic struggles in it's core, but this heavy-handed treatment of these issues make it melodramatic and distance the viewer, rather than draw him in with the intricacies and nuances of small intimate moments- as they project into life's greatest questions.Is it worth watching then?It is, but as they say: "A bird will fly to the sun as the leaf falls to the earth. Just as good will triumph over evil, so will our toils forever stain the ground with the sweat of our forefathers" (meaningful look, sweeping shot, climactic cinematic music)

Although there are visually stunning places like Numenor and Eregion, probs like armour and weapons look cheap and bad for a billion dollar production. Not to mention the rings which look like they came straight out of a gumball machine. The showrunners unfortunately show absolutely no love for detail and only care for the modern political ideology of diversity. As a viewer you fail to establish an emotional bond to any of the characters due to bad character development and writing, which is just sad. Therefore I'll have to give this series a generous 5/10.

ipc-title__text: series is inconsistent and lack of direction in story telling
ipc-html-content-inner-div: As a long-time fan of Middle-Earth, I had high hopes for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power. While I can't say the journey has been smooth in terms of storytelling, the sheer scale and ambition of the series are undeniable. The last episode of Season 2 really captured the highs and lows of this show.Yes, much of the story felt scattered, with some plotlines meandering or lacking the cohesion we've come to expect from the works of Tolkien. It's clear that the writers are building something big, but at times, the narrative has struggled to connect all its threads in a way that flows seamlessly. Still, the stunning visuals and world-building more than make up for any inconsistencies. The craftsmanship in design, costumes, and effects are nothing short of breathtaking.However, I do agree that the ending of Season 2 leaves a lot to be desired in terms of a promising setup for Season 3. It's as if the conclusion didn't quite live up to the buildup, and while I remain optimistic, it wasn't the most satisfying note to leave on. That said, this series continues to be a visual and immersive feast, and I'll be tuning in to see where the journey goes next. There's not enough magic in the air to give it even 1 star.

I swear, if Tolkien rose from the grave and was not offended by Amazon's series you would all question his sanity. And as another reviewer pointed out, there were critics for both The Lord Of The Rings trilogy and Fellowship Of The Rings trilogy claiming they were an insult to Tolkien too. And yet both have stood the test of time.I have watched many tv series, and movies, based on books, comics or games where 'canon' devotees are brutal in their reviews. Sadly when these same devotees are pleased with something, the productions can be so niche that they often lose the interest of the general audience. That's obviously because the audience is not familiar with the material on which they were based. It's pretty myopic to expect millions of dollars be spent to serve a small portion of a potential viewership. Plus I'm not sure anything, rocking the title 'Lord Of The Rings', could ever escape the heavy criticism that would be levied by those with unrealistic expectations of a masterpiece they deem worthy of Tolkien.But for the rest of us it's about was it entertaining, was it captivating, was the video/audio well done, the story intriguing, the characters relatable and acting respectable. If this series was not tagged with The Lord Of The Rings namesake it would have overall rated much higher by the general public. That truly is a disservice since this series has a lot going for it. So many series of much lower caliber, that did not have to jump through the hoops this one did, were rated much higher.As a non-hardcore Tolkien fan, I thoroughly enjoyed both offerings but I must admit more so when we upgraded to an OLED tv with Dolby Vision and added height speakers to give us Dolby Atmos. This series is really meant to be appreciated with the visuals and audio it delivers. It breathes life into it and makes it much more enveloping ... theater like. You can perceive the workmanship that went into its making and let the visuals/audio do a lot of the heavy lifting.If I find fault with this production it would be for that same reason. Not everyone is able to have the equipment necessary to take full advantage of those features. This can lead to the story feeling disconnected and weaker. In a made for TV series, not made for a Movie theater, it would seem writers and directors should take into account all the devices it will be watched on and adjust the content accordingly. Creators and critics don't watch on IPads, small TVs or listen in stereo so their detachment (maybe even arrogance) has made this series understandably fall flat for some.Nevertheless, if graded by theater standards, this series deserves the marks only given to productions of the highest quality video, audio and storytelling.

ipc-title__text: Season 2 is better than season 1 and the movies!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I'm a big fan of Lord of the Rings and to be honest, I enjoyed season two more than season one and the movies. Lots of little stories going on but doesn't seem overwhelming. In the end you feel emotionally connected to the characters, even the bad guys. Some complicated character conflicts that pull at your heart strings. Makes me want to go back and watch all the movies and season one again. You can see parts of yourself in the characters, both good and bad. Full of surprises that you should've seen coming but didn't. Timing was great. They tease out plot points and aren't a hurry to reveal important story details. Hope they continue the series!

ipc-title__text: A Promising Story Undermined by Confusing Details and Missteps
Rip it up and start again!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Who would have thought 100s of millions of dollars could buy so little?The plot and script are so poor that you could be forgiven for thinking the screenwriters were still on strike. The storyline does not move in a way that engages an audience - so much time is wasted on meaningless scenes, with boring characters. The harfoots could have been left out completely and no one would care. They just talk non-stop drivel and pull along their crappy handcarts - have they never heard of horses?Although a few scenes are quite exciting, the mood is almost instantly ruined by yet another boring section, with badly-voiced accents.O don't blame the actors - they were just miscast and given some of the worst plot and script ever.I do not really care if it is faithful to Tolkien's legacy, or the Jackson films - just make it more exciting!

ipc-title__text: Slow to get going, but wow!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: There's a lot of hate for RoP, and I'll admit that season 1 was slow to get going- I didn't get fully drawn into it. But season 2 has really ratcheted up the stakes. Episode 7 was nail biting and the production value was amazing for a mere TV show.I have found myself going from merely casually interested, to fully invested in the show from season one to two. The story is so engaging and is slowly starting to live up to Peter Jackson's trilogy.My only complaint is through watching in Amazon Prime - why are we subjected to the sheer number of adverts??! We already pay for a subscription- why are there adverts as well! It's infuriating!

The Rings of Power manages to feel incredibly cheap despite its monumental budget. The constant CGI, abysmal dialogue & writing, and questionable costume design leave much to be desired, not to mention the fact that characters' motives rarely make sense and change on a whim.The writing is the biggest weakness. Characters teleport all over the place inconsistently and fight scenes have no real risk. Almost every character has plot armor - every elf except the main characters are bumbling, uncoordinated idiots who fight like toddlers and make illogical decisions in the middle of battle.Almost every episode is riddled with shameless copy-paste moments from Peter Jackson's trilogy as an attempt at fanservice, but it always falls flat and feels forced and out of place.This show tries so hard to be taken seriously but fails to meet standards, feeling more like bad fan fiction. It insults its viewers intelligence by breaking the number one rule of screenwriting: show, don't tell.Any criticism of this show can only be defended by, "Just don't think about it, it's fantasy!" as if it's an excuse for subpar television despite its monumental budget.Rings of Power is a lifeless husk with no memorable soundtrack or scenes and does very few things right. 3/10.

Here's the translation of your text into English:"Basically, episode 4 of season 2 of 'The Lord of the Rings'...Overall: A complete disaster of bad acting, a trivial plot with a seasoning of rotting stupid dialogues. I can't believe these were written by people who work in television or anything related to it. The level of dialogue is as if the director won an international directing festival for the mentally challenged, with clearly pronounced oligophrenia. And the judge who gave him the award is an imbecile. Even a 12-year-old child could write better. I literally can't sometimes listen to their dialogues.Visually... Well, it's okay. But listening to and taking this seriously is just impossible. It's like 'The Rings of Power' is a burger from Ozy that accidentally ended up in McDonald's, sitting among double cheeseburgers and Big Macs. Compared to this masterpiece, 'She-Hulk' is an absolutely serious, interesting, and cool series that, honestly, I don't even remember, but I know I'd watch it again, honestly.But as for 'The Rings,' God willing, I'll finish watching it. Speaking of God, it seems the Bible was wrong. There are actually five horsemen of the apocalypse, and the first is 'The Rings of Power.'"

"I would draw some of the great tales in fullness, and leave many only placed in the scheme, and sketched. The cycles should be linked to a majestic whole, and yet leave scope for other minds and hands, wielding paint and music and drama."
J. R. R. T.It is sad that the recent attempt to adapt the magnificent stories so many cherish so much fails to grasp the greatness, fails to use the source material available, whose richness is unsurpassed both in internal coherence and depth. Instead the authors try to reinvent the wheel, add asinine arcs, unneeded characters and, frankly, weird twist to the material.Had the attempt tried to cherish and elevate the stories of the second age to a visual form, much could have been forgiven.Instead we are given bland corporate run-of-the-mill corporate prefabricate with Middleearth water thinned paint over it. One coat, sadly. The bones shine through, and were the story stripped of this paint and repainted in, say, Baldurs Gate colors, it would be just as bland and untrue to the source material.Three stars is generous.

ipc-title__text: Tolkien is turning in his grave

ipc-html-content-inner-div:
I am a huge fan of The Lord of the Rings but I did not want to watch this show and had little interest. But with Season 2 just starting its release schedule, I thought it was time for me to watch this show and I have now watched the first season of Rings of Power and here is my review for it. The premise of the show is set thousands of years before Lord of the Rings and sees the different species try to survive against the dark forces of Middle Earth.Main Character
Morfydd Clark plays a young Galadriel and I did find it unfortunate that I really didn't care about this character. She is just really dull and the show doesn't do a good enough job of making you care about her or her character. Clark, does try and that deserves a bit of credit but with her being the clear protagonist of this show, she falls really flat.Supporting Cast
The cast is pretty large, and it is mixed for sure. I think a lot of the performers were hampered by shoddy writing and poor storytelling which gave them little to work with.Robert Aramayo plays young Elrond and I really liked him. He doesn't really feel like Elrond but I can't deny that he is entertaining to watch and there is plenty of depth made to his character and I found the scenes involving him and Durin played by Owain Arthur to be the most entertaining of the show.Charlie Vickers plays Halbrand and he is alright, he actually has some charm and charisma to him which helps him rise above some shoddy writing for the character. I thought he did a good job and made me intrigued by his character.But the rest of the cast really suffers, Arondir played by Ismael Cruz Cordova is really boring. He is great in the action sequences, but he is so monotone and soft spoken that it was hard to care about him and he just falls really flat, especially with how much time we spend with him.The story involving Daniel Weyman as The Stranger and Markella Kavenagh as Nori is really dull and boring. It tries to be mysterious but it never really goes anywhere, it took till the finale to try and make them interesting but there characters were a sore part of the show.Story
The story really misses the mark. I saw it described as a fan fiction of JRR Tolkein's work and I am afraid that it does really feel like that. The show tries to force intrigue and interest by hiding a lot of information about the characters but that made it really hard to get invested. Then the final episode has a few reveals that feel rushed and not earned for the show and I hope the story improves in the future.Script
The show is unfortunately not written well. All the dialogue feels really forced and those bits that are good are due to the actors rising above this shoddy writing. Not much makes sense and making so many storylines that involve mystery makes things feeling frustratingly not complete.Style
Easily the best part of the show is the style. The show looks beautiful, you can tell it has a huge budget and for the most part it is really effective. Middle Earth looks great and I am glad that this show has the essence of the universe with both its looks and also its fantastic music choices. The action scenes are also great and have a bit more brutality which I definitely enjoyed.Overall
Overall, Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power Season 1 is a bad show and falls really flat of its licence. It is definitely an example of style of substance and I hope the second season is a huge improvement on this as the franchise deserves way better.Rating - 3/10.

I don't recommend this show at all. It's very boring, the characters are awful, nothing happens, none of the jokes land, there's no drama or conflict, and the dialogue can be seriously cringe. None of the magic from Peter Jackson's original trilogy is present, nor even the Hobbit trilogy. What baffles me is how this is supposed to be the most expensive TV series ever made. Where is the budget going to? Majority of the scenes are just people talking about completely irrelevant topics. There were several scenes where you think something is about to happen and then it immediately cuts back to something pointless and unnecessary. Shame on you Amazon for insulting Tolkien's work.

I wouldn't be surprised if the Rings of Power was written by an AI program. It's like those prompts where they say "We made an AI program read every Batman comic and then made it write a screenplay."It's characters and places you (might) know but with a completely random plot.But if it was written by a person, then they got very lazy. Any form of research could've still made a coherent plot that follows the text. It's obvious that any amount of liberties had to be taken, because only the rights to the Appendices were obtained, but this wasn't even close.My 2 star rating is because it did look pretty, which is obviously where the money went.

People are just saying its bad and Things like "its not Tolkien worthy", because they think they have to say it, because they're such big fans of Tolkien or something, I Don't know.Those people have shot their mouth and just watch it.I mean, yeah, Peter Jacksons Lord of the Rings is waaaayyy better, but so what?It doesn't need to be better. Just watch it and go back to Middle-Earth and just enjoy it.The first two episodes are a little slow, but after that it is a really cool show.Believe me, i'm also a huge Tolkien fan and I loved it and can't wait till season 2.Just watch it and make your own opinion.

What else can you expect from Amazon thinking it can really do justice to a work such as Tolkien's by simply throwing money at it? I really wanted to like this series but I just couldn't; that "suspension of disbelief" never happened. Full disclosure, I have read the Silmarillion, Unfinished Tales, etc. So yes, I know the lore and no--absolutely no--this series does not follow the stories Tolkien wrote (the writers borrowed actual character names and then threw the rest of the source material in the bin) but pretending that I went into this series without all of that background, I still found the series difficult to enjoy.First, too many concurrent storylines. Each episode jumps among up to four different plots and since each episode is only about an hour, this makes it difficult to "get into" something after only about 10-15 minutes.Second, the storylines themselves fall flat. So much is being crammed into these almost bite-sized chunks of aforementioned storylines to move things forward but why? Why not take things more slowly and focus on letting the audience get to know the characters before rushing to the next thing? Which leads to my third complaint:
Third, the characters are either flat, unbelievable, or unlikable, with a few exceptions. Durin and Elendil are the best cast and acted characters in my opinion. Galadriel... Why was she written and acted to be so pugnacious and unlikable? She's still thousands of years old in the second age so the reason of "this is in her younger years" is absolutely trash. But that's getting into lore so moving on. The elves themselves were very disappointing both in their appearance and acting. Different skin tones for elves? Yes, bring it on. But short hair? No, come on. Did the costume department not get enough $ for good wigs? That's what it feels like, and also not enough money for more convincing armor for the Númenoreans.Bottom line: Not the worst show to ever be made but it's also pretty boring in a lot areas. I didn't care about any of the characters, never teared up with them, didn't have any anxiety when danger was imminent. As the experience was all just "meh", again, it's pretty disappointing when you think of what could have been done with a billion dollars.

ipc-title__text: Could have been good, but really isn't.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Where to start with this one? I have to admit that I'm not a LOTR fan, but am aware of its history and lore. Even with my fairly limited knowledge of the source material its pretty clear that this is just some pretty generic fantasy show with LOTR branding overlaid on it.The acting is ok and you have to feel a bit sorry for them given the material they have to work with. The only two characters that seem to have had any effort put into theirs plots are Elrond and Durin. Easily the best part of the show. Everyone else I really didn't care about. I actively hated every Harfoot scene and character. The show would be better for not including them.The script/plot/dialogue are awful. Really bad. It tried to be clever with the whole Halbrand is not Sauron and the giant is not Gandalf plots. However, it was so blatent it was quite irritating to watch week after week. I found it frustrating when characters who we know are alive during the main trilogy are put in 'danger' . Why? We know they are going to be fine, so why bother doing it?The less said about Galadriel the better. What an completely unlikeable character who always seems to do the most annoying and stupid things consistently.It was interesting to watch the first series, but based on the above I won't be returning. Spend less money on the CGI and more on getting a script that makes sense and isn't annoying.

ipc-title__text: Visually outstanding, but melodramatic script lacks subtlety
ipc-html-content-inner-div: As I watched the first season of LOTR: TROP I was amazed at the scope and beauty of the production. Incredible environments, vast landscapes and sweeping shots. Meticulously made sets, designs, props and costumes, and fantastic top-of-the-line special effects, CGI and animations. A real treat for the eyes.The script on the other hand, is problematic. While the overarching main plot is reasonably good, the problem lies with the tempo and gravitas of the scenes that build the individual scenes. Specifically, every scene, and almost every single line ever spoken has the weight of life-and-death, good versus evil, fate of middle earth and all races in it.And I do mean every scene.A character cannot say hello without a dramatic pause, followed by a line such as: "in our language, we don't say hello. We say fluggely-mugguly, which means 'may the light of dawn show you the way of righteousness' " followed by meaningful looks, cinematic music and a sweeping shot.Now repeat that same vibe a thousand times.Every. Scene.It gets tedious real fast.I understand that LOTR is about epic struggles in it's core, but this heavy-handed treatment of these issues make it melodramatic and distance the viewer, rather than draw him in with the intricacies and nuances of small intimate moments- as they project into life's greatest questions.Is it worth watching then?It is, but as they say: "A bird will fly to the sun as the leaf falls to the earth. Just as good will triumph over evil, so will our toils forever stain the ground with the sweat of our forefathers" (meaningful look, sweeping shot, climactic cinematic music)

ipc-title__text: Tolkien is the only reason anyone is watching.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I will be watching future seasons and I really believe that the show has potential because it's Tolkien and this should really write itself with the source material.Firstly the positives, the music is fantastic, It's beautifully shot, the sets look amazing.It looks the way a show like this should look.That being said there is just so many moments in this show that take you out of the world and make you feel like it's badly written fan-fiction, so many continuity errors, people appearing in two places at once, not walking out of open doors just to build tension, so many characters either who do completely irrational things or react in ways that just don't make sense because the writers want a pay-off that has not been earned.All I ask for season 2 is that people earn their pay-offs and that characters are strong because they are strong and not because all other characters are useless.Legolas was strong because he was strong and we saw it not because every other elf was useless and he kept having to save everyone, Merry and Pippin put up more of a fight than some of Arondir's comrades.Imagine if when Gandalf was holding the eye of Sauron and Pippin took it during the night that after that Pippin and the other hobbits became afraid of Gandalf and he had to prove himself, it just makes no sense, when characters act irrationally just for the sake of a writers pay-off they have in mind it really makes you realise you are watching a tv show."I am good" indeed, yes we know, thanks for telling us.

ipc-title__text: Starts like.. "this could get better' finishes with 'this cant get any worse'
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Too much wrong with this to put here. Teleport.. no back story... random enemies showing up with no explanation... no character development.... whole plots which were boring... bad re-enactments from original trilogy.. more teleporting... one or two likeable characters (non of the main cast)... unrealistic fight scenes... the feeling of NO EPICNESS... no goosebumps... how easy it is to skip the boring plots... no realism (fighting... people... number of people..... no anticipation... no big scale... big number of stupid characters doing stupid things... no big deaths... (I feel bad writing this for the people who worked on this)The best episodes were near the beginning. Felt like the whole thing was directed at small children.On the other side it was obvious lots had been spent on outfits / scenery and cgi. Or it would be sub 4.

ipc-title__text: Great visuals, mediocre storytelling, uninteresting in general
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I cut off any naysayers before watching the show, I like the Tolkien world but I'm open to adaptations and improvisations within it. Actually we paid for prime just for this show (thank god there are so many better shows in there to justify our money).Also during the season I tried my best to keep anything that felt wrong or was bad from stopping me watching the whole season, I wanted so badly to like the show, I wanted so badly to CARE about someone or something within it, but in the end it failed me so bad.I loved the visuals of the show, the story and acting was meh, there where scenes that I was like "did this slipped from the final edit", like for example this slow motion horse riding scene with Galandriel, that felt like some tiktok video joke or something and it was the first punch in my face about where this show is heading.But the worst part is nothing of all the above, I could have gave at least a 5 and short of ignore ALL the issues and wrongs with this show if it could do one simple thing.That is to make me care even a little bit about any of the characters, or even about what happens at all. It failed to make me care to come back and watch the next episode, I dragged myself back again and again, I even forgot an episode was out at some point, I wanted so bad to finally watch the episode that fix it all, that make it all justice and make my time not being spent in vein but alas... that episode never came.Sorry Amazon, but it seems like you spent all the budget in the visuals and not in writing something interesting.

ipc-title__text: Promised much but did not deliver - terrible storytelling and unlikable characters!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: After the excellent dramatisations of 'Reacher' and 'The Terminal List' I had high hopes for the Rings of Power, but to be honest this series was a story telling disaster and that is a terrible start when you have the literary genius of JRR Tolkien to work from.I have read Professor Tolkien's works from a young age and I still find new things in his legendarium as I near the end of my fifties. However, it was difficult to liken this earlier age world to what was to come. Journey jumps faster than a Star Trek Transporter and disjointed moves from one story line to another, just did not work. There were some nice visuals and an OK score, but that was not enough for me to get enthused and eagerly await the next instalment. Even the costumes were very variable in their practically and quality, why did Elendil have two slices of melon on his helmet?I tried to look at this as a general fantasy fan, but it just does not work as a good ... 'Sit down after a hard day and lose myself' watch, alas it is just very average and did not excite me at all. The biggest problem for me was the dumbing down of the elves, they were not made to look or act like ethereal beings and pretty much came across as folks who's IQs had been turned down by 1000, they didn't represent anything Tolkien that was for sure. The Hobbits, yes Harfoots are Hobbits, were completely out of character, seemingly leaving compatriots behind for anything worse than a sprained ankle, and I don't recollect any of the three hobbit tribes being portrayed as dirty urchins, with so little compassion for their peers.Apart from the dwarves, who when they got screen time were enjoyable to watch, the races of men and elves were pretty ridiculous with their actions, the male characters who will endure, were all made out to be stupid and incompetent in their decision making, so I guess they will need to be schooled, please give us some credit.I found myself getting behind Adar and his Orcs, but when it came to battle they then became incompetent and were easily defeated alas. I don't like to criticise, but if you are going to invest so much in a series, surely you recruit the best of the best. The story being told did not come across as intelligent or believable, sensible links were not made and instead the audience is told everything, sometimes even twice or more.I am hoping that when I reach old age I will have as good hearing as the Balrog, that can literally hear a leaf drop.

ipc-title__text: I couldn't watch this beyond Episode one
ipc-html-content-inner-div: But kept an eye out in case things changed by occasionally watching reviews. It just didn't happen for me. After Jackson's treatment, going back to a grander time demanded a grander showing.This is NOT it.If this had been its own thing, I might have been more forgiving, but it's not. And it doesn't cut it. It's a shame because every time one of these shows like RoP, WoT, etc, fail, it makes it that much harder for the next to float.You just really need people honestly dedicated to the source, otherwise it's a bait & switch waste of time for everyone.But I'm happy for anyone that's into it. Just isn't me.Final Rating: 5. As six is generally watchable, it's a "kind" five since I realize my bias based on knowledge of the material. For others familiar with the material, I'd argue a four or perhaps even a three. A seven or higher rating (somehow some are giving it) starts getting into striking a cord, which I'm be surprised anyone could honestly claim.

ipc-title__text: Not so bad but so far from a masterpice
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Not so bad but so far from a masterpice. After a bad and chaotic start (1/2/3 episodes, the third really terrible episode) the series starts to take off with great graphics, keeping a good pace. It is not faithful to what emerges in the Sigmarillion but that is not the problem, it is not a novel. The biggest problems are: 1) Far from the atmospheres of LOTR and Lo HOBBIT 2) Trivial dialogues 3) Direction often naive, trashy, not very original and capable, slow, regardless of fidelity to the work 4) Actors often unconvincing and not very complex and in-depth plot. Overall an enjoyable and entertaining series, without however giving great emotions or giving the viewer much more than some beautiful images.

ipc-title__text: I just don't care.l about them.

I feel sorry for the cast, as script wise they have nothing to work with.Plot is everything, and everything this does not have. I don't care about the characters. I want the orcs to just kill them all and the show get cancelled.It is so boring. Please help me. I have two episodes to go and it keeps getting worse. ipc-title__text: Thank you Amazon for having the courage!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I feel like it's not being judged quite honestly by many lord of the rings fans, many of whom have already slammed it beforehand. It is in fact much better than it is made out to be. Sure you have to get used to it because you compare it to the movie, but after a few episodes you get more and more into it and you learn to appreciate it. I am grateful to Amazon for having the courage to do it, because you know in advance that there will be a lot of criticism because many fans will compare it to one of the best films ever. Love the scenery, the music and after a while also the characters. Great series and I can't wait for season 2.

ipc-title__text: Better Knowledge of the Tolkien world would be nice
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The Cinematography and much of the costumes were of excellent standard. Which makes the writing that much more atrocious.There are significant details they overlook or ignore the inconvenience of continuity even to the PJ movies. I would go into the details of those breaches but that would spoil the series for whoever is watching.I do understand why now that Amazon was not able to get any licensing from The Tolkien Estate. What they did with what they had was .. well it breaks the book canon.The actors did very well and in the scenes were quite convincing but to someone who has read the collected works ... it falls short and changes some core fundamentals.

ipc-title__text: All that Glitters is Not Gold, but it Still could Be worth Mining
ipc-html-content-inner-div: In the video game , Lord of the Rings- War in the North , one of the characters states "All that glitters is not gold." That quote seems very fitting for the early episodes of this series. Despite breathtaking shots and sets the story is empty and even quite boring for long periods of time. Both Galadriel and Elrond as characters were slow to impress me and the Harfoot scenes just did not have the same feel as a Lord of the Rings series and felt like some other fantasy tale. Early during the release of the series I found it to be well below average and a waste of a high budget. In other words it was another fantasy tale relying on its visual appeal and brand to keep viewers. Admittedly, if it were not for the Lord of the Rings brand I likely would not have continued with the series.However around the midpoint some new interesting developments began to happen. The dwarves were really well done and Elrond and Durin show some depth. Still, the show was not exceptional but enough to keep watching.Eventually when arriving at the Udun episode everything accelerates. This episode was fantastic , it once again had that Lord of the Rings feel I was craving. The battles were exciting and the orcs so well done. Characters began to show some evolution from their initially raw undeveloped selves. Most importantly of all, it became entertaining.There was some filler leading up to the finale with characters delivering speeches of how wise and knowing they are by almost speaking in riddles, but this is right up the alley of Lord of the Rings so it would be unfair to criticize it here and not in Peter Jackson's trilogy.Finally the finale ties much of it together, or in the very least begins to set the stage for where the series will go with the next season. Even the Harfoot sequences I dreaded early in the series had a warm comforting conclusion to it.In taking everything into consideration I'm modestly satisfied with how this played out. I understand the strong disappointment from those heavily invested in the lore and official Tolkien cannon, but for a re-creation of Tolkiens work in the modern day it might be as good as can be hoped for. The content of the series itself managed to avoid politics so that all were welcome to enjoy. While the series might glitter but not be gold, in my view it is at least bronze and still warrants prospecting.

ipc-title__text: Made for profit not for love
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Amazon have put this together out of respect for algorithms and statistics, not story. It wouldn't surprise me if Jeff Bezos has intentionally pushed the use of AI to write the story. It simply has a cold, robotic feel to it and is frequently clumsy, as if written by a computer.To avoid spoliers, I'll not go into any details. Having now seen the whole first series, I'll just summarise the experience.Primarily it's very boring. The first and final episodes contain the majority of anything remotely interesting and the rest is spread out so thinly that you could literally just jump from the first to last episode and it would probably be a lot better.The plot is riddled with stupidity and implausibility and hangs off a myriad of "mystery boxes" which is its sole mechanism to keep the viewer watching. There's no intelligence to any of it. I would think the maximum age that would be dazzled by this kind of thing is probably about 10 years old but I'm being generous there.The visuals are poor too. Far too much reliance on CG which renders the experience very cartoon-like.As for the characters, there are none with whom it's possible to emapathise with. No decent arcs or development and as a result you just don't care about any of them.I think most have stuck with it out of morbid curiosity as to how far it can possibly fall below the original movies from Peter Jackson.

Give it a chance it's good to see a new take on this fable. There's always fanboys whinging about anything they can. The ring of power is thoroughly enjoyable and is beautifully presented. You can tell the money was well used it's nice to see a big budget for each episode. Yes there are some issues but on the whole it's pretty epic. It's full of all the lore you love and yes there is poetic licence with some bits. But wouldn't life be boring if there was no change. Well done Amazon looking forward to more seasons. Remember it's all a made up story and reinvention can be good like this epic show ..

It is frustrating to see so much potential wasted. There is no need to write the characters in a way where the fans hate them.Please reconsider how you write season two and please get better writers. This could be amazing, but the execution of season 1 is terrible.I was cautiously optimistic after episode one and two, but the characters decision-making started to go downhill fast. You can't have your main character make questionable decisions at every turn that are completely illogical. It felt like they went for the most general audience possible and completely ignored any and all lore. Please consider how you handle the lore and don't write characters we hate!

ipc-title__text: Tolkien Created A Living World. Living Things Evolve & Become Greater Still
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I have been thoroughly impressed by this new series. Occasionally, I find myself muttering that they have changed something from the original stories. And yet... I allow this adaptation to sweep me along in a new imagining of the war between beauty and darkness. The few cosmetic alterations and/or the few necessary changes to tell such a gargantuan series of tales in a coherent manner (and in a short time) hardly dissuade me from watching. Nor, do I find myself stuck on purist details overmuch.Tolkien created a living, breathing world that was constantly evolving into more. The Rings of Power series continues that tradition in no less of a magnificent and exciting way. Middle-Earth continues to evolve in ways that will both surprise and delight. And it must. They are very possibly the greatest stories written in the last 100 years. In order for them to continue to be relevant in our modern world, those stories must evolve to include new elements and ideas. I am so pleased to be seeing this happen in this series!Tolkien blew the breath of life into Middle-Earth. In the minds of fans, it is a living world. Living worlds grow and change and then, they become even more than they were before. This series exemplifies the amazing vision that Tolkien gave to the world. I can not wait to see more!My only REAL complaint is that the season was far too short. I think it should have been 12 episodes at a bare minimum.Until then, I will be waiting "patiently" (NOT) to see what happens next season. Hope you will too!

It looks pretty, that's about it.The characters are two dimensional, the dialogue is some of the worst television since 90s fox and the story is bland.You think they would've paid the writers a little more with all the big bucks they threw into this mess.Besides turning lore on it's head, which isn't the biggest issue, the character barely incorporate the spirit of those we've not only read about, but actually seen on the silver screen.Why make a twilight saga romance of Sauron's coming to power? With a character who has a husband that was written out of the the show to be "missing" with no further explanation.Waking ancient evils with mundane plot points and making the turning point of a character literally saying "I am good!".It's as if it were written and edited by 5th graders.

Ok, first off: I'm not a huge LOTR Fan. I loved the movies, but I never read the books, but I didn't like the Hobbit movies. The Hobbit movies were boring, honestly. Not one character was interesting to me.The Rings of Power on the other hand has many characters that are intriguing. Even the plot was a bit slow at times, I really liked the characters.I also loved Galadriel. In the movies she has an evil side to her. And in the series she's still young, not wise, but flawed. Really interesting to think she would one day become this unearthly being.I loved that Sauron played them all. He is a lot more handsome than I'd imagined, but he's deceiving as ever.I love this series and can't wait for the next season.

Galadriel is single handedly ruining the show. Terrible acting. Whoever thought a strong female character means to be stiff all the time and absolutely no body language and expressionless face, blank stare, and not to mention no trace of grace that comes from years of wisdom. It's a shame and a surprise that a show where millions are spent to produce could miss an obvious thing such as this. This show is nothing compared to the house of dragon or the last kingdom. There are some good characters like Nori and the elf that loves the south lander woman. They should seriously consider reducing the screen time for Galadriel and focus on the good characters. The plot moves very slowly overall.

I was really hyped for this show, Peter Jackson's trilogy are my favorite movies of all time and seeing that i would got more hours in this universe blinded me at first, and after watching 6 episodes i feel kinda disapointed with what we got for now. The cinematography and cgi iare probably the best and only things on the show that are actually amazing, especially the dwarves reign that is shockingly beautiful, but my major problem and what kills this show for me are it's plot and characters. Apart from the dwarves, none of the races show anything intresting about them: the Elves are pretty boring, the harfoots plot feels like don't belong on the show and the humans are all hateable. None of the major characters are compelling characters, especially Isildur who feels like a Netflix bad animated comedy character. As a show Rings of Power is fine, but it's WAY worse than i expected. Probably being my biggest dissapointment with tv series for the last 2 years.

Five episodes in, I'm done: it's slow, boring, has no discernible hook lines, the characters are almost entirely unlikeable, unrelatable, annoying or dull. The acting is mediocre at best, but the main culprits have to be the writers (together with all those executives, producers and directors who failed to pick up on the obvious flaws).Possibly, you could argue they were tied down by the source material (or lack of it), perhaps they thought it was okay to spend the first season on exposition, lore and back-story and thought viewers would be patient enough to follow along?Galadriel is thousands of years old, but somehow in all that time has failed to gain any charm, diplomacy, wisdom or a sense of humour. She, like too many of the characters, acts like a petulant teenager (or more likely - an activist) - scowling at everything and anyone who doesn't bow to her immediate demands.Maybe it's an elf problem as Arondir claims to have taken two centuries to gain courage but appears to need a few more to gain a personality. He too, scowls and stares into the distance - obviously troubled by something (probably the script, or the possibility of his 'acting' career tanking).There's a tiny bit of much needed light relief from the dwarves, but finding anything enjoyable or exciting in this mess is as taxing as finding the elusive mithril.Too many scenes simply repeat the same thing, fail to push the story forward, fail to tell us anything interesting about the characters and fail to set-up any hook to want to watch further. (Yes, I know I'm repeating myself - but I need to outlet my frustration somewhere :).)In the era of streaming 'content' - lazy writers seem to take a viewer's time and commitment for granted - traditionally, storytellers have had to earn these things.We're forced, for example, to follow the Harfoots as they meander across the continent facing the occasional CGI threat and (please, no) singing their songs, but why are we supposed to care for these characters? They, (mild spoiler alert) leave behind anyone who's too slow or too weak and I can sympathise - that's how I ended up feeling about this series, regardless of how pretty the scenery might be.I started empathising with the orcs and hoping some great battle would wipe out these 'heroes' as soon as possible.

Gritty like the Jackson films, looks more practical and real, instead of that washed out Hobbit aesthetic.Score is beautiful, and composed by Howard Shore again.Looks stunning, everything is 'middle-earthen' and feels it.Story is a bit bland. But it's exciting to see the characters and locations you hear about briefly, like Numeanor and Elendil. You can tell a lot of care was putting into making it feel like a lord of the rings tale, but the story falls short.Let's be honest, the bar is set very high and haters will continue to hate, and exaggerate its failures, which to be honest aren't that bad.Do wish it was more about Morgoth, and not about Sauron, again. Anyone who's read the appendices and Silmarillion, knows there's very little actual story-telling for Sauron's early days and the fall of Numenor, so the creative license here is reasonable for the writers.Events are messaged like a bible passage or verse, not in-depth like the original 5 volumes and the Hobbit.

ipc-title__text: From a die hard fan of Peter Jackson's LOTR: this is a truly enjoyable, decent show
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Don't believe the hate hype. It's not a bad show at all. Feels very much like a modern fantasy book. Very solid, and I've enjoyed every episode so far. The production is top notch and the characters are surprisingly compelling. My wife and I have been waiting every week for the next episode to drop.Nothing will ever quite compare to Peter Jackson's Trilogy, but this is an excellent exploration of some of Tolkien's work. It's full to the brim with characters, events, and places that many Tolkien fans have always wanted to see more of on screen. It's far from perfect, but it is a genuine, heartfelt attempt at bringing more of Tolkien's to life.

ipc-title__text: Impossible task to start and they aren't doing themselves any favors
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Peter Jackson already made two near perfect trilogies, so it was already a incredibly high bar. If those would have never been made this series would still be mediocre at best, having seen the films it makes this almost hard to watch. It's impossible to watch without comparing the series in your mind, which makes this come off as a dumbed down music video version. The writing simply isn't good, and the action sequences are just bad. The visuals are above average, but a far cry from the films. All in all it's a time waster if you literally have nothing else you want to see, even then I just turned on the two towers again.

After all the hype, this show was a great disappointment. The writing is atrocious, the dialog is cringe, the characters are two dimensional and forgettable, the storyline breaks LOTR lore, the acting is subpar, some of the costumes look really cheap.I found myself getting bored at the slow pace and it's not improving as we get into later episodes.This is written by people who don't seem to care about tolkein's work, and don't honor the world he created.Instead, they are focused on projecting their own world views to make it look more like our world. Mission successful, the show does look more like our world. Unfortunately, it doesn't look anything like tolkein's world. If you take all the characters and story and plop it down in an AD&D world, you wouldn't be able to tell the difference.Anything good? The visuals are nice. It's easy to see where all the money went. But the visuals aren't enough to carry the show.

If Amazon wants this show to succeed they must fire 90-95% of the crew for season 2, doo a big time jump and start over... in the whole show there is only 2 likable characters.. The dialog is worst then low budget 90s show, the main character is annoying unlikable with zero charisma. The script feels like pitch ideas frankensteinned together and in the end we got this abomination. Its not okay when you sympathize with the orcs more then the main focused character. The númenóreans are reduced to nothing. This mystical land is turned into Rome rip off with bad costume design, you cant even tell from the extras who is lowborn and who is noble.. I still have hope for good Lord of the rings show just doo full rework and recast.

The writing in this show is atrocious. No character that is of importance is interesting or makes you want to root for them. Every scene contradicts either the book or a prior scene in the show itself, just showcasing the lack of care the writers and actors put into learning about middle earth and wanting to create something the fans can get behind and watch.From the outside looking in, this show was nothing but a money grab. Amazon wanted the next game of thrones which is nonsense considering we are talking about Lord of the Rings, arguably the greatest story in the fantasy genre. There has to be more that we do not know because I truly do not understand how they ruined something so great and sophisticated and just dumbed it down to be a shell of itself with no story/character progression.Besides the orcs and dwarves, the show runners cared nothing about details of the other characters. Elves look terrible and nothing like what they should - they don't even have distinctions between humans unlike every other movie based on LotR lore. People of numenor are great warriors and historically tall - could've fooled me watching this show as the show made these characters act as if they were lowly peasants.I can only describe this show to others when they ask about it as just a shame. It's a shame they didn't even try to make this show good, hopefully they cancel it after season 1 and start anew or just sell the rights to hbo who would actually care to make a product that fans would watch.

As a fan of the incredible books I was worried this series would loose some of the beauty and essence. I am relived and glad that it has not and has been done with thought and is a tribute to this uniquely magical world. The choices of music, characters, costume and even the flow of the story is reminiscent of the books and the original movies. I have seen too many series fall prey to the action packed punch line, overdone style of series making. I truly believe, from what I have seen so far this will not fall be another victim. I have been waiting for this series for a long time and it has most definitely delivered. Thank you.

Not having read the books I came to this with an open mind and 4 episodes in I'm really enjoying it. I agree with other reviews that the storyline is a tad slow, but it's good to invest the time in getting to know the characters/backstory. For me the most impressive thing about The Rings of Power is the sumptuous and super detailed visuals which are simply stunning. I am fortunate that I have a very large projection screen and a high end sound system, so I can fully immerse myself in the amazing visuals and captivating soundtrack. Every episode is like a mini feature film with outstanding cinematography and I'm really looking forward to seeing where this adventure goes.

ipc-title__text: It as NOT worth the wait
ipc-html-content-inner-div:
Having read The Lord of the Rings, The Silmarillion, and other of Tolkein's works, I eagerly awaited the origin stories of Middle-earth put to screen. Of course, I have high expectations after The Lord of the Rings films.After 4 episodes, I can say this is joke storytelling -portraying deaths of characters introduced 2 minutes earlier as tragedy, and leaving nothing to mystery.The best story arc might be the Stranger, only since I like the idea of seeing Mithrandir befriend the Hobbits. Daniel Heyman does a pretty good Jackie Earle Haley.Watch House of the Dragons, it's better. It has humans you can relate to. This isn't fantasy, it's a farce.Characters: 2
Story: 2
DECOR and VENUE AND MUSIC and costume: who cares.

Having suffered through the first half of the season, I can say that this show is the most overhyped, dry, boring and annoying shows I've ever watched.4 episodes of painful, drawn-out character development that is utterly pointless. Galadriel, Elrond, Elendil, Isildur don't need this much time fleshing out their story. Yet for some reason Amazon decided we need 4 episodes of meaningless dialog. Time compression, bad characterization of we'll established people in the universe, and blatant pandering have ruined this for me.If I'm like most people, I'd want some kind of backstory on the dwarves and kings that received their rings. Or maybe just a little more meaningful action. But no, we get hours and hours of of the most boring dialog. We get to find out about Mithril. We get to see an entire cgi city that has no bearing itself on the story.If meh was a show, this is it.

ipc-title__text: Everything About this show is great
ipc-html-content-inner-div: As a loyal fan of Tolkin books and LOTR and the Hobbit movies , I thank the creators of this great show for the utmost respect they show to this marvelous magical world and not neglecting any detail.From where I see it , The show creators spares no efforts or financial resources to convert the wonders of this amazing world in to some of the most mesmerizing and magical scenes I have ever seen on a TV show.And I hope they will be able to continue on the same level of excellence in the future challenges a head.As for the inexplicably bad reviews , I think they belongs to some childish post millennial kids who just need a silly mix of blood, sex, drugs and may be some dragons .For those bad reviwers I say, sorry folks ,this show is not for you.

ipc-title__text: Let go and just enjoyed it
ipc-html-content-inner-div: It's just a beautiful show. It's fun. The storytelling is excellent. The characters are believable. Why does everyone have to be so critical of everything? Why not just enjoy it for what it is? Who cares whether it's true to Tolkien? If you want Tolkien you know where to find it. The show is meant to be a newly imagined history based loosely on Tolkien's work. I enjoyed it. Let go of your snark and enjoy it, too.I look at this show as art as much as I see it as entertainment. Someone out a lot of thought into colors, contrast, ambience and atmosphere.I also like the characters. Galadriel is passionate and belligerently good. Elrond is noble. The orcs are terrible.

I hate this so much. Wjen I heard of this shows conception I had low expectations, but was still hopeful. Within the first ten minutes all hopes of being transported back to middle eart were dashed. It is a poor, soulless, lazy, unoriginal attempt at a show that's only selling point was that it was "inspired" by Tolkien. Riding on the coat tails ofThe Lord of the Rings, The Rings of power offers nothing in substance but rather seeks to justify every episode with the introduction of a different ancestor of the members from the fellowship. Galadriel is an insult and utterly exhausting to have on screen. Elrond is soulless, one dimensional and bland. Every costume in the show is cheap and out of place with random pops of vibrant color that don't belong in middle earth. The makeup feels just as foreign to something supposedly "inspired" by Tolkien. Eleanor Brandyfoot is cringy, with the most irritating storyline and even more grating accent. The fact that this show has so much funding and is planned to have 4 seasons is beyond me. This is show is the product of bad fan fiction that was taken seriously. Either follow the silmarillion properly or try an original story set after the destruction of the ring. But The Rings of Power is a mistake.

The story elements within The Rings of Power is keeping me very interested and involved in each passing episode. The excitement and suspense is what's driving this show. Character development is solid and the cast members perform believable, and engaging, roles. The fight scenes revealed so far are unexpectedly more disturbing than what was seen in director Peter Jackson's films. Parental guidance is recommended for sure. The visual scale of the show is very realistic and breath-taking. The Elven Kingdoms of Lindon and Eregion; the subterranean Dwarven realm of Khazad-dum; the Edain kingdom of Numenor; and the overall beautiful landscape scenery; all completely stunning, and marvelous, in their own ways. The stunning imagery will have you admiring what the show-runners have presented us. Bear McCreary's musical score is spot on and can become very moving in many scenes. I'm completely sold on this show. So far so good. And despite some deviations to Tolkien's lore, it seems the show-runners and writers are doing the best they can with what rights they have to Tolkien's Second Age source material. Much of the lore is still there, while even the creative liberties capture the spirit of Tolkien's writings. I'm looking forward to more episodes. From someone who has been a lifelong Tolkien fan, and approached this series with the highest level of caution, I was impressed! My expectations were exceeded.10/10 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Indecisive lackadaisical melodrama with fantastic motifs modeled after Tolkien's world mixed with modern identity politics mimicing P. Jacksons LOTR style.Amazon is playing with fire.Showrunners and directors of The Rings of Power might be falling into a trap of unoriginality. Here's why. Its simple and obvious. They are mimicing, simulating Peter Jackson's style, intentionally, hoping for the best, or at least I like to belive that, but it could be somthing else, more malevolent. So many points in the show indicate to this. And I think that's just wrong. Bad approach. Insted of finding their own way, they only amplify Peter Jacksons uniqueness and genius. And based on the assumption that most copyes are doomed, this could be highly counter-productive for Amazon.The biggest mistake, considering the first episode, is that everything is shown in such a way that the viewer's know, more or less, all part's of the story, so here we witness fast and constant jumps, which in my opinion is wrong.Points that indicate to mimicing are many considering episode 1 ,,A Shadow of the Past'' (and it took me so long to figure it. Sich fetails will be notoced only by those who watched LOTR trilogy contless times): Naration of Galadriel followed by the wars of the past, then appearance of Hobbits/Harfoots, represented by two main Harfoot girls, both great actress by the way (indicating to Frodo and Sam). Some situations, like chemistry between the Elf guard and a village woman (same as Aragorn and Arwen in LOTR), silly and pointless fireworks, snow troll fight lacrdia, Galadriel killing the troll without any trouble (Moria troll fight in LOTR). Even Arondir in episode 3, when he says that he will cut down the tree is indescribably reminiscent of the moment when Frodo says that he will take the ring to Mordor. Are they making a remake or making fun of Jackson, or they are trying to simulate something perfectly made before?Now back to the show. Watching the opening with the first episodes I felt some indifference, ambivalence towards the interpreted world. It turns out somehow as if I immediately thought something was wrong, and I must to figure it out, to reach an understanding.At first, wasn't expecting much to be honest, but at least I was hoping for a bit more interesting interpretation of the story. Instead of this I somehow felt monotony and disconnection from the Tolkien world. I wonder how tho? How can u make such an error? I thought that wasn't possible because Tolkien is an amazing and absolutely extraordinary story teller, with rich story and beautiful imagination, narratives and powerful dialogs.Well, behind this great visuals of the show, I felt there was something wrong with it, I just felt it, beside character development that is poorly executed, and the story that feels sluggish, uninteresting and distant. Then I remembered that I watched this before, somewhere else (Jackson's The Fellowship of the Ring) but far better made. This is just below standard, same but diferent, soulless and empty. And it didn't hook me up that time, knowing this, remembering. It took me a while to figure it out, it cost me a re-watch of episde 1 to understand why is this so familiar to me. And when it doesn't hook you up, u know it's just something wrong.Now plot felt soulless, almost empty. And the representation of Elf's is just bad, they are meant to be the fairest creatures in Arda, a far more beautiful race than Men, not casual humans with pointy ears.It's pretty bad start considering episode 1, poor opening, unoriginal, souless, indecisive, lackadaisical, melodramatic with scattered structure which makes it even harder for me to rate this higher than 3.However Episode 2 was already getting better. Is seemed like they were finding their way here. Orc scene was epic. Dwarfs are well made, Price Durin, played by great Owain Arthur, village woman Bronwyn by Nazanin Boniadi and Nori the Harfoot (Markella Kavenagh) carried the episode.I'm not disappointed, nor sad, I'm not even angry, I'm just ambivalent and a bit impatient to see how this will unfold. Because I honestly don't see a passage pointing out usually in conclusion the lessons to be drawn from the story, therfore I don't find myself satisfied with what they showed. All I see is Galadriel driven by just pure mindless rage towards the one-dimensional entity of evil Sauron, as presented here.However, acting is good, visuals are great, cinematography and camera work are marvelous, but they cannot make up for lack storytelling talent, combined with identity politics of a modern era that are implemented here, feels just highly unnecessary and nonsensical to me.

ipc-title__text: One of the best shows on tv in past 5 years, amazing story telling.

I can't imagine why other stupid people rate it low. It should win show of the year. The visual effects were incredible as well. The orcs are quite scary digging tunnels everywhere. ipc-title__text: Spend $500 million on visual effects and then get the intern to do the writing...
ipc-html-content-inner-div: It's a laughably bad act of vandalism and hijacking of a great story to convey 21st century American left-wing identity politics. It's a Hollywood activists' diatribe. Nothing makes sense. The dialog is objectively terrible - even good actors would struggle. The characters are unlikeable and/or unremarkable, especially the main character, Strong Woman. If your main character is broken, your story is broken. It's intensely boring. They could literally just string together random scenes. Canon is out of the window. The music doesn't complement the story, but distracts from it. What a disaster. It's disrespectful to Tolkien (he/him), and it's disrespectful to audiences. It truly is epic - an epic fail.

If go in to watch this as a prequel to Peter Jackson's LOTR, you will be disappointed. To be honest, even Peter Jackson could not recrate the magic in the Hobbit movies.The first two episodes are visually breathtaking - the high production value is evident. Story starts off slow but picks up pace towards the middle of the second episode. I haven't been able to find any fault with the casting decisions and the actors have so far been good - not excellent but good.Ignore the naysayers and give this watch. You won't be disappointed.Peter Jackson's LOTR can't be recreated and that's a fact. As soon as people realize and recognize that, the ratings for the show will jump a couple of points.

The Rings of Power was a visual feast for the eyes and fantasy mind as I took pauses to turn pages reading up on the lore, I had been hoping to see a more expanded portrayal of the future elven queen Galadriel, pleasantly surprised by the full dimensions of Morfydds Clark's young and restless Galadriel. Trading in her crown for a blade she sets out to avenge her brother following a personal calling, even louder than the elven one calling to the undying lands. Clark's portrayal is a subtle one with hidden wisdom building up within a stoic mask and there's a reckless side of her I loved. But with over fifty hours of story to unfold there is no telling how much of it will be covered in Rings of Power, there simply wont be time. I'm curious to see what the future holds and how much of the lore they will have time to capture, and in what ages it will stretch and take them.Galadriel was fully engaged in the continual warfare of the first age, and the ruse of Sauron in the 2nd age. In the 3rd age she fought off the attacks on Lorien then led her armies to Dol Guildor. I always sensed Tolkien had a weak spot for Galadriel as he lovingly wrote her in his lore, Galadriels mother-name was Nerwen ('man-maiden') & she grew to be tall beyond the measure even of the women of the Noldor; she was strong of body, mind, & will, a match for both the loremasters and the athletes of the Eldar in the days of their youth. -History of Galadriel & Celeborn. I'm hoping Rings of Power will cover as much as possible.

ipc-title__text: Don't listen to the review bombs
ipc-html-content-inner-div: People on here are complaining about "oh it doesn't feel like Tolkien." What they really mean when they say that is "it doesn't feel like Peter Jackson." The show is incredible! It introduces us to a whole new world of middle earth that we previously have never been able to see before. As a REAL Tolkien fan, I couldn't have asked for any better. Anyone who complains otherwise isn't a Tolkien fan, but a Peter Jackson fan, and can't accept someone new showing their creative vision for the lore.For anyone who really loves the stories and beauty behind Lotr or the hobbit, you will love this too. The shots are gorgeous, acting and cast is fantastic, and wonderful writing and score! Can't wait to see more of what's next!

ipc-title__text: Stunning ! Just what I've been craving
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Simply stunning. Fans of Lord of the Rings, Hobbit might be split on this as it wasn't technical written by Tolkien BUT he himself said he'd created this world that other artists can create into and that's exactly what they've done.It's got all the elements of LOTR lore, the elves, humans, dwarves, orcs, hobbits and so on. It has stunning cinematography, vistas and set pieces. The story, understandably, is tricky to get moving but I have no doubt that once it gathers pace it'll be an unstoppable masterpiece.I highly recommend Rings of Power. If you love Tolkien's universe you can't not love this. Shows like this will start to fill the thousands of years of Middle Earth history we 'know' exists and fill it with life and a rich tapestry of stories woven together in a way that just 'fits'.I simply cannot wait for this.

There have been many many attempts by this show to make a "wink wink, nudge nudge" reference to other works, but this one really irked me.I get the feeling that instead of making a show which could stand on its own the makers instead made a really thin sheet that can cover many seats at once.Like: It has references to Peter Jacksons movies( and so many god awful references at that), yet it is nowhere near comparable,
political drama compared to Game of Thrones, but the problem is that the source material was not written as a morally gray work, but very clearly black/white - good vs evil show. The reason that Game of Thrones works as political drama is that showrunners had George R. R. Martins books to adept, books he took 20 years to write and make the drama engaging and coherent. And the reason that this show does not is because the showrunners have no source material to draw upon and they are clearly incapable of making the story by themselves.I am more then disappointed, i feel like somebody took my favorite song, made a cheap remake video on TikTok which got trending and now all the kids are going crazy for the remake without even knowing the original.
